citacoes.trecho: Based on these findings, we design a novel approach COTTON which can leverage ℓLMs to automatically generate CoTs for code generation.
The generated CoT by COTTON serves as an additional piece of information that is added to the original prompt in code generation tasks.
To reduce the training cost, we adopt instruction-tuning and LoRA techniques [24] to fine-tune the model parameters.
For our CoT generation task, we design a template that incorporates task-specific instructions, which is illustrated as follows.

We adopt a zero-shot approach [18] and some few-shot approaches (such as Self-planning [13], SCoT [14], and the self-cot we propose), which provide ℓLMs with a set of examples to generate the corresponding CoT.
To investigate whether ℓLMs can independently generate high-quality CoTs for code generation, we conduct experiments based on few-shot prompt learning techniques as described in Section 3.1.
This agent employs a one-shot approach, providing an example to aid the agent in learning the desired output style and generating CoT based on user input.
Furthermore, we utilize Agent 2 (cf. Section 3.1) as the Teacher Model.

To assess the impact of generated CoTs on improving the code generation performance of LLMs (such as CodeGen, StarCoder, and CodeT5+ as discussed in Section 4.2), we initially compare different models in the Self-CoT scenario (i.e., the CoTs generated by the model itself using the few-shot method in RQ1).
We analyze the performance of ℓLMs when utilizing CoTs generated by CodeLlama, ChatGLM 130B, Gemini, and the Teacher model.
To evaluate the performance of ℓLMs with and without CoT in the zero-shot scenario, we conduct experiments on three code generation datasets.
When the code generated by the model without the guidance of the CoT fails to pass the corresponding test cases, the model is provided with the CoT guidance to generate code.
We can observe that, under the guidance of the CoT generated by the Self-CoT method, the performance improvement of all ℓLMs is very limited, and even the performance of some ℓLMs may decrease.

These LLMs pose challenges in terms of time, computational, and financial costs when applied to code generation, rendering them impractical for most individual users, or in resource-constrained scenarios, such as restricted access to LLM APIs or constrained GPU availability.

In addition, in terms of the Consistency metric, gpt-3.5-turbo and gpt-4 achieved the best results on the OpenEval and HumanEval datasets, respectively, yet the cost of calling gpt-4 is 20 times higher than that of gpt-3.5-turbo.
This approach ensures that the CoT is used when necessary to avoid unnecessary overhead.
These rules are designed to filter data that contains syntactically incorrect code and documents that are inconsistent with the code, in addition to avoiding data leakage problem.
For each problem, we designed additional test cases in a manual way that can effectively evaluate the quality of the generated code and minimize bias and leakage.
The HumanEval-plus dataset [4] aims to alleviate the test case coverage limitation in HumanEval, which may result in false positive rates.

However, after our manual analysis, we find that a significant portion of the code snippets in these datasets are not self-contained, requiring external modules or files for program comprehension [33], which poses challenges for CoT generation.
Specifically, in terms of the Consistency metric, without the Consistency Checker for filtering, COTTON shows a relative performance decrease of 5.23% on HumanEval-CoT and 4.69% on OpenEval-CoT.
The first internal threat is the possibility of implementation faults in COTTON.
To mitigate this threat, we conduct a careful code inspection of the implementation and utilize well-established third-party libraries (such as PyTorch and Transformers).
The main construct threat is related to the metrics used in our automated evaluation.
In comparison, the LLM ChatGLM 130B only achieves an improvement of 36.59%.
Moreover, the Self-CoT method proposed in our study can perform better than Self-Planning and SCoT on all datasets.
To facilitate the replication of COTTON, we make our source code, trained models, and datasets publicly available on GitHub.

tecnicas.observacao: Condição principal de avaliação dos seis modelos (Tabela 6) e condição sem mensagens de execução e com uma amostra nas análises das Figuras 3 e 4. Instrução direta para corrigir o código e explicar a modificação em menos de 20 palavras (instrucao); delimitadores e e proibição de texto adicional (restricoes); o código com bug é inserido no prompt como {BUG INSTANCE} (contexto). Sem base identificável, por isso mecanismos_acrescentados vazio. A Figura 2 (p. 3) mostra um «Input Prompt» com redação diferente (inclui a questão e pergunta «Can you fix it up?»), divergência registrada em heterogeneidade. A explicação é pedida junto com o código corrigido, não como raciocínio prévio; por isso não foi classificada como raciocinio.

tecnicas.observacao: Objeto de investigação declarado no resumo (achado 3), na introdução e na conclusão. Contrafactual: condição com e sem mensagens de execução para gpt-4-0613 e gpt-3.5-turbo-0613, por categoria de bug (syntax, reference, logic), Figura 4. O texto do prompt dessa condição não é impresso; os mecanismos herdados (instrucao, restricoes) supõem que ela parte do prompt zero-shot do Apêndice A, o que o estudo não declara explicitamente. O ingrediente acrescentado são mensagens do ambiente de execução do LeetCode (saída do programa, traceback); nos exemplos do Apêndice F as mensagens acompanham o código com bug, sem resposta anterior do modelo, e o estudo não descreve iteração. Por isso foi classificado como contexto (informação externa de execução fornecida no prompt) e não como feedback, que o dicionário reserva a ciclos com retorno; se houver ciclo com a resposta do modelo, a classificação seria feedback, mas o estudo não o informa.

riscos.descricao: Risco de vazamento de benchmarks de depuração para os dados de pré-treinamento dos LLMs; o estudo controla o risco filtrando instâncias por data de publicação posterior ao corte de conhecimento dos dois modelos fechados (ver mitigacoes). O estudo não afirma contaminação efetiva do DebugBench.

Mensagens de execução podem atrapalhar a correção de bugs lógicos: o estudo afirma que são de nível baixo demais e podem causar perturbações, e a Figura 4 mostra redução da Pass Rate em logic para os dois modelos.

Amostragem múltipla melhora a depuração ao custo de mais tokens de inferência; o custo da amostragem não é quantificado. O estudo também limita a amostragem a nove respostas por restrição de orçamento.

Falha de conformidade com o formato de saída exigido pelo prompt: alguns modelos, como Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct, falham em casos por não seguirem as instruções de formato, o que reduz a Pass Rate por motivo não ligado à correção.

mitigacoes.descricao: Filtro de data: só trechos de código publicados a partir de julho de 2022, apresentado como corte de conhecimento oficial dos dois modelos fechados, para reduzir vazamento de dados.
Filtro automático que exclui código com bug contendo comentários que poderiam revelar o bug, e exigência de que o código com bug falhe em casos de teste.
Inspeção manual por três programadores de 180 casos segundo validade do bug, segurança de informação sensível e alinhamento ao cenário (Tabela 3).

A análise de realismo usa GPT-4 e Claude 3 Sonnet como juízes com temperatura 0.01 e top_p 0.7; esses parâmetros referem-se apenas aos juízes. Os parâmetros de decodificação e o número de execuções da avaliação de depuração não são informados.

citacoes.trecho: We evaluate two commercial and four open-source models in a zero-shot scenario.
As an extension, we also compare LLM debugging and code generation, revealing a strong correlation between them for closed-source models.

We find that (1) while closed-source models exhibit inferior debugging performance compared to humans, open-source models relatively lower pass rate scores; (2) the complexity of debugging notably fluctuates depending on the bug category; (3) incorporating runtime feedback has a clear impact on debugging performance which is not always helpful.

citacoes.trecho: In this section, we investigate the influence of runtime messages on the debugging process.
We leveraged the built-in runtime environment of the LeetCode test suites to obtain feedback information.
However, for logic bugs, the details provided in traceback messages are often too low-level to facilitate effective debugging and may even cause disruptions.
In this scenario, a language model is permitted to generate multiple responses to a single debugging query.
An instance is marked as ‘pass’ if at least one response successfully meets all test case criteria.
As illustrated in Figure 3, increased sampling attempts enhance debugging performance, indicating an effective trade-off: better debugging at the cost of using more inference tokens.
Due to budget constraints, we limit our sampling to a maximum of nine answers for each instance with logical errors.
While it’s challenging to ascertain the exposure due to a lack of training details, there’s a significant risk of data leakage.
The release date of code snippets must be no earlier than July 2022, the official knowledge cutoff date of two closed-source models (OpenAI, 2023) in case of data leakage.
The buggy code should not include in-line comments that could leak information about the bug.
It is also worth noticing that some models like Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct fail certain cases because they cannot comply with the instructions regarding the format.
We analyze the debugging and code generation performance of gpt-4-0613 (OpenAI, 2022) and gpt-3.5-turbo-0613 (OpenAI, 2023) on identical instances.
We hire three programmers with over four years of experience in programming to conduct the manual inspection on 180 cases over two hours each after training on 30 cases.

Em APPS, um gerador de tags baseado em prompts e exemplos 3-shot antecede o pacote. Base de comparação dos mecanismos acrescentados: geração direta pelo ChatGPT com 1-shot (instrucao, exemplos). Em relação ao comparador Plan, de que a técnica deriva no estágio passo a passo, o acréscimo é só contexto (ver o componente Knowledge Description). O contrafactual é o pacote contra a geração direta (Tabelas 3, 4 e 8), na mesma configuração padrão (1-shot, Temperature=1, Top_P=1); o ganho não se atribui a um único mecanismo. citacoes.trecho: Prompt Engineering Stage: In this stage, the LLMs learn the one-shot example prompt that we furnish and subsequently generate knowledge-aware prompt pertinent to the problem based on the algorithms and data structures information in the Knowledge Library.
Coding Stage: In this stage, we guide the LLMs to incorporate the problem and the prompt generated in the preceding step.

In Prompt Engineering Stage, we designate ChatGPT as a prompt engineer, accountable for comprehending the problem and learning as well as reviewing the algorithms and data structures knowledge pertinent to resolving the problem, subsequently generating a problem-solving prompt.

In Coding Stage, we assign ChatGPT the role of a coder, tasked with perusing the problem and implementing this solution in a programming language, guided by the prompt provided by the prompt engineer.
Therefore, we update and customize the knowledge for each problem by performing absolute value matching via dictionaries to associate the tags of the problem with the tags in the Knowledge Library.
Following the review, we identified four representative examples for experimentation, ultimately selecting one as the one-shot example.

Simultaneously, to further investigate the capabilities of each method, we crafted a system prompt tailored for the four baselines methods with the aim of enhancing the quality of the generation results.

Drawing from its idea, we fashioned a two-phase process: initially, we allow ChatGPT to generate a step-by-step prompt for problem-solving, following which, the code of the problem is generated under the guidance of the prompt.
SCOT first generates a Structured COT, delineating the solution process in programming logic, then transmutes this Structured COT into a program using a specific programming language.
SCOT specifies a temperature setting of 0.8 and a Top_P value of 0.95, we adhered to these parameters in our experiments.
SCOT&KareCoder is a way to combine KareCoder’s knowledge-aware prompt with SCOT’s Structured COT.
In conducting the experiments for these research questions, we adhere to a default configuration of a one-shot setting, with the temperature parameter set to 1 and the Top_p parameter also set to 1.
We evaluated the tag generator’s accuracy with Cohen’s Kappa and manual evaluation methods.
This results likely arises from the inherent risks associated with the intermediate step of prompt or Structured COT generation.
However, multiple shots may lead to waste of resources caused by long input length.
Conversely, the integration of unsuitable external information could potentially yield adverse effects.
Moreover, KareCoder utilizing the Knowledge Description consistently outperforms the Plan method without a Knowledge Library.
In light of the experimental results, we hypothesize that this may be attributed to overlapping data within APPS that is present in the ChatGPT training set.
From this phenomenon, we can still discover the role of incorporating knowledge into code generation through a two-by-two comparison of Plan and KareCoder, SCOT and SCOT&KareCoder.
Although we have checked the tags generated by tag generator manually, the algorithms and data structures recommended may not always be the most fitting.
It is important to note that the existing dataset partitioning might lose relevance due to updates in the ChatGPT training data.
To address this, we have included release timestamps for each problem in the dataset.

Establishing Temperature=1 and Top_P=1 endows ChatGPT with greater randomness, thereby circumventing the generation of chained error code owing to errors encountered during the production of knowledge-aware prompt.
According to the cutoff date of ChatGPT’s training data - September 2021, we partitioned the dataset into CodeF pre2021-9 (comprising 805 problems) and CodeF post2021-9 (consisting of 718 problems).

citacoes.trecho: This study presents MPIrigen, a tool developed to assist MPI programmers in automatically generating correct MPI functions in an MPI-based domain decomposition parallel code.
Subsequently, we introduce a dedicated downstream task of MPI-based program generation by fine-tuning MonoCoder on HPCorpusMPI.
Comparative analysis against GPT-3.5 zero-shot performance, using a novel HPC-oriented evaluation method, demonstrates that MPIrigen excels in generating accurate MPI functions calls.

Figure 4: Performance breakdown of GPT3.5 using prompt “Generate the optimal MPI functions for the provided code, and supply in the response the entire complete code with those MPI functions: [CODE]”.
citacoes.localizador: p. 4 do PDF, legenda da Figura 4

citacoes.trecho: Any semantic information has been replaced using TokomPiler (Figure 1b) and thus, a measure of reliance of these pre-trained models on semantic information has been tested.
citacoes.localizador: p. 4 do PDF, parágrafo «RQ1: MPI code generation»

citacoes.trecho: This code completion task has been done over a thousand examples with up to 2048 tokens in HPCorpusMPI and under an initial context of 100, 300, and 600 tokens (Figure 2).
citacoes.localizador: p. 4 do PDF, parágrafo «RQ1: MPI code generation»

citacoes.trecho: Results show that as context grows, MonoCoder is significantly outperforming PolyCoder and GPT-3.5 results, while also proving to not fix on local semantics for those results, suggesting high generality capabilities.
citacoes.localizador: p. 4 do PDF, parágrafo «RQ1: MPI code generation»

citacoes.trecho: HPCorpusMPI is a corpus consisting of both of the corpora above but under the filter of MPI domain decomposition codes only and with duplication removal resulting in a total of 16,384 programs.

For convenience, the final dataset (with 13,322 programs) contains three fields – “Program”, “Code”, “MPI label” – and corresponds to the program’s GitHub username, the code with removed MPI functions, and the label of the locations and their MPI functions.
Figure 3: Performance breakdown of MPIrigen (fine-tuned MonoCoder-0.7B over 16K MPI codes from HPCorpusMPI) over programs containing (n) or less of MPI function calls (X axis).
citacoes.localizador: p. 4 do PDF, legenda da Figura 3

citacoes.trecho: Functions accuracy is measured for matched locations only and arguments accuracy for matched functions only.
citacoes.localizador: p. 5 do PDF, «Evaluation metric for RQ2, RQ3, RQ4»

citacoes.trecho: The results are given as a function of the number of original MPI calls (1-20), showcasing that accuracy drops as complexity grows (besides the ultra simplicity of one or two MPI function calls).
citacoes.localizador: p. 5 do PDF, «Evaluation metric for RQ2, RQ3, RQ4»

citacoes.trecho: The training was carried out with a batch size of 2, 2048 tokens and 3 epochs.
citacoes.localizador: p. 5 do PDF, «Results for RQ2, RQ3, RQ4»

citacoes.trecho: As shown in Figure 3, for MPIrigen, the location as well as functions accuracy under variance of 2 reach 80% and converge to 70%, while for arguments it reaches 95% and converge to 94%.
citacoes.localizador: p. 5 do PDF, «Results for RQ2, RQ3, RQ4»

citacoes.trecho: For GPT3.5 on the contrary, the accuracy converged to 50% for locations and approximately 55% and 80% for functions and arguments resp (Figure 4).
citacoes.localizador: p. 5 do PDF, «Results for RQ2, RQ3, RQ4»

citacoes.trecho: As the figure shows the accuracy of predicting the correct location varies for different MPI functions, and we believe it correlates with the proportion of different MPI calls in the training dataset and possibly in open-source repositories on GitHub.
citacoes.localizador: p. 5 do PDF, «Result analysis and future work»

citacoes.trecho: It would be thus an interesting study to develop a balanced MPI dataset and train MPIrigen on it.
citacoes.localizador: p. 5 do PDF, «Result analysis and future work»

citacoes.trecho: Currently, we do not evaluate the correctness of generated MPI codes, nonetheless we are envisioning an approach based on compilation and output verification as a part of immediate future work.

tecnicas.observacao: O objeto de investigação é a geração de código a partir do mesmo prompt (parte em linguagem natural de problemas do Multilingual HumanEval) traduzido para 23 línguas naturais, isto é, a generalização entre línguas naturais do prompt. 'instrucao' = descrição do problema em linguagem natural, completada pelo modelo (formato zero-shot herdado do HumanEval). O artigo não mostra o prompt: a parte de código do prompt (assinatura) e a eventual presença de exemplos na docstring são nao_informado no texto lido, por isso não se atribuem 'contexto' nem 'exemplos'. O inglês é a língua de origem das traduções, mas o estudo não o trata como linha de base. Por isso avaliada_isoladamente = nao e tipo_contrafactual = nenhum.

citacoes.trecho: In response, we introduce HumanEval-XL, a massively multilingual code generation benchmark specifically crafted to address this deficiency.
HumanEval-XL establishes connections between 23 NLs and 12 programming languages (PLs), and comprises of a collection of 22,080 prompts with an average of 8.33 test cases.
By ensuring parallel data across multiple NLs and PLs, HumanEval-XL offers a comprehensive evaluation platform for multilingual LLMs, allowing the assessment of the understanding of different NLs.
We make our evaluation code and data publicly available at https://github.com/FloatAI/humaneval-xl.
The extracted texts are translated into 23 different languages using GPT-4.
Translations with a low similarity score (threshold < 0.95) are rejected and subjected to re-translation.
Heuristic checks and manual evaluations are performed on the quality of the translated texts.
We have manually checked randomly sampled examples and make corrections if the translation is problematic.

tecnicas.observacao: Condição avaliada na geração de código: GPT-3.5 + CAPIR (ours), cujo prompt contém a tarefa (assinatura e docstring) e 5 APIs com descrições recomendadas pelo CAPIR (Figura 1c; Seção 5.2). O pacote inclui: Summarizer (gpt-3.5-turbo; gera pares <task, subtasks> a partir de exemplos de uso da documentação, com saída em formato JSON especificado no Prompt 1 → restricoes); Selector por embeddings que recupera k_e = 4 exemplos (→ exemplos e contexto, pois os exemplos vêm da documentação); Decomposer few-shot (→ decomposicao, exemplos); Retriever por embeddings (ada-embedding-002) sobre a documentação de APIs (→ contexto); Reranker_ws e Reranker_as por LLM que reordenam e filtram os APIs recuperados dentro e entre subtarefas (→ outro: reranqueamento/filtragem por LLM do contexto recuperado, sem categoria específica no dicionário); prompts com instruções em linguagem natural (→ instrucao). Base de comparação: GPT-3.5 em geração direta (instrucao). O contrafactual da Tabela 3 é do pacote inteiro contra a geração sem recomendação de API e contra GPT-3.5 + ADA-retrieve; o ganho não pode ser atribuído a um ingrediente isolado. O pacote não é híbrido no sentido de ajuste fino (o estudo declara uso sem treinamento), mas depende de modelo de embeddings pronto para seleção e recuperação.

O estudo afirma que esse baseline usa o mesmo pipeline de DocPrompting e CodeGenAPI, com embedding pronto. A Tabela 3 traz a mesma geração com e sem esses APIs (GPT-3.5 vs. GPT-3.5 + ADA-retrieve), e o texto analisa o contraste; é contrafactual do pacote de prompt aumentado por recuperação. O número de APIs inseridos para este baseline não é declarado separadamente: o texto diz apenas «we add 5 APIs for each task in the prompt» (nao_informado se vale igualmente para ADA-retrieve). citacoes.trecho: This paper investigates the performance of popular LLMs in handling repository-level repair tasks.
To solve the problem, we propose a simple and universal repository-level context extraction method (RLCE) designed to provide more precise context for repository-level code repair tasks.
To demonstrate the effectiveness of our method, we implement a preliminary method as the baseline that only provides the function itself where the error is located as the context.
Finally, 5 segments with the highest similarity are selected as the context.
We use two types of instructions, Simple and Detail, in the experiment.
We use the same instruction as the Detail method in the zero-shot strategy in the experiment and add a complete repair example.
To investigate the efficacy of the CoT strategy in the field of repository-level APR, we propose a straightforward zero-shot-CoT [14] approach in this paper.
Detailed descriptions of the Preliminary and Slice-similarity methods can be found in Section 4.3, both employing the one-shot prompting strategy.

citacoes.trecho: In these experiments, we remove three context sources and extra semantic information, excluding EF due to the inclusion of error localization.
Furthermore, datasets created too early may pose a potential risk of data leakage if used as training data for LLMs.
To minimize the risk of leakage due to the repositories being used as training data for LLMs, we set the search date condition to later than October 1, 2021.
From the analysis above, we hypothesize that in the CoT method, incorrect interpretations can introduce significant interference, leading to erroneous outcomes.

We posit that, for program repair tasks, a longer prompt may provide more information to the large language model, but simultaneously, it may also distract the model, increasing the difficulty of repair.
Additionally, in our experiments, we standardize the temperature parameter across all LLMs to 0, ensuring stable outputs when facing the same prompt.
Increasing the temperature parameter leads to unstable model outputs, potentially influencing the final results.
Secondly, an increase in the scale and complexity of repositories may escalate the cost and difficulty of context retrieval, affecting the reliability of the results.
However, the repository-level context offered by the preliminary method often proves redundant and imprecise and easily exceeds the prompt length limit of LLMs.
In practical repair tasks, it is desirable for the model to exhibit low sensitivity to prompting strategies.

However, given that RepoBugs is the only dataset known to us specifically designed for repository-level error repair, the generalization of our approach to datasets involving other error types may vary.
Then, the two experts independently evaluated all the experimental results.

O estudo a apresenta como «our text-augmented prompting» (p. 2). O contraste Direct vs. Text-Augmented, nos mesmos modelos, difere apenas no texto anexado conforme a descrição da seção 3.1; o prompt aumentado não é impresso literalmente no Apêndice D (só a descrição).

tecnicas.observacao: Parte da saída do Text-Augmented Prompting: fornece a captura de tela de referência, a captura da página renderizada a partir do código gerado, o código gerado como solução inicial e os textos extraídos, e pede que o modelo revise o código. Retorno da renderização do próprio código → feedback; textos extraídos e código anterior como insumo → contexto (herdado/insumo); papel e diretrizes → instrucao; código sintaticamente correto, marcador de imagem, resposta só com o HTML → restricoes. O comparador de que deriva é o Text-Augmented Prompting (Tabela 1 traz ambos). O contraste é de pacote: a rodada de revisão muda ao mesmo tempo o texto da instrução, acrescenta o código anterior e a captura renderizada, de modo que o efeito não é atribuível só à captura renderizada. Para modelos abertos, as duas capturas são concatenadas numa só imagem (p. 15), condição diferente da dos modelos comerciais. Uma única rodada de revisão.

Anotadores pagos a US$ 16/hora via Prolific; 60 participantes no total.

Regressão logística sobre diferenças das métricas prevê preferências humanas com 79,9% de acurácia no teste; taxas de vitória simuladas correlacionam com «win + tie» anotadas (Pearson r = 0.975, Kendall τ = 0.931).
Análise da curva de aprendizado do Design2Code-18B (Figura 9) e correlação das métricas com indicadores de dificuldade (Tabela 7, sobre GPT-4V self-revision) não são ablações de prompting.

citacoes.trecho: This can enable a new paradigm of front-end development in which multimodal large language models (MLLMs) directly convert visual designs into code implementations.
To rigorously benchmark MLLMs, we test various multimodal prompting methods on frontier models such as GPT-4o, GPT-4V, Gemini, and Claude.
Our fine-grained break-down metrics indicate that models mostly lag in recalling visual elements from the input webpages and generating correct layout designs.
We provide the reference webpage screenshot, along with the instruction to generate the HTML and CSS code (full prompt in Appendix D).

To reflect such a setting, we also explore a text-augmented prompting method, where we extract all text elements from the original webpage first and append these texts after the instruction prompt along with the screenshot input.

In this setting, we mitigate the difficulty of performing OCR and instead allow the model to focus more on layout design, where the model could copy text content from the prompt and insert it into the correct positions.

To test whether the models can visually contrast the websites rendered by their generated code and the reference websites to further improve the code generation, we develop a self-revision prompt where we provide the following as input: (1) the screenshot of the input webpage, (2) the screenshot of the generated webpage from text-augmented prompting, (3) the generated code from text-augmented prompting as the initial solution; then we ask the model to improve the generated implementation code so that the result can look closer to the reference webpage (full prompt is in Appendix D).
You are an expert web developer who specializes in HTML and CSS.
Include all CSS code in the HTML file itself.
Do not hallucinate any dependencies to external files.
Please compare the two webpages and refer to the provided text elements to be included, and revise the original HTML implementation to make it look exactly like the reference webpage.
citacoes.localizador: Apêndice D, p. 14 (PDF), prompt de self-revision

citacoes.trecho: For all commercial models, we use greedy decoding and set maximum new tokens to 4096.

Since most of the open-source models only support single-image input, we concatenate the reference screenshot and the generated screenshot into one image before prompting, following Jiang et al. (2024a).
Note that other open-source models like Qwen-VL-Chat (Bai et al., 2023) and Mantis (Jiang et al., 2024a) fail to generate HTML format in more than 80% cases, which are not reported here.
We keep getting empty responses with unexplained errors while testing Gemini 1.5.
Note that the comparisons here are not apple-to-apple comparisons, given the differences in model sizes and training data.

Self-revision has some minor improvement on block-match and position similarity for GPT-4V and Claude 3, but brings no improvement on Gemini Pro Vision and all other open-source models, potentially due to the limited capabilities of LLMs to do self-revision (Huang et al., 2023).
We use Gemini Pro Vision Direct Prompting as the baseline and collect the other seven methods' Win/Tie/Lose rates against this baseline (we randomly shuffle the ordering to avoid position biases).

The first desideratum of the task is that all visual elements from the reference webpage should be reproduced in the generated webpage, and the generated webpage should not hallucinate non-existent new elements.
WebSight VLM-8B excels at color recognition but hallucinates text contents.

Despite our intention of democratizing webpage building, we recognize the potential dual use danger of Design2Code technologies, such as automated generation of malicious websites, or even generating code for licensed websites.
Moreover, when performing manual filtering, we explicitly filtered out webpages containing private or sensitive information (e.g., dating website profiles).
We will provide clear ethical use guidelines for all data, code, and model releases to define acceptable and unacceptable use cases.

In table 3, we observe a significant performance drop on GPT-4o compared to the “easy” version of our dataset, and state-of-the-art models fail to generate 30% - 40% of the block elements (Block-Match).
Interestingly, GPT-4o can steadily improve performance through text augmentation and self-revision, while Gemini 1.5 Pro cannot.
However, the matching may still not be perfect, especially when there are large granularity differences (our search does not consider merging non-contiguous blocks).
Fleiss’ kappa for pairwise model comparison is 0.46 (5 annotators).

tecnicas.nome_original: library of prompts (stand-alone LLM; linha «LLM only» da Table 1)
tecnicas.localizador: Seção 4.1, p. 6-7 (PDF p. 6-7); Table 1, p. 18 (PDF p. 18)
tecnicas.observacao: Biblioteca de prompts aplicada em laço iterativo até solução correta ou esgotamento da biblioteca. instrucao: persona («You are a good synthesizer»), requisitos em linguagem natural, estímulo emocional e pedido motivacional de nova tentativa; restricoes: especificação SyGuS/SMT-LIB no prompt e regras de formato (uma única função, sem funções embutidas, sem iterações); decomposicao: solução pedida em Lisp e depois convertida para SMT-LIB por outro prompt; raciocinio: só nos benchmarks de invariantes (explicação das restrições antes da solução); feedback: novo prompt após falha do verificador, com a resposta anterior mantida na conversa. Sem base de prompt identificável na Table 1, por isso mecanismos_acrescentados vazio. Os comparadores executados (enumerator, A*, cvc5) são sintetizadores sem LLM: não constituem condição sem a técnica em condições comparáveis e não isolam mecanismos de prompting.

tecnicas.localizador: Seção 4.1, p. 6 (PDF p. 6); Prompt 1, p. 6
tecnicas.observacao: Frase «Write it correctly, or I will lose my job and 100 grandmothers will die. Don’t disappoint me.» no Prompt 1. O estudo relata em prosa comparação com «standard, non-emotional prompts» (aumento de 8%), sem informar amostra, modelo, número de execuções nem se o valor é variação relativa ou p.p.; os detalhes são remetidos à versão estendida, não consultada. Mecanismos do pacote listados conforme o Prompt 1; a presença de raciocinio depende da categoria (não informada para este experimento).

tecnicas.nome_original: solicitar a solução em Lisp e converter para SMT-LIB (Lisp to SMT-LIB Converter)
tecnicas.localizador: Seção 4.1, p. 6-7 (PDF p. 6-7); Prompt 3, p. 7
tecnicas.observacao: Etapa intermediária: o LLM escreve a função em Lisp e um segundo prompt («You are a good programming language converter») a converte para SMT-LIB. Em subconjunto de 50 benchmarks, o estudo relata em prosa melhoria de 6% de Lisp sobre Python e que ambos foram melhores que pedir SMT-LIB diretamente (sem número para este último contraste). O contraste Lisp × Python varia a linguagem intermediária, não a presença da etapa; o contraste com/sem etapa (SMT-LIB direto) é só qualitativo. Condições detalhadas apenas na versão estendida, não consultada.

tecnicas.localizador: Seção 4.1, «Prompts for invariant synthesis», p. 7 (PDF p. 7)

O texto atribui o desempenho inferior do iLLM-synth em INV à ausência desse prompt personalizado (hipótese do estudo, p. 16), mas iLLM-synth difere em vários outros ingredientes, portanto não é contraste pareado.

tecnicas.localizador: Prompt 2, p. 7 (PDF p. 7); Seção 7, p. 16 (PDF p. 16)
tecnicas.observacao: Após falha na verificação, o LLM recebe «You are close to the right answer. Take another guess...» (sem contraexemplo), até 6 tentativas completas. O estudo relata só contribuição por rodada (média de 4 tentativas nos benchmarks resolvidos; na 6ª iteração, novas soluções < 2%, 0 em LIA), sem condição de tentativa única com o mesmo protocolo.

tecnicas.localizador: Seções 3 e 5, p. 4-13 (PDF p. 4-13); Seção 7, p. 16; Table 1, p. 18
tecnicas.observacao: Pacote híbrido: usa as mesmas técnicas de prompting do LLM stand-alone (Seção 4) e converte as soluções incorretas do LLM em uma wCFG/pCFG que guia um enumerador (top-down probabilístico ou A*) dentro de CEGIS; enumerador, inferência de pesos e CEGIS estão fora do escopo. Comparado com o mesmo algoritmo com peso 1 para todas as regras («enumerator» e «A*»), o que isola o pacote, não um mecanismo de prompting. Variantes e-/A* diferem só no enumerador (componente fora do escopo), por isso não são técnicas de prompting distintas. mecanismos_acrescentados em relação ao enumerador sem LLM, do qual deriva.

tecnicas.localizador: Seção 6, p. 13-15 (PDF p. 13-15); Prompt 4, p. 13-14; Seção 7, p. 16; Table 1, p. 18
tecnicas.observacao: Pacote híbrido: o enumerador chama o LLM a cada n-ésima iteração com prompt de papel («You are teaching a student to write SMT-LIB») → instrucao; restrições do problema e «You must print only the code and nothing else» → restricoes; programa parcial enumerado fornecido como insumo → contexto; candidato falho mais recente e contraexemplo acrescentados depois de falha → feedback. As funções auxiliares retornadas viram regras e pesos da gramática (fora do escopo). Não usa os prompts da Seção 4 (prompts mais curtos). Comparado com o enumerador com pesos uniformes; isola o pacote, não um mecanismo.

riscos.descricao: Os problemas SyGuS são públicos e podem estar nos dados de treinamento do LLM; os autores acreditam que as soluções não estavam públicas, sem verificação descrita.

GPT-3.5 se comporta de forma não determinística sem possibilidade de semente; respostas podem não ser reprodutíveis; pequenas variações no número de benchmarks resolvidos e maior variação no tempo médio.
Reprodutibilidade: a OpenAI pode descontinuar ou atualizar o modelo e a API, alterando o comportamento.

Modos de falha do LLM stand-alone: mal-entendidos por restrições complexas, erros sintáticos simples (operandos em ordem errada, concatenação de bit-vectors na ordem errada) e erros semânticos simples; o estudo também levanta a hipótese de que a orientação do LLM atrapalha o enumerador em benchmarks com restrições complexas e soluções curtas com operadores menos comuns.
Entre os erros sintáticos identificados está alucinar operações.
Com especificações por exemplos (PBE), o LLM tende a sobreajustar aos exemplos com um grande case split, inútil para guiar o enumerador; por isso essas trilhas foram omitidas.
Viés de benchmark: o conjunto SyGuS pode não ser diverso nem representativo de problemas reais.
Hiperparâmetros não ajustados (temperatura, pesos, profundidade de enumeração, heurísticas); resultados melhores ou piores poderiam ser obtidos.

mitigacoes.descricao: Renomear funções e variáveis dos benchmarks para nomes genéricos, para evitar soluções baseadas só nos nomes das funções.
Registro das respostas e parâmetros do LLM em todos os experimentos.
Resultados não determinísticos (marcados ⋄) executados 3 vezes, com média relatada.
Verificação dos candidatos por solver SMT (Z3) no CEGIS e verificação de formato do programa Lisp extraído; soluções incompletas e funções auxiliares malformadas são descartadas.

citacoes.trecho: In this paper, we set out to investigate whether off-the-shelf large language models can solve formal program synthesis problems.
We design a library of prompts for program synthesis problems with logical specifications and a single target function to synthesize.
These prompts are deployed in an iterative loop, until a correct solution is obtained, or the library of prompts is exhausted.

On a subset of 50 benchmarks, we observed that soliciting responses in Lisp resulted in a 6% enhancement in the resolution of benchmarks compared to utilizing Python (and both were better than asking for SMT-lib directly).
Incorporating the emotional prompt leads to an 8% increase in the likelihood of generating accurate solutions compared to standard, non-emotional prompts in our study.
Write it correctly, or I will lose my job and 100 grandmothers will die. Don’t disappoint me.
You are close to the right answer. Take another guess. You have to try something different, think harder.

Inspired by “chain-of-thought” [42] prompting, where the LLM is asked to provide a step-by-step explanation, we augment our prompting strategy for invariants by asking the LLM first to explain the constraints.
The final prompts in our prompt library are to ask the LLM to convert any functions given in Lisp to correct SMT-LIB functions:

The first method, shown in Figure 1, prompts an LLM for solutions to the benchmark, and generates a pCFG from these solutions before deploying an enumerative synthesizer, increasing the chance of the LLM solving the synthesis problem outright.
In this section, we describe how we prompt the LLM as a stand-alone synthesizer. These prompting techniques are then also deployed by pCFG-synth.
We give the LLM the constraints from the target synthesis problem and the partially complete program at the point the enumerator calls the LLM.
If the LLM fails to solve the problem with this prompt, we later add the most recently failed candidate solution and the counterexample it failed on.
As a baseline, we run the same algorithms assigning a weight of 1 to every rule in the grammar (referred to as “enumerator” and A∗ respectively in the results).
The SyGuS problems are publicly available and might be part of the training data for the LLM we use, although we believe the solutions were not publicly available at the time of training.

We have recorded the responses and parameters generated by the LLM in all experiments, but these may not be reproducible [33] since GPT-3.5 behaves non-deterministically in a way that cannot be seeded.

Broadly, we identify the following common failures: Misunderstandings due to complex constraints (the LLM suggests solutions that are not syntactically close to the correct solution); simple syntactic errors, e.g., applying non-commutative operators to operands in the wrong order, concatenating bit-vectors in the wrong order or hallucinating operations; simple semantic errors, e.g., operators in the wrong order.
We hypothesize that the LLM guidance becomes an impediment to the enumerator in these scenarios.
This is not useful for guiding the enumerator because the LLM overfits to the examples in the specification and fails to provide any bias towards operators other than “if-then-else”.
Furthermore, we rename any functions and variables in the SyGuS benchmarks to generic names to avoid the LLM producing solutions solely based on the function names.
We run nondeterministic results, marked ⋄, 3 times and report the average (standard deviation is less than 1% for all methods except the baseline enumerator for number of benchmarks solved).

tecnicas.observacao: Prompt base: assinatura da função-alvo com docstring (descrição em linguagem natural → instrucao; assinatura com anotação de tipos e exemplos de entrada/saída no formato doctest, tratados como especificação → restricoes) e os imports correspondentes. O estudo a declara linha de base. Para os modelos CodeLLaMAInstruct, o prompt é convertido em instruções geradas automaticamente e no template de conversa do modelo (Apêndice A.2, p. 12–13 do PDF), o que altera o formato da condição para esses modelos.

tecnicas.localizador: Seção 4.1, p. 3 do PDF; Tabela 1, p. 5 do PDF; Figura 2a, p. 6 do PDF
tecnicas.observacao: Acrescenta ao prompt Direct uma função auxiliar irrelevante (assinatura, docstring e implementação), amostrada de um pool de soluções canônicas do HumanEval, inserida entre os imports e a assinatura-alvo. Código fornecido como insumo → contexto; os autores interpretam que a função atua como demonstração semelhante a few-shot → exemplos. O contraste Direct × Irrelevant isola o pacote 'função auxiliar irrelevante', sem separar contexto de exemplos. Forma de amostragem por problema (uma função por problema, semente) não informada.

tecnicas.localizador: Seção 4.1, p. 3–4 do PDF; Tabela 1, p. 5 do PDF; Figura 2b, p. 6 do PDF
tecnicas.observacao: Duas etapas: o modelo primeiro sintetiza a função auxiliar relevante a partir da assinatura do HumanEval e, depois, essa implementação é anexada ao prompt para implementar a função-alvo (etapas encadeadas → decomposicao; os autores comparam ao Least-to-Most prompting). A implementação da função auxiliar no prompt recebe contexto e exemplos pelo mesmo critério aplicado às condições Irrelevant e Oracle (mesmo ingrediente: função completa inserida antes da assinatura-alvo). O contraste com Direct isola o pacote, não a decomposição separadamente. Não informado se cada uma das oito gerações da função-alvo usa uma implementação auxiliar distinta.

tecnicas.localizador: Seção 4.1, p. 4 do PDF; Tabela 1, p. 5 do PDF
tecnicas.observacao: Acrescenta ao prompt Direct a função auxiliar relevante escrita por humanos (solução canônica do HumanEval). Mesmo ingrediente das condições Irrelevant e Step-by-step (função completa no prompt) → contexto e exemplos. Para CodeLLaMAInstruct, a função auxiliar é apresentada como primeiro turno de conversa e o segundo turno inclui a frase 'You can use the above function whenever you needed.' (Apêndice A.2, p. 13 do PDF), instrução ausente nos modelos base.

citacoes.trecho: We measure the effectiveness of an auxiliary function in a code synthesis task by designing several prompts varying their existence and type.

Currently, the prompt used in the existing work to solve the task is mainly composed of a target function signature with the corresponding import statements (Ben Allal et al., 2022; Cassano et al., 2022; Chen et al., 2021).
We attached the auxiliary function signature and their implementation between the import statements and the target function signature to allow LLMs to access the knowledge about auxiliary functions.
No auxiliary function (Direct): Prompt consists of a target function signature without auxiliary functions. This setting acts as a baseline in our experiments.
We constructed an auxiliary function pool with the canonical solutions in the HumanEval dataset (Chen et al., 2021) and sampled an irrelevant function from the pool to construct the prompt.
Concretely, LLMs first synthesize relevant auxiliary function and then it is attached to the prompt for implementing the target function.
Human-written relevant auxiliary function (Oracle): We provide a relevant auxiliary function written by humans to the model.
In this sense, this approach is similar to the Least-to-Most prompting (Zhou et al., 2023a) that solves target tasks with the model-generated answer of predefined subtasks.
In Figure 2, we found that the irrelevant auxiliary function acts as a demonstration like few-shot prompting so that the few models exhibit performance improvement.
We apply two perturbations: (1) replacing the name of the auxiliary function with other function names in the HumanEval dataset or (2) deleting the docstring included in the function.

The experimental results show that even if the functionality of the function does not change, a performance drop is observed depending on the name of the function or the existence of a docstring (Figure 3).
We design a prompt with nine auxiliary functions followed by the target function signature.
However, since the location of relevant functions is independent of their functionality, LLMs need to be tuned to robustly utilize them regardless of where they are placed.

Usually, the model-generated white-box implementations tend to repeat the identical mechanism inside the auxiliary function, which is not preferred in software engineering fields (Hunt and Thomas, 2000).
To reduce the variance of the pass@1 metric, we generate eight implementations for each problem when estimating the model performance.

citacoes.trecho: We filtered out some examples in the HumanEval dataset that are not appropriate for using auxiliary functions.

citacoes.trecho: We also conducted a thorough inspection of the newly crafted extended functions and verify that there was no personally identifiable or sensitive information.
The prompt is formulated into two consecutive turns where the first turn is about the auxiliary function and the second one is about generating the target function.
We observe that providing an irrelevant auxiliary function brings meaningful improvement on few models.

Contrafactual: comparação com RawGPT (problema dado diretamente ao ChatGPT, zero-shot), mesmo modelo e temperatura, cinco execuções e teste t. O 'sim' vale para o pacote e não autoriza atribuir o efeito a um mecanismo isolado. Os exemplos de invocação contidos na descrição do problema (método, descrição, exemplos de chamada) existem nas duas condições e foram tratados como especificação da tarefa, não como exemplos resolvidos.

observacoes.descricao: Em média, o FlowGen gera quatro testes por problema antes da reunião de revisão e seis depois.
Avaliação de qualidade do código com Pylint 3.0.4 e densidade de exceções tratadas; resultados por atividade só para HumanEval e MBPP, por compartilharem problemas e código com as versões ET.

RQ3: resultados de estabilidade por versão e temperatura aparecem só nas Figuras 2 e 3; não foram extraídos valores numéricos das figuras.

citacoes.trecho: We emulate three process models, FlowGenWaterfall, FlowGenTDD, and FlowGenScrum, by assigning LLM agents to embody roles (i.e., requirement engineer, architect, developer, tester, and scrum master) that correspond to everyday development activities and organize their communication patterns.
The agents work collaboratively using chain-of-thought and prompt composition with continuous self-refinement to improve the code quality.

Our findings show that FlowGenScrum excels compared to other process models, achieving a Pass@1 of 75.2, 65.5, 82.5, and 56.7 in HumanEval, HumanEval-ET, MBPP, and MBPP-ET, respectively (an average of 15% improvement over RawGPT).
Notably, integrating CodeT into FlowGenScrum resulted in statistically significant improvements, achieving the highest Pass@1 scores.
Instruction leverages chain-of-thought reasoning [40, 20] and refers to role-specific instruction listed in steps, such as 1) analyzing the requirement and 2) writing the requirement documentation.
Finally, Context contains the programming question, the agent conversation history, or the agent-generated artifacts.
We design testers using a prompt composition technique, which is shown to improve the LLM-generated result [22, 50].
It is important to note that oracles are kept aside and never used in the code-generation process.

We follow a disordered communication pattern in the design of FlowGenScrum, because, in sprint meetings, every development role can provide their opinion (e.g., to simulate the planning poker process).
1) Read the context documents; and 2) Write the code. Ensure that the code you write is efficient, readable, and follows best practices.

citacoes.trecho: We assign the agents from both the downstream activity and the tester to examine the generated artifacts and provide suggestions.
In our implementation, we currently set t=3.
We send prompts using JSON format [41] and send all the conversation history as part of the prompt [14].
As a baseline for comparison, we directly give the programming problems to ChatGPT (which we refer to as RawGPT).
To study the impact of each development activity on code quality, we remove each activity separately and re-execute FlowGen.
We also ensure reliability of our results by repeating all of the aforementioned approach three times.
Hence, as a pilot study, we made the developer agent repeats the implementation activity multiple times to produce several versions of the code (i.e., FlowGenScrum+Test).
We apply these two techniques using their released code, replacing the LLM version and temperature settings with those used by FlowGenScrum, and repeat the experiment five times.

Upon manual investigation of prevalent test failures types, we discover that FlowGenWaterfall and FlowGenTDD introduce various validations and enforce programming naming conventions in the generated code, which may help improve code quality but cause tests to fail.
One limitation is that there is no guarantee of the correctness of the generated tests.

riscos.descricao: Programas que compilam podem falhar na execução; CoCoGen não trata erros FUNC, que surgem na execução após compilação bem-sucedida.

Soluções degeneradas (código simplista ou redundante) frequentemente passam na compilação, tornando a verificação por compilador ineficaz; também há soluções que interpretam mal os requisitos (Figuras 7-9).

riscos.descricao: Erros de compilação residuais não corrigidos pelas iterações (blocos Markdown, parênteses desbalanceados não corrigidos em três iterações, confusão com a função de biblioteca sum); desempenho atinge platô com mais iterações.

A compilação bem-sucedida não garante segurança para execução; o estudo menciona requisitos de segurança entre os aspectos da correção funcional, sem detalhar se se trata de cibersegurança ou de segurança operacional, e não avalia o aspecto.
Exceções em Pass@1 atribuídas pelos autores à variação das soluções geradas; sugerem n maior (por exemplo, 1000) para estabilizar.
Uso de análise estática aumenta a latência; medida por caso de teste: média 1,27 s, mínimo 0,359 s, máximo 6,984 s; os autores a consideram aceitável.
Falha da recuperação estrutural em 6,8% dos erros: o LLM não segue as demonstrações CodeQL e gera consultas inválidas, ou a consulta não retorna resultado.

mitigacoes.descricao: Feedback do compilador combinado à recuperação de contexto do projeto para corrigir erros de compilação ligados ao contexto (a própria técnica), medido contra condições sem CF.
Recomendação de verificação adicional por testes e revisão manual para assegurar a correção funcional.
Geração de n = 20 soluções por tarefa com estimador não enviesado de Pass@k para reduzir a variância amostral.
Sugestão de n muito maior (por exemplo, 1000) para estabilizar Pass@1.
Trabalho futuro: integrar documentação, resultados de busca na web e logs de execução como referência para a geração.

citacoes.trecho: We present COCOGEN, a new code generation approach that uses compiler feedback to improve the LLM-generated code.
It then iteratively aligns and fixes the identified errors using information extracted from the code repository.

Experimental results show that COCOGEN significantly improves the vanilla LLMs by over 80% in generating code dependent on the project context and consistently outperforms the existing retrieval-based code generation baselines.
We implement this by transforming the textual compiler feedback into an SQL query using the ChatGPT.
Several examples of paired compiler feedback and SQL queries are provided as demonstrations for in-context learning.

In addition to returning the project-level context retrieved by the SQL query, we also enhance the acquired context by retrieving similar code snippets using dense passage retrieval (Karpukhin et al., 2020).
This process goes iterative until no error is reported by the compiler, resulting in an error-free solution that aligns with the project's environment.
It is noteworthy that COCOGEN does not take into account FUNC errors, which arise during execution despite successful compilation.
This line of method denotes directly inputting the task requirements into LLM for code generation, without providing additional context.
More precisely, we retrieve project contexts aligned with the task instructions semantically through embedding similarity, and leverage them to augment the prompts of LLMs for better code generation.
Specifically, it involves retrieving similar code snippets derived from the previously generated ones, and employing them to augment the prompts of LLMs.
One distinguishing feature is that this baseline does not leverage compiler feedback.
To explore the impact of each component within COCOGEN on overall performance, we remove various components from COCOGEN, including the compiler, SQL retriever, and semantic retriever.
Notably, the configuration that excludes the compiler and SQL, relying solely on semantic retrieval, is known as RepoCoder (Zhang et al., 2023a).
We attribute such exceptions to variations in the generated solutions.

To reduce sampling variance, we generate n ≥ k solutions (for this study, n = 20 and k = 1, 5, 10) for each task, count the number of correct solutions c ≤ n that pass the unit tests, and calculate the unbiased estimator:
However, it is important to note that even programs that compile successfully can experience execution failures.
Furthermore, the successful compilation of programs does not guarantee their safety for execution.

As a result, while our findings indicate improvements in quality metrics through the correction of code to properly leverage context, it is imperative to undertake additional verification methods such as testing and manual review to ascertain the functional correctness of the generated code.
Our analysis reveals that degenerate solutions frequently pass compilation, rendering compiler-based verification ineffective.
Utilizing static analysis tools to inspect code typically results in increased latency.
The average latency is recorded at 1.27 seconds, with a minimum of 0.359 seconds and a maximum of 6.984 seconds.

For the remaining 6.8% of cases, there are two reasons for failure: first, the LLM does not follow the demonstrated CodeQL examples and generates queries that are syntactically or semantically incorrect, thus rejected by the CodeQL query system; second, the query does not return anything because the specified conditions in the query are not satisfied in project context.
In the inference stage, we set the decoding temperature to 0.7, and adopt the top-k sampling strategy.
There are 55, 68, and 23 tasks associated with each dependency level, respectively.
This dataset comprises 85 function-level tasks and 145 project-level tasks.

citacoes.trecho: Code translation between programming languages (PLs) is a long-existing and critical task in software engineering, facilitating the modernization of legacy systems, ensuring cross-platform compatibility, and enhancing software performance.

To mitigate output format bias, we propose a strategic combination of prompt engineering and regular expressions that effectively extracts source code from mixed-format outputs, enabling the eleven open-source models to achieve an average Code Extraction Success Rate (CSR) of 92.73%.
The first template is proposed by Pan et al. 2024 for evaluating open-source LLMs.
Lastly, Controlled Prompt is a variation of Vanilla Prompt designed to control the output format of the models.
Additionally, for the instruction in our prompt template, we follow OpenAI’s suggested prompting strategy, i.e., “Ask the model to adopt a persona”
Vanilla Prompt instruct the models to ”Output code only” as seen in Fig. 4.
For prompt engineering, we modify the Vanilla Prompt (Section 3.3) by adding a control statement that instructs the model to generate the code excerpt within triple back-ticks (Wrapped Code format).
We use the Regex in Fig. 6 to find and extract source code from the generated outputs.

It is crucial to understand and address variations in output format, as non-code elements can interfere with evaluation metrics, resulting in biased (inaccurate or unfair) assessments of model performance and comparisons.

In this paper, as the CodeNet benchmark contains one test case per sample, there may be translations considered computationally accurate, but that do not contain identical functionality to the input program, i.e., false positives.
Results in RQ3 show that our current specific prompt and regex may not apply to all models, which is particularly evident in the case of the Mixtral 8X7B model.
This suggests that the presence of additional text significantly inflates the Data Flow component score.

For instance, accounting for output format is crucial when benchmarking open-source models against closed-source ones, as the latter tend to exhibit more consistent output format characteristics, which could bias the results in their favor.
Using Greedy Decoding guarantees the reproducibility of the inference outputs across multiple runs.

When we compare the metrics (BLEU and CodeBLEU) computed on the extracted code (CRE, VRE) against the metrics calculated over the direct output from inference (CDE, VDE), we exclude points where the Regex does not match to ensure the same data points for both experiments (intersection set).
Regarding the labeling of output formats, this task was undertaken by the first author of this paper.

While this could introduce subjective bias or errors in labeling and taxonomy, we established clear, easily identifiable categories to minimize ambiguity and enhance consistency in our categorization process.
We replicate their experimental setup, using deepseek-coder-33b-instruct (deepseek-ai, 2024) with greedy decoding, and remove the triple-backtick suffix from the translation prompt templates.
The CRE approach achieved an impressive average MSR of 93.40%, coupled with an average CR of 52.19% and an average CA of 35.74% over the models.
The second highest CA is for VRE, with 35.74%.
After this refinement, our final dataset retained 93.17% of the original filtered samples, resulting in 3,657 translation pairs for answering RQ4.

tecnicas.localizador: Seção 6, p. 5-6 do PDF (Tabelas 2 e 3); RQ4, Figuras 9-12, p. 8-9 do PDF
tecnicas.observacao: Proposta do estudo: reescrita automática, determinística e por regras (9 reduções para equações, 7 para expressões), da fórmula do prompt para forma reduzida, mantendo o texto em inglês. Classificada como otimizacao_prompt (refinamento automático do próprio prompt), embora não haja busca nem seleção; leitura alternativa possível é outro. Herdados do prompt base: instrução em linguagem natural (instrucao) e especificação formal, pré/pós-condições e formato de saída fixo (restricoes). Contrafactual: prompts reduzidos contra prompts mutados (mesmo texto, fórmula mutada sem redução) e contra prompts originais (Figura 9); também contra cada ataque (Figura 10) e Top-K na distância 5 (Figura 11) e no Clover (Figura 12).

tecnicas.observacao: Condição comparadora da redução: prompt com a mesma parte textual e fórmula sintaticamente mutada, semanticamente equivalente (distâncias 1-5). As mutações e os ataques são perturbações adversariais propostas pelo estudo para avaliar e explorar falhas de robustez, não técnicas de prompting para melhorar a geração; por isso ficam como comparador, sem categoria acrescentada. O contraste original contra mutado mede a perda de robustez, não o efeito de uma técnica.

citacoes.trecho: Finally, to mitigate syntactic robustness failures in LLMs, we propose a pre-processing step that uses reductions to transform formulas in prompts to a simplified form.

Our experimental results demonstrate that the syntactic robustness of LLM-based code generation improves significantly using our approach, improving syntactic robustness of LLMs from 54.05% to 74.42%.
Then, we feed the reduced prompt with the same English text and the reduced mathematical formula to the LLM-based code generator to generate the target code.
We experiment with Chain-of-thought (CoT) [100] and Deeply Understanding Problems (DUP) [116] approaches as they are zero-shot prompting techniques that are generalizable, and cost-efficient.
citacoes.localizador: Seção 7, Benchmark Models, p. 7 do PDF

citacoes.trecho: For CoT, we use trigger-based prompts (e.g., “Let’s solve this step-by-step”) to preserve automation [60].
citacoes.localizador: Seção 7, Benchmark Models, p. 7 do PDF

citacoes.trecho: DUP, which addresses semantic misunderstandings for mathematical reasoning, has achieved state-of-the-art results on arithmetic tasks [6] and is adapted here for mathematical code generation.
citacoes.localizador: Seção 7, Benchmark Models, p. 7 do PDF

citacoes.trecho: In code generation accuracy, Gpt-3.5 and Gpt-4 frameworks outperform others, achieving ≥ 85% on HumanEval [21], a trend reflected in our results; thus, framework-based techniques are applied only to Gpt models, excluding Llama models due to lower performance.
citacoes.localizador: Seção 7, Benchmark Models, p. 7 do PDF

citacoes.trecho: However, the generated codes from Gpt-4o are not semantically equivalent.
Thus, we conclude that LLMs do not achieve syntactic robustness and increasing number of mutations (equivalently, increasing syntactic distance) leads to a decrease in syntactic robustness.
Our evaluation demonstrates that LLMs are vulnerable to adversarial prompt-based attacks, motivating the need for assessing and improving the syntactic robustness of LLM-based code generators.
The goal is to induce incorrect or non-compiling code without changing the intended semantics.
LLMs are inherently non-deterministic.

citacoes.trecho: To address this, we experimented with various temperature, top_p, and seed configurations (where applicable) and selected the most deterministic settings, detailed in our artifact [7].

citacoes.trecho: Additionally, we executed the LLM-based code generator five times per prompt to mitigate variability.

This issue is even more pronounced in Llama-based models, where code is generated without user input processing in approximately 150 cases for Llama-3.1-70B and 600 cases for CodeLlama.

Although we selected o4-mini for its efficiency over larger reasoning models like o3 and o1-pro, our experiments reveal that it still takes approximately 4× more time than Gpt-4o and about 10× more time than Gpt-3.5 for comparable tasks.
First, there is the possibility that the Gpt API (for Gpt-3.5, Gpt-4o, and o4-mini) may be learning from prior requests we send.

citacoes.trecho: This work is a systematic effort to investigate how to construct effective prompts for LLM-based automated program repair (APR) by composing facts extracted from the buggy program and external sources.
In this work, we investigate a zero-shot APR approach.
The prompt is constructed with the directive “Please fix the buggy function provided below and output a corrected version” along with the included subset of facts.
We employed the standard chain-of-thought [15] approach by instructing the LLM to reason about the provided facts, as detailed in supplementary materials (Appendix C).
To address it, we explicitly added the import statements in the current file to the prompts.
Thus, to automate creating bug-tailored prompts, we introduce MANIPLE, a random forest trained to select relevant facts for inclusion in the prompts.
Additionally, we trained MANIPLE only on the top five highest-performing fact sets.

Inspired by this approach, we added a variant of angelic forest to a prompt; this variant combines variable values at the beginning of a function’s execution coupled with the angelic values at the end of a function’s execution, i.e. the input/output requirements of the function.
A corrected function must satisfy all these cases.
citacoes.localizador: PDF p. 15, Apêndice B, template de Angelic Values (2.3)

citacoes.trecho: To estimate the utility of each fact, we generated prompts containing all subsets of the considered 7 facts (the remaining one, the buggy function, is always present in the prompt), which resulted in a total of 19228 prompts for BGP314, which is less than 314 × 2^7 since some facts are not available for some bugs.
Since tests do not fully capture the intended behaviour, automatically generated patches based on tests may be incorrect [29].
Too much information in the prompt “distracts” the LLM from the relevant part of the issue description, significantly reducing pass@1 and the correctness rate.
Nondeterminism in LLMs leads to varying outcomes between responses, which poses a challenge for analysing results [26].
To alleviate it, we use the pass@k measure, which represents the probability that at least one query out of k succeeds at solving a problem.
In assessing LLMs, we recognise the challenge of potential data leakage, as some training datasets are not publicly available.
Thus, our findings are robust even with possible data leakage, and using the same model across our baselines partially mitigates this issue.

Meanwhile, enumerating sets of facts via e.g. greedy strategies while repairing each bug might be impractical, because of the high cost of LLM queries and the necessity to generate multiple responses due to LLMs’ nondeterminism.
As of March 2024, the cost of reproducing the experiments detailed in this paper, using the OpenAI API [30] for GPT-3.5 and DeepInfra [31] for llama3-70B, is estimated at $479 + $269.
Without listing import statements of the current file in APR prompts, the LLM may generate arbitrary import statements and call functions that are not defined within the repository.
The pass@5 calculated from the above example was 0.271, which suggests a noticeable enhancement in the fix rate.
The proportion of prompts that successfully led to a fix, incorporating CoT, stood at 0.46; this figure fell to 0.38 in the absence of CoT.
Each patch undergoes evaluation by two independent raters.
To ensure the model’s generalisability and to prevent overfitting, we employed k-fold cross-validation with k = 5.
For a fair comparison, we supply the same prompts, built from these facts, to MANIPLE and all the baselines.
On our testing dataset of 157 bugs, MANIPLE repairs 88 bugs, 17% above the best configuration.

Empirical evidence shows that MANIPLE significantly outperforms a universal fact selection strategy, fixing 11 more bugs than a generic set of facts that exhibited the optimal performance on the training data.
For instance, the fact set 0010101 achieves a pass@1 of 0.21 on GPT-3.5 for the Sanic project, which is below the highest pass@1 score of 0.26.

riscos.descricao: O prompting CoT zero-shot reduziu a taxa de aprovação dos modelos pequenos e médios em relação ao prompt padrão, com queda mais acentuada no modelo de 3B; no estudo de caso, os passos de CoT reinterpretados de forma ambígua levaram a código que falha.

riscos.descricao: Variabilidade do desempenho conforme a formulação do prompt, que o estudo chama de aleatoriedade do modelo em resposta a estilos de prompt; os grupos de CoT apresentam desvio-padrão maior que o grupo LCP entre paráfrases. Trata-se de sensibilidade à formulação, não de variação entre execuções repetidas.

O estudo aponta que a eficácia das estratégias de decomposição existentes depende de LLMs avançados como GPT-4, em particular de chamadas de API, o que limita sua aplicabilidade prática; não quantificado.

mitigacoes.descricao: Reformulação dos prompts em 15 versões por categoria (3 sementes manuais e 4 paráfrases geradas por GPT-4 para cada) para mitigar a aleatoriedade do modelo em resposta a estilos de prompt, com relato de média e desvio-padrão.
Verificação da implementação do SFT padrão contra o Pass@1 guloso relatado para CodeM-Python, com margem de erro declarada inferior a 1%.

citacoes.trecho: Code generation aims to understand the problem description and generate corresponding code snippets, where existing works generally decompose such complex tasks into intermediate steps by prompting strategies, such as Chain-of-Thought and its variants.
We use the logical comment prompting strategy to guide the model to generate comments explaining the code logic in the decoding stage.
This setting uses the LCP strategy to guide standardly fine-tuned models generating codes with comments.
As another baseline, this setting uses zero-shot-CoT (Kojima et al., 2022) on the standardly fine-tuned models, and the detailed prompt is the “CoT-pre1” appended in the Appendix 5.1 Table 11.
We construct the standard instruction template in WizardCoder (Luo et al., 2023) for the CodeM-Python dataset, and the training objection is cross entropy.
During the inference stage, the logical comment prompt (LCP) strategy will be used.
To accommodate the task of guiding the model to generate annotations, we adopt a contrastive learning approach to encourage the model to emphasize code comments more during the fine-tuning process.

Furthermore, for a more nuanced analysis, we segregate CoT into two categories: the first involves specifying the chain of thought text before generating the final code, representing the most typical and universal form; and the second is a freestyle CoT devoid of position-constraining guidance.
Secondly, comparing the pass rates of the backbones in the CoT settings, we observe a decline in model performance in all instances, with a more pronounced gap evident in the smaller 3B model.
The final generated code fails due to the generated ambiguous reinterpreted bullet points, and there is a large gap between the code implementation and the problem description.
We rephrase the prompt into several versions to mitigate the model’s randomness in response to different prompt styles.
The result in Table 7 demonstrated that the LCP prompting strategy yields a considerably higher average performance and a lower standard deviation.

While these studies have achieved some success, their effectiveness is highly dependent on the capabilities of advanced Large Language Models (LLMs) such as GPT-4, particularly in terms of API calls, which significantly limits their practical applicability.

Our standard supervised fine-tuning implementation results have an error margin within 1% the Pass@1 result in the greedy search strategy in CodeM-Python (Zan et al., 2023), which indicates that our experiment setting leads to consistent results compared with the existing work.
In contrast, LCP prompting consistently contributes to the enhancement of model performance, demonstrating its stability and effectiveness.
Furthermore, the ablation components also show lower error rates in three types, indicating that MANGO has reduced the code error rate across various degrees of comprehension error.
In the case of WizardCoder-7B, there is a 4.17 percentage points enhancement in the Pass@10 outcome for the MBPP test set.

citacoes.trecho: We quantify four creative sub-components, fluency, flexibility, originality, and elaboration, through various prompting and post-processing techniques.
To this end, we query the target LLM with different Verilog-based prompts, and analyze the responses through various methods of post-processing to calculate the desired metrics, as explained below.
Our prompts contain a brief English description of the module and the module’s declaration, as shown in Listing 1.
As the inference process of LLMs contain variations in the generated responses, we generate t responses for each prompt to estimate the average performance.
The prompts for this metric are constructed for a set of Verilog modules in which a correct solution (the golden response) is included (Listing 2).
// You are a professional hardware designer that writes correct, fully functional Verilog modules.
// Finish writing a different and unique implementation of the provided true_module in the module below, top_module.
To measure an LLM’s capacity for elaboration, the LLM is provided with multiple smaller Verilog modules in a prompt, and tasked with utilizing them to implement a larger, more complex module.
The originality metric is defined as the variance (uniqueness) of an LLM-generated Verilog module in comparison to a typical, fully functional implementation.
Then, the total amount of n prompts with a response less than the threshold is determined, and normalized by the total prompts n.

The prompt dataset utilized for functionality, fluency, and originality consists of 111 single-module HDLBits [41] prompts sourced through AutoChip [42], each containing a correctly implemented solution and testbench.
The smaller prompt set used for elaboration contains 9 separate multi-module prompts from the same source.
The base functionality metric (pass@10) is measured on all 120 prompts.
All responses were trimmed to the first generated instance of “endmodule” for effective functionality evaluation.

The models that struggled (e.g., CodeLlama) produced results that were often direct copies of the provided module, indicating the ability to understand the prompt’s natural language description as an important factor that determined flexibility.
As for originality, the GPT models had slightly worse performance than the others, with CodeLlama performing best.
The models primarily excelled in correctly connecting the input and output parameters between separate modules, while struggling to generate the larger module solution.
Creativity is shown to slightly drop for the larger model sizes of GPT and VeriGen.

tecnicas.observacao: Pacote de prompting de um passo: instrução de papel no sistema («As an debugger, you should refine the buggy program for bug report») → instrucao; exemplo fixo único (bug report e função refinada) → exemplos, que também restringe o formato de saída a uma função refinada completa → restricoes; bug report com código da função defeituosa, documentação/comentários, entradas e saídas esperadas dos testes falhos e mensagens de erro → contexto; 10 amostras por bug validadas por testes e depois manualmente → amostragem. Não há iteração guiada por erros sobre a saída gerada (as mensagens de erro são do programa original, insumo de contexto), por isso não recebe feedback. mecanismos_acrescentados em relação à condição Mask-Hunk (formato de entrada e saída do APR por preenchimento no mesmo arcabouço, Tabela IV): artefatos no lugar do trecho mascarado (contexto) e saída de função completa no lugar do trecho (restricoes); as duas categorias já estavam presentes na base com outro conteúdo. Contrafactual de pacote: Report-Func vs Mask-Hunk no DebugBench (mesmo modelo, 10 amostras), o que não autoriza atribuir o ganho a um único ingrediente. Na comparação com os sistemas da Tabela II (RQ1) os valores dos comparadores foram reaproveitados dos artigos originais, com outro orçamento de amostras e localização perfeita de trechos.

observacoes.descricao: O estudo declara não ter o objetivo de propor o D4C como nova técnica de APR, e sim um novo modo de usar LLMs em APR; o D4C é ainda assim o objeto de investigação.
Pressuposto de localização perfeita em nível de função: a função defeituosa é fornecida e o D4C escolhe as linhas a modificar; no cenário real, uma ferramenta de FL em nível de método a forneceria.

Validação: a função refinada substitui a original, a suíte de testes é executada e os patches plausíveis do Defects4J são conferidos manualmente; no DebugBench o bug report só inclui os exemplos de teste fornecidos, e a correção é verificada pelos testes ocultos do LeetCode.

observacoes.descricao: Artefatos indisponíveis são substituídos por uma frase padrão no bug report (por exemplo, ausência de testes conhecidos); documentos README podem substituir comentários ausentes.

O prompt é implementado como texto único em modelos locais e como mensagens de sistema, usuário e assistente nos modelos da OpenAI; no Mixtral usam-se os tokens [INST] e [/INST].
