citacoes.trecho: In this work, we present EvoCAD, a method for generating computer-aided design (CAD) objects through their symbolic representations using vision language models and evolutionary optimization.
Our method samples multiple CAD objects, which are then optimized using an evolutionary approach with vision language and reasoning language models.
During initialization, a language model LM takes the prompt p and k randomly selected few-shot samples from the CADQuery documentation.
The LM is asked to generate CADQuery code for the object described in p.
If a generated code is not compilable, we apply one attempt of self-debugging following the strategy outlined in [4] by providing the output error message to the LM.
First, a vision-language model VLM is prompted to generate a textual description of each object using chain-of-thought prompting [27].

In the second step, a reasoning language model RLM takes these object descriptions, carefully compares them to the prompt and to each other, and finally ranks the objects from best alignment to the prompt to worst.
In each evaluation, the ranking procedure is performed three times, and the average object rankings are calculated.
During the mating process, we give the LM the CAD codes of the two objects, their respective descriptions, and the prompt.

Provided with this information, we ask the model to analyze similarities, strengths and weaknesses of the respective CAD codes, and to combine them in a complementary way to generate an improved version.
If selected, we provide the offspring’s CAD code and prompt to the LM and request that the model refine and improve the code.
3D-Premise [29] removes the need for user intervention by providing a VLM additional refinement prompts in the loop to correct any discrepancies.
Their method first generates a question catalog about the object using the prompt, in a second step the VLM utilizes these questions for refinement.

Experiments are conducted using GPT-4V [15] as generating LM and visually analyzing VLM, allowing a fair comparison to the prior methods 3D-Premise [29] and CADCodeVerify [1], which are based on the same model.
Performance data for these methods is obtained from [1].
Similar to [1], we set the number of few-shot samples k to 5 for initialization by leveraging a set S of 40 samples from the CADQuery documentation.
Additionally, we chose the number of elites to be one, i.e., we move the object with the highest fitness unmodified to the next generation, ensuring that the current best object does not deteriorate.
To enable a fair quantitative comparison, all metrics depict the average values calculated over the same watertight joint subset, which approximately represents 80% of the full dataset.
For non-watertight objects, neither a closed volume nor a valid χ exists, making the calculation of volume or topology metrics infeasible.
We have frequently observed that objects with incorrect topologies can have better spatial metrics than those with correct topologies.
A current limitation of this work is the relatively small population size and number of optimization generations, because of the growing number of required LLM API calls as these parameters increase.
In some samples, this may lead to unrealized potential due to insufficient exploration and early exploitation.

riscos.descricao: O código gerado pode ter pass@k alto e mesmo assim não impor as pré-condições (contratos) exigidas, aceitando silenciosamente entradas inválidas; com o prompt padrão o CSR é 0% em todos os modelos.
riscos.localizador: Resumo, p. 1; Seção 1, p. 2; Seção 5 e Tabela 2, p. 6

riscos.descricao: Os prompts com contrato reduzem o pass@1 em relação ao padrão (EAS preserva 92% do pass@1 original, segundo o estudo), e o Multi-Turn tende a reduzir o CSR em 2–7 p.p. em relação ao EAS.
O CoT sobre EAS colapsa pass@1 e CSR para 0–4% em Phi-4 e Phi-4-plus; o estudo considera o CoT inadequado quando a saída precisa continuar executável.

Os contratos derivam das asserções de referência, que podem ser incompletas; os CVTs são um conjunto finito de padrões de violação e não cobrem todas as entradas semanticamente inválidas (limitação de validade do benchmark).
Os julgamentos auxiliares por modelo (filtro de alinhamento, LLM-as-judge) podem herdar viés do modelo juiz.

A enumeração SMT e a filtragem de viabilidade acrescentam sobrecarga computacional à construção do benchmark: 126,89 min de inferência do o4-mini, 228,23 min de solver SMT e 1,75 min de filtragem. É custo de construção, não dos prompts de geração. Também se afirma que usar GPT-4o ou Gemini-3-flash como motor teria custo computacional e financeiro maior, sem quantificar.
riscos.localizador: Limitations, p. 10; Apêndices A-B e Tabelas 7-8, p. 11; Apêndice C, p. 12

mitigacoes.descricao: Pipeline SMT para gerar CVTs precisos, comparado com a geração direta pelo o4-mini sem SMT: TS de 72,69% para 84,92% e AVC de 97,58% para 94,11% (Tabela 4).

Filtro de alinhamento contrato–especificação, validado por dois especialistas numa amostra de 100 tarefas (92,00% de concordância) e por GPT-4o e Gemini-3-flash (96,48% e 97,80%); é validação do filtro, sem condição sem ele.

Análise do CSR condicionada à correção funcional, para separar o comportamento de contrato de falhas incidentais.

citacoes.trecho: For our code generation experiments, we evaluate a set of open-source models including gemma-3-12B-it (gemma-3), DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-14B (DeepSeek-R1), Qwen3-14B (Qwen-3), Phi-4-reasoning (Phi-4), and Phi-4-reasoning-plus (Phi-4-plus).
The standard condition uses the reference natural-language query.
Contract specification (CS) uses the contract-aware rewrite from Section 3.1.
A commercial LLM interprets each assertion and rewrites the original query to include the corresponding constraint.
Example-augmented specification (EAS) further appends verified CVTs as concrete examples of inputs that should be rejected.
The negative-example prompt augments the standard prompt with a small set of wrong input–output pairs for the same task.
The contract prompt is our EAS setting: a contract-aware description paired with CVTs.
We consider Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting and a refinement-style multi-turn strategy that first generates a solution with functional logic and then refines the code with contract information.
As a result, generated code may achieve high pass@k scores while failing to enforce the preconditions that the task actually requires.
Table 2 shows that the standard prompt yields 0% CSR for every base LLM despite 75–82% pass@1.
More critically, CoT catastrophically fails on Phi-4 and Phi-4-plus, collapsing both pass@1 and CSR to 0–4%.
This gain is typically accompanied by a modest drop in CSR of 2–7%p, indicating that refinement tends to prioritize preserving functional behavior over implementing every contract check.
ContractEval derives contracts from reference assertions, which may be incomplete with respect to all validity constraints that developers intend.

SMT enumeration and feasibility filtering introduce computational overhead compared to purely LLM-based test generation, and any auxiliary model-based judgments (e.g., contract–specification alignment checks or semantic scoring) may inherit bias from the judge model.
The more informative number is TS, which rises from 72.69% to 84.92% under our pipeline.
Two computer science experts assessed the semantic alignment on a 100-task sample and resolved disagreements by discussion.

Accordingly, we filter synthesized CVTs by executing each input on the reference implementation under two configurations: (i) with assertions removed to verify functional feasibility, and (ii) with assertions intact to confirm the targeted violation.
On average, EAS achieves 50.94%p CSR improvement over the standard prompt and preserves 92% of the original pass@1.
We evaluate GPT-4o and Gemini-3-flash on a 100-task sample drawn from ContractEval under the same three prompting conditions.

citacoes.trecho: We investigate the full spectrum of ICL through five shot configurations: zero-shot (0 examples), few-shot (5 and 25 examples), and many-shot (125 and 625 examples).
For all configurations with demonstrations, the examples were randomly sampled from a disjoint training partition to prevent data leakage.
This random selection serves as a baseline to isolate the effect of quantity, though it may introduce noise compared to curated examples.

Our prompt was deliberately minimal to test the models’ core ICL capabilities, containing only a task instruction, output format guidance, the N in-context examples, and the source code to be translated.
We evaluate three variants from Gemini family: Gemini 1.5 Flash, Gemini 2.0 Flash, and Gemini 2.0 Flash Lite [11, 12].
For each pair, we randomly sampled 200 unique source code snippets from a held-out test partition, leading to 90,000 total translation experiments.
All dynamic tests were conducted within isolated Docker containers to ensure a consistent and reproducible execution environment.
Pass@1 measures the rate of compilation success, while the stricter Success@1 requires a translation to be fully successful (i.e., outcome is "Successful Translation").
Critically, this decline is accompanied by a rise in Functional Errors (FE) and Runtime Errors (RE), which become the dominant failure modes.

The consistent decline in Pass@1 suggests that for the complex task of code translation, naively increasing the quantity of examples introduces noise or conflicting signals that impair the model’s ability to maintain functional correctness.
As shown in Table 4, the prompt lengths and the corresponding API costs grow exponentially as the number of in-context examples increases.

For our best-performing model, Gemini 2.0 Flash, moving from the peak-performance 25-shot configuration to the 625-shot configuration represents a more than 21-fold increase in the estimated cost per translation.
Practically, our results suggest prioritizing the curation of small, high-quality exemplar sets, which is not only more effective but also reduces API costs by 20-30x compared to many-shot prompting.
We hypothesize that "high-quality" examples—idiomatic and semantically related—may mitigate the paradox, whereas our single-pass, random approach exposes the noise sensitivity of current models.
Crucially, despite these baseline performance differences, the many-shot paradox persists across all categories.
The non-monotonic trend in Pass@1 (rightmost plot) is observed across three categories, demonstrating the robustness of the "many-shot paradox."

The paradox is most evident in (c) Pass@1, where functional correctness, measured by compilation success, consistently peaks in the few-shot range (5-25 examples) before significantly degrading for all models as the number of examples increases.
This phenomenon is illustrated in our teaser figure (Figure 1) and detailed with full statistical breakdowns in Table 2.
Estimated prompt lengths (tokens) and API costs (USD) per translation, assuming an average output of 1000 tokens.
The success rate shows the raw count of successful translations over the total number of valid attempts.

O raciocínio em passos é aprendido por ajuste fino (política com reinforced fine-tuning, cabeça de valor treinada, ajuste contínuo com KL), e o artigo não reproduz o prompt de inferência (templates só no GitHub, não acessado); por isso o contraste com Direct Generation (modelo base sem ajuste) confunde prompting, ajuste fino e orçamento de busca (B1=3, B2=4). Os componentes de treino estão em componentes_fora_escopo. Aprendizado em contexto com três demonstrações e delimitadores ⟨step⟩ é usado na expansão do MCTS (coleta de dados), não descrito na inferência.

riscos.descricao: 'Overthinking': o raciocínio CoT pode levar a soluções desnecessariamente complexas e incorretas; no exemplo do DeepSeek-Coder-6.7B-Instruct no MBPP, 4.7% das respostas antes corretas ficaram incorretas com raciocínio.

observacoes.descricao: Sem adaptive CoT, o SEER aplicaria raciocínio a todas as questões; com ele, aplica raciocínio a 65.6% (DeepSeek) e 73.5% (Qwen) das questões do MBPP.

Sem KL no treino contínuo ('Two stage no KL'), o desempenho cai fortemente (LCB: −4.3 com DeepSeek e −13.1 com Qwen, segundo o texto), o que os autores atribuem a esquecimento catastrófico; trata-se de ajuste fino.

O estudo afirma que técnicas de prompting dependem de modelos proprietários grandes e funcionam mal em modelos menores, que não aprenderiam o raciocínio só pelo prompt; essa é a motivação da abordagem por treino.
Os valores dos modelos de referência (proprietários e 15B+) não têm origem declarada (execução própria ou transcrição).
Na Tabela 6 (modelos treinados em Python e avaliados em C++ e Java), SEER melhora 0.76 e 4.41 pontos para DeepSeek e 1.01 e 2.07 para Qwen; o texto não nomeia a métrica.
Experimentos em servidor Ubuntu 20.04 com 4 GPUs NVIDIA Tesla A100 (40GB).

citacoes.trecho: Experimental results demonstrate that SEER outperforms all baseline methods such as DeepSeek-R1-Zero’s reinforcement learning [22] and improves the base model by 4.2%∼9.3%, 1.9%∼9.1%, and 3.5%∼5.3% in terms of pass@1 on three popular coding benchmarks: MBPP [2], HumanEval [9], and LiveCodeBench [28], respectively.

Experiments on state-of-the-art code LLMs DeepSeek-Coder and Qwen2.5-Coder demonstrate that SEER achieves remarkable performance gains across three popular code generation benchmarks, consistently outperforming all baseline methods and achieving absolute improvements by 4.2% ∼ 9.3% in MBPP, 1.9% ∼ 9.1% in HumanEval and 3.5% ∼ 5.3% in LiveCodeBench, respectively.
Following [31] and as illustrated in Figure 1, we use a single implementable sub-task to solve this question as a step and the last step will give the final solution code.
To force the model to generate solutions without reasoning, the response prefix ```{lang} is appended to the end of the prompt, where lang is the target programming language (lines 5–7).
Then, the algorithm leverages the value predictions from the value model Vϕ to rank the steps and directly-generated solution, determining whether to use step-by-step reasoning or not.
During the expansion stage of MCTS, we employ in-context learning and incorporate three demonstrations which are randomly selected from a pool of eight prepared examples.
Self-Planning [31] first leverage LLMs to plan concise solution steps from the intent combined with a few-shot prompt and then generate code step by step, guided by the preceding solution steps.
Code CoT [31] is a prompting method that asks LLMs to describe the implementation code line by line and then write the code.
Reflexion is a framework that iteratively refines code generation through self-reflection and error correction.

We further investigate the importance of the value model-based reasoning quality assessment by removing the validation of intermediate reasoning steps, i.e., changing Vϕ(st+1) in line 14 in Algorithm 1 to 0 and selecting C randomly in line 16.
Finally, we validate the effectiveness of the adaptive CoT reasoning mechanism by disabling direct solution generation in line 7 in Algorithm 1.
Specifically, we propose to leverage the ground truth solutions to refine the reasoning process through self-reflection [39].

For example, as shown in Figure 2 (a), although CoT reasoning improved DeepSeek-Coder-6.7B-Instruct’s performance on MBPP [2] by 7.5%, it also caused 4.7% of previously correct answers to become incorrect (details referring to Section 5.2).

This not only results in performance degradation on problems that could have been straightforwardly solved (e.g. Figure 2 (b) and (c)) but also increases computational costs through higher token consumption.
The initial data construction takes 43 and 47 hours respectively, but this process is performed only once and the data can be reused.
Removing this component increases generation time for these two models by 34.5% and 32.6%.
This process simulates scenarios where the model hallucinates or misinterprets requirements, which is a common occurrence in LLM-generated code [66].
Another threat is potential data contamination.

To address this, we utilize the Self-OSS dataset as our seed data, where the original authors have already performed comprehensive data decontamination and removed benchmark questions with high similarity.
In this work, we select two state-of-the-art pre-trained models Deepseek-Coder and Qwen2.5-Coder for evaluation.
We repeat SEER three times and report its average results to eliminate the influence of sampling and fluctuations in LLM.

tecnicas.observacao: Pacote completo: (1) seletor por instância entre CoT e síntese de programas, baseado em prompt de autoavaliação com dez critérios de confiança (instrucao; o prompt pede 'Explicitly reason through each criterion' → raciocinio; rota CoT → raciocinio; roteamento por confiança autoavaliada → outro); (2) gerador com diretrizes e plano ('You MUST always plan extensively') → instrucao, raciocinio; etapas encadeadas extração de símbolos em JSON → plano → programa `solve(symbols)` → execução → decomposicao; formato obrigatório (JSON em bloco markdown, função chamada `solve`, sem main, retornar e não imprimir, código não trivial) → restricoes; (3) avaliador composto por LLM e interpretador, cujo resumo de problemas e resultado de execução voltam ao gerador por até 30 iterações → feedback; o prompt do gerador apresenta o resumo como produzido 'by another model', papel distinto que interage com o gerador → multiagente. Acrescentados em relação a PoT (comparador de que deriva): raciocinio (rota CoT e planejamento), decomposicao, feedback, multiagente e outro; restricoes pode também ser acréscimo, mas o prompt de PoT não é reproduzido no artigo. Contrafactual: PIPS contra PoT, CoT e CI no mesmo modelo e conjuntos (Tabelas C.2-C.8); 'sim' vale para o pacote e não autoriza atribuir o ganho a um único mecanismo. Pacote híbrido: a decisão do seletor usa um classificador logístico treinado em 20% dos dados (calibração), e a execução é feita por interpretador Python (ver componentes_fora_escopo).

citacoes.trecho: We introduce Per-Instance Program Synthesis (PIPS), a method that generates and refines programs at the instance-level using structural feedback without relying on task-specific guidance or explicit test cases.
To further improve performance, PIPS incorporates a confidence metric that dynamically chooses between direct inference and program synthesis on a per-instance basis.

It then iteratively generates and evaluates programs using feedback based on structural checks (e.g. non-triviality, syntax, type errors), specifically designed to avoid the collapse to trivial solutions and ensure well-formed computation.
To handle unstructured input, PIPS explicitly performs instance-specific symbolic extraction before synthesis, decoupling program search from perceptual inference.

Given the model’s own assessment of its abilities through these probing questions, the final switch decision can either be derived in a fully zero-shot manner, or a held-out calibration set can be used to derive the decision from a learned logistic classifier, enabling the switch to leverage problem solving experience for higher accuracy.
If an issue is detected, E produces structural feedback to aid in fixing the problem.

tecnicas.observacao: Prompt único (Listing 1) que pede um script Python com SymPy como traço de raciocínio. Persona ('You are an expert mathematical reasoner.') e diretrizes numeradas (documentar variáveis, restrições e objetivos; verificar substituindo soluções e checando domínio) → instrucao; raciocínio passo a passo como comentários e etapas intermediárias comentadas → raciocinio; saída restrita a um único bloco de código Python, uso obrigatório de 'import sympy as sp' e resposta final impressa em formato \boxed → restricoes. As etapas intermediárias são comentários dentro de um único script, não subtarefas executadas em etapas (não classificado como decomposicao). mecanismos_acrescentados vazio: o SymCode não deriva de um prompt base identificável e os prompts dos comparadores (CoT, ToT, Decomposition) não são apresentados. Contrafactual: SymCode contra CoT, ToT e Decomposition nos mesmos três modelos e três benchmarks (Tabela 3); 'sim' vale para o pacote. Pacote híbrido: o script gerado é executado em interpretador Python com a biblioteca SymPy (ver componentes_fora_escopo), de modo que o ganho não é efeito isolado do texto do prompt.

tecnicas.observacao: Extensão do prompt SymCode com um 'agentic wrapper': se o script falha (exceção ou AssertionError), mensagem de erro e traceback são anexados ao histórico e o LLM recebe a instrução 'debug the following code based on the provided error message', até execução bem-sucedida ou limite de iterações ('e.g., 2–3 attempts'; limite exato nao_informado) → feedback. O estudo apresenta SymCode+ como formulação própria ('SymCode+ (ours)') em linhas separadas da Tabela 3, por isso é tratada como técnica focal distinta. Contrafactual de ingrediente: SymCode+ contra SymCode (mesmo prompt sem o laço) na Tabela 3 e SymCode+ contra 'No Self-Debug' na Tabela 4 (GPT-5-nano, AIME). Contra CoT, ToT e Decomposition, SymCode+ é comparado como pacote (híbrido, com execução em interpretador).

Falhas do SymCode (GPT-5-nano, AIME): interpretação errada do problema (56.2%), uso incorreto da API (31.3%) e 12.5% de 'Other' (laços infinitos, falhas de verificação). Número de erros categorizados não informado.
A confiabilidade depende da correção do interpretador Python e da biblioteca SymPy, não verificados formalmente, que podem propagar erros raros.

Desempenho depende fortemente da proficiência em código do LLM base; o framework tem dificuldade com raciocínio abstrato (provas de geometria sintética, indução ou contradição, argumentos combinatórios) que resiste à formalização em SymPy.

Nos baselines em prosa (ToT, GPT-5-nano, AIME), parte dos erros 'Other' (24.1%) inclui restrições alucinadas; o Apêndice C mostra resposta justificada por 'apelo à autoridade', descrita como forma de alucinação. Risco atribuído aos comparadores, não ao SymCode.

O laço de self-debugging eleva a média de tokens de saída de 699 (SymCode) para 890 (SymCode+), com sobrecarga maior no Llama 3.2. O estudo trata tokens como custo de inferência e latência; custo monetário não quantificado.
Sensibilidade ao desenho do prompt: o SymCode depende de prompts cuidadosamente estruturados.
Uso indevido para fraude acadêmica (tarefas e testes padronizados); não é segurança de código nem de sistema.

citacoes.trecho: Instead of prompting an LLM to describe its reasoning in prose, SymCode instructs it to construct a verifiable, executable Python script where the code serves as the reasoning trace.
Next, the generated script is executed in a sandboxed Python interpreter, which provides a deterministic pass/fail signal for programmatic verification.

We introduce and formalize SymCode, a prompt-based framework for advanced mathematical reasoning that transforms an LLM into a neurosymbolic reasoner generating self-contained, verifiable Python scripts.

To what extent does reframing mathematical reasoning as verifiable code generation improve a system’s accuracy on complex mathematical problems compared to established prose-based prompting techniques?
You are an expert mathematical reasoner. Your output must be ONLY a single Python code block fenced as ``` python ... ``` with no prose before or after.
2. Add explicit step-by-step reasoning as comments throughout your code
The explicit instruction to use import sympy as sp is critical.
The requirement to define symbols with appropriate assumptions (e.g., ‘sp.symbols(‘x’, positive=True, integer=True)’) forces the model to formalize the problem’s constraints upfront.
The prompt requires the model to insert assert statements into its generated code.

The effectiveness of this verification, however, is contingent on the quality of the assertions generated by the LLM; an absence of failure does not guarantee correctness if the assertions are weak or located in an unexecuted code path.
The captured error message and traceback are then appended to the prompt history, and the LLM is instructed to “debug the following code based on the provided error message.”
This cycle of execution, failure, and correction repeats until the script runs successfully or a preset iteration limit (e.g., 2–3 attempts) is reached.
Chain of Thought (CoT): A standard baseline where the model is prompted to “think step-by-step” to generate a prose-based rationale before giving the final answer (Wei et al., 2022).
Tree of Thoughts (ToT): An advanced baseline where the model explores multiple reasoning paths, evaluating and pruning them to find the most promising solution (Yao et al., 2023).
Decomposition: A baseline where the model is instructed to break the problem into smaller, simpler sub-problems and solve them sequentially (Khot et al., 2023).

Furthermore, our initial exploratory tests confirmed that PAL is of limited utility for the complex problems in our benchmarks, as it is primarily designed for numerical outputs and struggles significantly with problems requiring a final symbolic expression as the answer.
With Llama 3.2 (90B), a less code-optimized model, standard SymCode underperforms ToT on OlympiadBench, but SymCode+ closes this gap, achieving 21.6% accuracy on AIME.
The self-debugging loop in SymCode+ raises the average token count to 890.
In contrast, SymCode shifts failure modes toward the structured stage of problem setup, with most errors due to problem misinterpretation (56.2%) and incorrect API usage (31.3%).

The remaining 24.1% of “Other” errors primarily consist of incomplete solutions, where the model fails to finish the reasoning chain, or hallucinated constraints, where it invents details not present in the problem.

We evaluated three progressively degraded versions of our framework, removing one key feature at each step: the iterative self-debugging loop (No Self-Debug), the use of assertions (No Verification), and the symbolic SymPy library in favor of standard numerical libraries (No SymPy (Numeric Python)).
Its reliability also depends on the correctness of the Python interpreter and SymPy library, which, while mature, are not formally verified and may propagate rare errors.
Finally, SymCode relies on carefully structured prompts, making performance sensitive to prompt design and motivating future work on more robust instruction formats.
Such a tool could be misused to cheat on assignments or standardized tests, undermining the educational process.

Potential mitigation strategies include the development of specialized detectors for AI-generated code and promoting educational policies that focus on assessing the reasoning process rather than just the final answer.
Internal reasoning tokens are observable in the open-source setting; we include them in the token count for all methods under GPT-OSS.

A primeira tentativa do RCI é zero-shot, sem exemplo (p. 6). O contraste executado é RCI × one-shot (Tabela II): as duas condições diferem em mais de um ingrediente (o RCI não tem o exemplo resolvido do one-shot e acrescenta o laço de feedback), de modo que o ganho é do pacote e não pode ser atribuído só ao feedback. O contraste com a tentativa zero-shot inicial (p. 6) é por rodada, dentro das mesmas execuções do RCI (contribuição cumulativa das rodadas de feedback), e não uma condição executada separadamente. citacoes.trecho: In this work, we critically evaluate five state-of-the-art open-source LLMs, spanning 3B to 8B parameter sizes, on the EMR task for Python code.

We systematically assess functional correctness and code quality using automated metrics and investigate the impact of prompting strategies by comparing one-shot prompting to a Recursive criticism and improvement (RCI) approach.
You are an expert Python software engineer.

citacoes.trecho: One-Shot Prompting: A single EMR example is provided to guide the model's transformation, minimizing complexity and inference time.
If incorrect, targeted feedback based on test case errors is added to the prompt, and the model tries again.
By design, initial attempt of RCI is a zero-shot attempt, the model is given only the task specification and target code (no examples, no test-failure feedback).
Models were instructed to output only executable code, avoid explanations, and limit changes to the EMR.
TPP serves as the primary metric for comparing models and prompt strategies head-to-head.
We computed TPP for every model and both prompting strategies (one-shot and RCI) across all 840 code samples.
One-shot logs the failure, while the RCI appends test feedback to the conversation and retries, up to two attempts.
This process can repeat up to three times, simulating iterative improvement.
Candidates passing test cases are then analyzed using metrics like CC and LOC.
Importantly, even with this simple capped budget, RCI delivered >10 percentage point improvements in TPP, showing robustness across models.

We observed that most improvements occurred early: for instance, Qwen2.5-Coder and DeepSeek-Coder, successfully refactored about 64% and 67% of cases, respectively, in the first iteration, with a further 25% and 30% corrected after the second.

Zero-shot results were consistently lower than both one-shot and RCI conditions, TPP = 0.472 for CodeQwen-1.5, 0.686 for Qwen2.5-Coder, 0.706 for DeepSeek-Coder, 0.334 for Llama-3.2, and 0.427 for Phi-4.

Interestingly, Llama3.2-Oneshot and Phi-4-RCI report the lowest CC values (2.87 and 3.28), but as with LOC, these models also produce many incomplete or incorrect outputs, as indicated by their low TPP.
The best-performing approaches: Qwen2.5-Coder-RCI (5.58) and DeepSeek-Coder-RCI (6.19) achieve more than a 50% reduction in LOC compared to the original code.
This is due to incomplete or trivial code generations that may be short, but do not produce functionally correct solutions.
This detailed view shows that specific problems, such as p02684, p02685, and p02686, are complex for all models: even the highest-performing models fail to achieve a 50% pass rate on these tasks.
Gains were largest for high-performing models.
Across all models, RCI-based prompting consistently outperformed one-shot prompting, with average TPP improvements of 8–14 percentage points depending on the model.
RCI-based prompting consistently outperforms one-shot prompting in test pass rates and refactoring quality.
A developer survey on RCI-generated refactorings shows over 70% acceptance, with Qwen2.5-Coder rated highest across all evaluation criteria.
Prompting Strategies: Comparison of one-shot vs. RCI, showing RCI significantly boosts refactoring success.

citacoes.trecho: To assess the consistency of human judgments, we computed the quadratic-weighted Cohen's κ across all rater pairs, obtaining an average κ ≈ 0.30, with individual values ranging from 0.17 to 0.52 depending on the survey statement.
To keep the survey manageable and avoid participant fatigue, each developer reviewed 20 code samples covering five distinct problems.
For every sample, developers rated the original code and three RCI-refactored versions.
From the full set of Python problems (800), we filtered for those that: (a) have a CC of three and sufficient length for EMR.
While traditional metrics like CC and LOC provide useful signals, they often diverge from human judgments, emphasizing the need for human-in-the-loop evaluation.
The RCI prompting approach uses automated test failures as feedback for language models, but this may overlook nuanced or contextual guidance.

[16]: o prompt de cada rodada traz a tarefa original, um buffer com todas as tentativas anteriores e os resultados do ICD (CWE sinalizadas e dicas curtas) e a instrução de revisar a tentativa mais recente, identificar práticas inseguras e corrigir preservando a funcionalidade → instrucao (herdada da tarefa e acrescida das diretrizes de revisão); retorno do analisador estático ICD a cada rodada → feedback; 'Prefer minimal, targeted changes and safer APIs' e 'Return only the updated code' → restricoes. Três rodadas (t1, t2, t3) sobre a geração zero-shot t0. Contrafactual: cada rodada comparada com a linha de base zero-shot t0 no mesmo modelo e no mesmo benchmark (Tabela III); 'sim' vale para o pacote (feedback do ICD + diretrizes + restrições + gerações adicionais) e não autoriza atribuir o ganho a um único ingrediente. Não há condição com o mesmo número de gerações sem o feedback do ICD. As rodadas t1→t2→t3 são contribuição cumulativa da mesma técnica, não técnicas distintas. O ICD é ferramenta de análise estática que alimenta o prompt (mecanismo de feedback), não intervenção fora do escopo; o mesmo ICD é usado na avaliação.

citacoes.trecho: We evaluate secure code generation using the Instruct Prime, which eliminated compliance-required prompts and cue contamination, and evaluate five instruction-tuned code LLMs using a zero-shot baseline and a three-round reflexion prompting approach.
Our findings show that insecurity remains common at the first round: roughly 25–33% of programs are insecure at a zero-shot baseline (t0).
The prompt specifies the target language and the task, and then leaves all design choices to the model.
In our setting, the model receives feedback in the form of CWE-aligned vulnerability returned by the ICD detector.

In each round, the prompt includes (i) the original task, (ii) a reflection buffer containing all prior attempts and their ICD results (flagged CWE(s)), and (iii) an instruction to focus on the most recent attempt while still considering earlier failures.
Prefer minimal, targeted changes and safer APIs when available.

citacoes.trecho: Second, evaluations usually emphasize first-pass success rates while overlooking regressions (e.g., a revised output reintroduces a vulnerability or introduce a new one).
Overall, one or two reflexion rounds capture most of the improvement, while additional iterations provide diminishing returns and occasionally undo earlier repairs.
We also experimented with different prompting techniques (e.g., chain-of-thought), but they did not result in any significant improvement over the zero-shot baseline.
While static analysis enables scalable, rule-based assessment, it can miss contextual cues or produce false positives.
Misclassifications at this stage could introduce unintended bias.
To mitigate this risk, we conducted manual reviews of LLM generations and adhered to validated post-processing established in prior work [28], [29].
While the dataset corrects for known cue contamination, the prompt distribution remains imbalanced.

Finally, similar to [2], [19], we enforced a simple fairness rule: only outputs classified as Complete Code were evaluated by ICD as usual; anything else (Incomplete, Natural Language, or Mixed) was marked insecure.
To ensure consistency, we fixed decoding hyperparameters across all models and reflexion rounds.
For inference, we use each model’s default Hugging Face configuration to preserve its intended decoding behavior such as temperature, top-p and other generation settings to keep comparisons fair.
OpenCoder lags across all categories.
Languages like Java, JavaScript, PHP, and C++ fall in the middle, with 20-35% of outputs remaining insecure.

Overall, these results indicate that the reflexion loop effectively assists in vulnerability repair, reducing ICD-detected security issues without adding instability or fluctuations to the model outcomes.
We report these metrics overall and for each model, and we further stratify by language and CWE family to show where models improve or degrade.
This worked reliably for four languages (C, C++, Python, and JavaScript), but failed consistently for the remaining ones (Java, Rust, PHP, and C#) due to missing build tools or dependencies.

citacoes.trecho: Inspired by this finding, we propose two multi-round simplification methods and generate them via GPT-4o: rule-based simplification (MRS-Rule) and jointly rule-based LLM simplification (MRS-Joint).
Additionally, we explore the potential of automatic code generation for text simplification, although further refinement remains necessary.
For the datasets, we use the same trial (40 examples) and test (200 examples) data sets provided by the TSAR workshop to build and evaluate our methods.
We use GPT-4o to generate the code first (denoted as Baseline or "Program 1"), which will call the OpenAI APIs (GPT-4o-mini) with the following prompt from (Barayan et al., 2025).

citacoes.trecho: The Prompt-only baseline model (§3) preserves the original meaning best (highest MeaningBERT-Orig) but shows the weakest control of CEFR level (highest RMSE).

After the evaluation, we found that simply merging two methods into MRS-Joint (§4.2) is more efficient, which is the most accurate model to match the target CEFR level (the best RMSE) while still maintaining the meaning.
It shows that our multi-round rules significantly improve the performance with a little sacrifice on the meaning preservation.
As shown in Table 3, the program excels in simplifying complex sentences C1-C2 to the B1 level.
This highlights that incomplete outputs can seem easier to cheat the CEFR predictor as the intended CEFR level.

These examples reveal three failure modes – overshoot, and undergeneration – demonstrating that successful CEFR simplification requires not only simpler words but also balanced control of meaning, style, and completeness.
The models we used are closed-source models such as using GPT-4o for code generation while using GPT-4o-mini for API, which are not explicitly finetuned in the text simplification datasets by us.
Our work is also limited to one dataset and one language (English), and two types of GPT-4o generated model.
Furthermore, focusing on coding generation, we could also extend the study to self-evolve algorithm discovery (Novikov et al., 2025) and compare it with other prompts and more coding agents.
Our submitted systems ranked 7 out of 20 teams.

citacoes.trecho: A diverse set of 13 leading proprietary and open-source models, generating Python solutions based on a one-shot prompt, was evaluated via the dedicated Eolymp environment against hidden tests, ensuring code correctness.
Each prompt contained one Ukrainian example plus a short correct solution to guide the model on the expected input and output formats.
For every task, the model produced a single solution without retries under a 30-minute timeout, using recommended sampling parameters with low temperature (0-0.2).
The programming language was set to Python 3 for solution generation.
Two primary metrics were used: pass@1 (accepted if 100% of hidden tests pass) and average score (0 to 100).
During evaluation, it was discovered that out of 500 problems, 14 (1 hard, 13 very hard) failed due to grader issues and were removed.
However, even the best system leaves 242 tasks unsolved.
About half of all problems (mainly hard/very hard) remain unsolved by any model.
The big problem with static benchmarks is that models may have been inadvertently trained on solutions widely available online.

The limitations of this research include the narrowness of the benchmark, with only one programming language being tested (Python), and a single source of problem tasks (the E-olymp platform), without an in-depth analysis of data contamination.

tecnicas.nome_original: Test-Driven Feedback-Guided Framework (instruction prompting + test-case-aware translation + QLoRA fine-tuning + feedback-guided inference)
tecnicas.localizador: Resumo e contribuições, p. 1; Seção 4 e Figura 1, p. 2-3; Seções 6.1-6.4 e Tabelas 2-4, p. 3-4; Seção 7, p. 4
tecnicas.observacao: Pacote híbrido: inclui ajuste fino QLoRA (fora do escopo) além de componentes de prompting. O estudo adiciona os componentes em sequência no Qwen2.5-Coder-14B (few-shot em bengali 0.74, Tabela 2 → few-shot com instruções traduzidas 0.81, Tabela 3 → QLoRA 0.90 → QLoRA + feedback 0.94, Tabela 4) e não relata, numa mesma tabela, o sistema completo contra a condição sem ele; a frase do texto que o compara com 'the few-shot baseline' não identifica qual das duas linhas few-shot é usada (ver heterogeneidade). Por isso classificado como contribuição por fase ('cumulativo'). Mecanismos do pacote: papel e regras ('You are an expert Python programmer', 'CRITICAL RULES', orientações de depuração) → instrucao; formato obrigatório (bloco ```python```, nome exato da função, tipo de retorno) e casos de teste no prompt como especificação → restricoes; encadeamento tradução → geração → execução → nova geração → decomposicao; reexecução com o traço de erro → feedback. O artigo não informa se o prompt de geração do modelo ajustado mantém os dois exemplos resolvidos do prompt few-shot; por isso exemplos e contexto não foram atribuídos ao pacote (nao_informado).

tecnicas.localizador: Seção 4.1, p. 2; Seção 6.1 e Tabela 2, p. 3; Apêndice B.2 (Listing 1), p. 6-7
tecnicas.observacao: Prompt base usado na comparação entre modelos: mensagem de sistema com papel e 'CRITICAL RULES' → instrucao; dois exemplos resolvidos (tarefa em bengali, casos de teste e solução esperada) → exemplos e, como código fornecido como demonstração (regra D102 do dicionário), também contexto; formato e nome exato da função, casos de teste da tarefa-alvo → restricoes. Não há condição sem exemplos (zero-shot) nem outra variação do prompt; o contraste entre modelos é seleção de modelo, fora do escopo.

tecnicas.nome_original: Instruction Translation Strategy (LLM-based, test-case-aware translation; Few-shot on Translated Instructions)
tecnicas.localizador: Seção 4.2, p. 2; Seção 6.2 e Tabelas 2-3, p. 3; Apêndice B.1 e B.3 (Listing 2), p. 6-8
tecnicas.observacao: Passo de prompting que pede ao Qwen2.5-Coder-14B a tradução de cada instrução bengali para inglês, com a suíte de testes no prompt e diretrizes de tradução com um exemplo; a instrução traduzida entra no prompt two-shot, cujos exemplos também passam a ter tarefas em inglês (Listing 2 versus Listing 1). O encadeamento tradução → geração é a categoria acrescentada (decomposicao); instrucao, exemplos, contexto e restricoes já estão no prompt base (o prompt de tradução também tem papel, diretrizes e um exemplo, categorias já presentes). Contrafactual: Tabela 2 (instruções em bengali) versus Tabela 3 (instruções traduzidas), mesmos seis modelos, mesmo two-shot, antes do ajuste fino; o estudo analisa o contraste no texto da Seção 6.2. O ingrediente isolado é o pacote 'tradução + exemplos em inglês'; a contribuição da suíte de testes no prompt do tradutor não é isolada. Componente do sistema proposto (contribuições, p. 1), não proposta autônoma.

tecnicas.localizador: Seção 4.4, p. 3; Seção 6.4 e Tabela 4, p. 4; Apêndice B.4 (Listing 3), p. 8
tecnicas.observacao: Após a geração, o código é executado contra os casos de teste fornecidos (timeout de 30 s); em caso de falha, o modelo é reinstruído com tipo de erro, mensagem, caso de teste que falhou, orientação específica por tipo de erro, análise das tentativas anteriores e uma 'SYSTEMATIC DEBUGGING APPROACH', até três vezes → feedback (acrescentado); as orientações e 'CRITICAL SUCCESS FACTORS' caem em instrucao e restricoes, categorias já presentes na condição base. Os passos de depuração ('ANALYZE INPUT/OUTPUT', 'Step through the failing test case manually') são diretrizes, sem pedido de explicação antes do código; não foram classificados como raciocinio. decomposicao é herdada do encadeamento com a tradução. Contrafactual: QLoRA versus QLoRA + Feedback mechanism (Tabela 4), mesmo modelo ajustado. O ingrediente também inclui o aumento da temperatura de amostragem a cada tentativa (0.1 → 0.3 → 0.5), intervenção de decodificação fora do escopo, de modo que o ganho não é efeito isolado do texto do prompt. O prompt de erro foi refinado iterativamente em execuções no conjunto de desenvolvimento. Componente do sistema proposto.

Limites da autocorreção na inferência: falhas por tradução errada ou lacunas de raciocínio raramente foram resolvidas, e quando os tracebacks não identificavam o problema as novas tentativas raramente levaram a correções.

citacoes.trecho: In this work, we propose a method that combines instruction prompting with a test-driven, feedback-guided iterative refinement process using a fine-tuned Qwen2.5-14B model.
The model generates code from Bangla instructions, tests it against unit tests, and iteratively refines any failing outputs through three evaluation passes, using test feedback to guide each step.

Proposed a lightweight and effective system for Bangla-to-Python code generation that combines QLoRA fine-tuning with a feedback-guided inference loop and includes a test-case-aware translation step to ensure semantic alignment with expected input-output behavior.
Each model was tested in a two-shot setting, where we prompted with two Bangla instructions and their reference solutions.
To evaluate robustness, we repeated the same experiments using translated English instructions.
Since the development dataset contained Bangla instructions paired with English test cases, we introduced an LLM-based translation step to better leverage English-centric code models.
For each instruction, the full test suite was included in the prompt, allowing the translator to align the natural language description with the intended input/output behavior.
We used Qwen2.5-Coder-14B as the translator for the full dataset.
Organizers provided instruction-to-Python code datasets for training (74 samples), development (400 samples), and testing (500 samples).
For fine-tuning, we additionally used the DeepMind MBPP dataset (Austin et al., 2021) to supplement our training data.
After the model generated a candidate solution, we executed it against all the test cases provided with a 30-second timeout.
If any test failed, we re-prompted the model with the error trace, allowing it to iteratively refine its output.
This loop was repeated up to three times, gradually increasing the sampling temperature (0.1 → 0.3 → 0.5) to encourage diverse candidate solutions.
We found prompt design to be crucial here, and iteratively refined the error-handling prompt over multiple development runs.
Unless otherwise stated, decoding was performed with a maximum of 768 tokens and an initial temperature of 0.1.
System performance was measured using the Pass@1 metric, defined as the proportion of top-1 generated solutions that pass all hidden unit tests.
Table 3 shows that translation substantially boosted performance for most models, with Qwen2.5-Coder-14B again leading at 0.81 Pass@1.
Fine-tuning Qwen2.5-Coder-14B with QLoRA yielded a notable improvement, raising Pass@1 from 0.81 to 0.90.
Relative to the few-shot baseline, this represents a +16.05% absolute improvement, and a +4.44% gain over fine-tuning alone.
However, failures caused by mistranslations or deeper reasoning gaps were rarely resolved, underscoring the limits of inference-time self-correction.
Although the LLM-based translation pipeline preserved semantics in most cases, some instructions suffered from semantic drift.
This caused the generated code to implement incorrect logic.
These components enabled the model to achieve Pass@1 accuracies of 0.94 on the development set and 0.934 on the blind test set.
These errors affected code generation and were only partially addressed by the feedback mechanism.
The feedback-guided inference loop depended on the quality of error traces.
When tracebacks did not identify issues, retries seldom led to meaningful corrections.
Hardware constraints restricted us to QLoRA fine-tuning on a single GPU, which prevented exploration of full-precision LoRA or larger models that could offer additional improvements.

tecnicas.localizador: Resumo, p. 1; Seção II, p. 3 (Figura 2); Seção III, p. 4; Tabela I e Seção IV, p. 5
tecnicas.observacao: Pacote de prompt construído pelo sistema: regras do dialeto Mitsubishi em linguagem natural (instrucao); restrições rígidas do fornecedor (proibição de palavras reservadas, declaração antes do uso, vocabulário de tipos restrito, estrutura de POU) → restricoes; contexto recuperado de três segmentos da base (definições de function blocks, trechos de especificação, contexto auxiliar com exemplos de usuários) → contexto; programa canônico de exemplo, templates de POU/referência a dispositivos e 'examples of incorrect label usage' → exemplos (os exemplos recuperados da base também → exemplos); reparo guiado pelo diagnóstico do compilador GX Works3 (até 3 tentativas de compilação) → feedback. A mesma técnica é aplicada a quatro backbones na Tabela I (GPT-4.1, GPT-5, DeepSeek Coder v2 Lite ajustado e modelo local não ajustado); são condições da mesma técnica, não técnicas distintas. Contrafactual: cada configuração RAG contra a configuração 'Standard' do mesmo modelo (GPT-4.1 Standard = 'minimal prompt, no retrieval'). 'sim' vale para o pacote (recuperação + prompt abrangente com restrições, templates e exemplo canônico); não há ablação que separe recuperação, restrições, templates ou exemplo canônico, nem condição sem o reparo. Mecanismos acrescentados atribuídos em relação ao prompt mínimo do Standard, que não é mostrado; o feedback consta nas duas condições porque a Tabela I informa 'Repaired' também para as configurações Standard (ver heterogeneidade). Na versão local com RAG o prompt de sistema foi encurtado. Uso da expansão opcional de consulta na avaliação: nao_informado. O ajuste fino do modelo local é intervenção fora do escopo (componentes_fora_escopo); nas linhas Local Fine-tuned o contraste RAG vs. Standard mantém o mesmo modelo ajustado.

tecnicas.observacao: A saída do último ciclo de compilação no GX Works3 é inserida literalmente numa instrução estruturada de reparo que orienta o modelo a tratar categorias de diagnóstico (variáveis não declaradas, palavras reservadas, tipos incompatíveis, instruções proibidas) preservando os segmentos validados; termina em sucesso, timeout do servidor ou esgotamento do orçamento (máximo de 3 tentativas). A coluna 'Repaired' da Tabela I e a frase 'of the 73% compiled code attempts, 50% did not need a repair, but 23% did need up to two repairs' dão só a contribuição da fase de reparo, sem condição executada sem o laço.

citacoes.trecho: We found that a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) supported coding assistant can work in low-data domains by using extensive prompt engineering and directed retrieval.
Our tool lets several AI models compete with each other, uses reasoning, corrects bugs automatically and checks code validity by compiling it directly in the chat interface.
We support our approach with an extensive evaluation that comes with code compilation statistics and user ratings.
Moreover, companies like Mitsubishi Electric and their customers do not trust cloud providers.

Prompt construction enforces vendor-specific hard constraints: reserved-word prohibition, declaration-before-use mandates, restricted datatype vocabulary aligned with GXWorks3 semantics, and explicit POU structure templates.
Retrieved context from the knowledge base is concatenated with a canonical example program encoding compliant timer usage, state-machine logic, and edge-detection idioms.

The system supports three model configurations executed concurrently on initial queries: (1) Azure RAG (GPT-4.1 with full retrieval), (2) Azure Standard (GPT-4.1, minimal prompt, no retrieval), and (3) Local RAG (fine-tuned quantized model with retrieval).
Follow-up turns use a single user-selected model to preserve conversational coherence.
For Azure RAG responses, the system performs bounded iterative repair (maximum 3 compilation attempts).

Failures trigger targeted correction prompts addressing specific diagnostic categories—undeclared variables, reserved-word violations, type mismatches, disallowed instructions—while preserving validated segments.
Given industrial requirements for low latency, we opted for a comprehensive single-prompt architecture rather than multi-agent orchestration.

The prompt embeds critical Mitsubishi Electric rules: reserved word blacklists, VAR block semantics (e.g., VAR_INPUT available for FUNCTION), examples of incorrect label usage, and mandates that declared function blocks must be instantiated and invoked.
The prompt explicitly instructs models to assume label pre-registration and provides templates demonstrating compliant device referencing patterns.

Rather than implementing complex pattern-based diagnostic parsing, we adopted a prompt-guided approach: compiler feedback is extracted verbatim from the last compilation attempt and embedded into a structured repair instruction that directs the model to address common diagnostic categories (undeclared variables, reserved-word violations, type mismatches, disallowed instructions) while preserving validated code segments.
However, to provide a structured and empirical evaluation, we generated 100 varied queries that were used to generate 100 ST programs with each model composition.
We got access to GPT-5 after finishing the project, but we also included it in our evaluation experiments (using reasoning set to low).
As can be seen, the local fine-tuned RAG model performed best (DeepSeek Coder v2 Lite Instruct).
The second best is the fine-tuned local model without RAG that achieved a 73% compile rate compared to 86% for the RAG.
The RAG version took much longer to generate code and we had to shorten the system prompt to achieve reasonable answer times (< 1 min).
Not all code that was compiled was reasonable, though.
The smaller model often did not produce coherent logic, generated shorter programs and applied functions incorrectly.
From Tab.I can be derived for sure that the fine-tuning and RAG approaches perform well, since standard models do not know Mitsubishi Electric ST style specifics.
Those generations that set up a function block or function but did not make use of it were regarded as failed attempt (not compiled).
The number of repaired attempts shows that, e.g., of the 73% compiled code attempts, 50% did not need a repair, but 23% did need up to two repairs.

citacoes.trecho: Retrieval-augmented approaches substantially outperform non-RAG baselines.
Limitations include said Mitsubishi Electric-only scope, task coverage and "specialist" local model behavior with occasional misinterpretation.
Human evaluation from a single organizational context may limit generalizability; longitudinal deployment studies are needed to assess adoption barriers and real-world productivity impacts.
The local model limits the available context and thus shortens the system prompt and synthetic training data may have downsides not yet visible.
We acknowledge that compilation success is a necessary but not sufficient criterion for code quality.
Faulty control logic could lead to equipment damage, production downtime, or safety hazards for personnel.
All generated code must undergo a mandatory review by qualified automation engineers before deployment or simulation testing in vendor-provided environments.

tecnicas.localizador: p. 2 do PDF, seção 4.2 e Figura 2; p. 4, Tabela 2, colunas Translated/Google e Translated/NLLB
tecnicas.observacao: Mecanismo 'outro': tradução prévia da instrução do bengali para o inglês por tradutor automático externo (Google Translate ou NLLB-200), sem outra mudança no prompt. Os dois tradutores são variantes da mesma técnica, avaliadas em colunas separadas; não são formulações de prompt próprias dos autores, por isso foram registradas como uma técnica, com extração por cobertura na primeira coluna (Google). Classificada como focal porque é uma das cinco abordagens experimentadas, comparada na RQ3, e a Figura 6 a inclui entre 'our approaches'. Contrafactual: mesma condição Vanilla, só com a instrução traduzida.

tecnicas.localizador: p. 3 do PDF, seção 4.3, item 1 e Figura 3; p. 4, Tabela 2, coluna Test-Driven Development/Generated
tecnicas.observacao: Uma chamada ao LLM gera até cinco casos de teste a partir do prompt; os testes e o prompt alimentam a chamada de geração final (etapas encadeadas → decomposicao; testes como especificação → restricoes). Os casos de teste também poderiam ser lidos como exemplos de entrada e saída; adotou-se restricoes de modo uniforme para todas as condições com testes no prompt. Comparada com Vanilla como pacote (geração de testes + inclusão no prompt).

tecnicas.observacao: Teste público do conjunto mais cinco testes gerados pelo LLM, todos usados na geração da resposta. Em relação a Vanilla é pacote; em relação a TDD Given difere apenas nos testes gerados (contraste disponível na Tabela 2, não analisado separadamente pelo estudo).

tecnicas.localizador: p. 3 do PDF, seção 4.4 e Figura 4 (caminho Vanilla); p. 4, Tabela 2, coluna Code Interpreter/Vanilla
tecnicas.observacao: O código gerado é compilado e executado no AWS Code Interpreter; a mensagem de erro é usada como entrada adicional na geração seguinte, com limite de cinco novas tentativas. Difere de Vanilla só pelo laço de feedback de execução. Classificada como focal por ser uma das cinco abordagens com seção própria (4.4) e coluna própria; também é parte do pacote CI+TDD.

tecnicas.localizador: p. 3 do PDF, seção 4.5 e Figura 4 (caminho With Given Test); p. 4, Tabela 2, coluna Code Interpreter/Given Test
tecnicas.observacao: Proposta principal do estudo: teste público no prompt (TDD Given) combinado com o laço do Code Interpreter, no qual o teste também é executado. Comparada com Vanilla como pacote; a Tabela 2 também permite os contrastes com CI (difere só pelo teste) e com TDD Given (difere só pelo laço de execução), não analisados separadamente pelo estudo. O ganho do pacote não é atribuído a um ingrediente isolado. Na Tabela 2 a condição aparece sob o cabeçalho 'Code Interpreter / Given Test'; a correspondência com 'CI + TDD' é confirmada pelo rótulo da última coluna da Figura 5 (p. 3) e pelos valores.

citacoes.trecho: We introduce a novel approach that combines Test-Driven Development (TDD) and Code Interpreter (CI), utilizing open-weight models, which improves the baseline accuracy for code generation with Bengali prompts and achieves an overall accuracy of 85%.
The primary aim of this task was to generate Python code from Bengali instructions using LLM (Raihan et al., 2025a,c,b).
Only one test case was publicly available during the competition.
The rest were hidden and could only be accessed after the submission phase had ended.
To establish baseline accuracy with the Bengali instruction, we conducted this experiment with plain (vanilla) LLM API to determine how different LLMs perform.
Since the primary language for most LLMs is English, our initial intuition was to translate the Bengali instructions into English.

Generated Tests - We started with an API call to an LLM to generate up to five test cases from the given prompt. We then input these test cases, along with the given prompt, to generate our final response.
Given Test - We injected only the publicly available assert statement (test case) from the dataset into the LLM prompt during code generation.
Here, we used the given test case from the dataset, along with five more LLM-generated test cases.
We also set a retry limit of five to fix the generated Python code that did not compile.
The error message received from the earlier execution was used as additional input for subsequent code generation.
We combined the TDD approach with the dataset provided single test case with the CI.
This test case was also executed in the interpreter to verify its success.
Instead, it harmed the overall accuracy compared to the non-translation approach.
Both TDD and CI reduce compilation errors, whereas Bengali to English machine translation increases the error count in most cases.
citacoes.localizador: p. 5 do PDF, quadro de destaque da RQ4

citacoes.trecho: Our study is limited in context, as we only checked a subset of open-weight models available on the AWS Bedrock API.
Moreover, we did not explore how our approach would perform in larger and complex coding tasks, as opposed to the single method-based problems provided in the shared-task dataset.
The CI+TDD approach improved the accuracy across all models by +57% to +450%.
The TDD approach improves the baseline by +47% to +420%.
Comparing the best outcome for each variant, we observed that 3B could reach 67% of the performance of 90B and 87% of the performance of 11B.
It should be noted that both TDD and CI+TDD performed significantly better than baseline in all models.
The CI+TDD methodology was the most effective, increasing overall baseline accuracy by up to 450% and virtually eliminating compilation errors across all models tested.

citacoes.trecho: This paper addresses the challenge of Bangla-to-Python code generation by introducing BanglaCodeAct, an agent-based framework that leverages multi-agent prompting and iterative self-correction.

Unlike prior approaches that rely on task-specific fine-tuning, BanglaCodeAct employs an open-source multilingual LLM within a Thought–Code–Observation loop, enabling the system to dynamically generate, test, and refine code from Bangla instructions.

First, Zero-Shot Prompting serves as a direct baseline where the model is given only the system prompt and the user task (Bangla instruction plus test cases) and is asked to generate the solution in a single turn.
Next, Few-Shot Prompting provides the model with a small number of solved examples in the prompt to help it generalize to new problems.

The Self-Consistency method leverages Qwen/Qwen3-8B to generate multiple independent solutions for the same problem and selects the final answer through majority voting, without using any iterative feedback loop.
This agent employs an iterative Thought-Code-Observation loop, allowing it to self-correct based on execution feedback until all test cases are satisfied.
Thought: The agent generates an internal monologue, outlining its understanding and plan for the task in <thought>, showcasing reasoning in Bangla before code generation.
Errors, like TypeError, provide feedback for iterative self-correction, refining the solution until valid or a max iteration is reached, with the result in <answer>.
To enhance reliability, we implement a retry handler (safe_run) that re-initiates the reasoning process if the agent produces an invalid or empty response.
The retry mechanism permits a user-defined number of task attempts, improving success rates by reducing sporadic failures.

This approach achieves varying results across models: Qwen/Qwen3-8B obtains 36%, Qwen-Coder-7B reaches 51%, TigerLLM-1B-it (Raihan et al., 2025b) it achieves 11%, and Llama-3.1-8B performs the best at 77%.
Primary failure cases occur with semantically ambiguous or complex instructions, where the agent may not converge within 10 iterations.
Moreover, the system relies on high-quality test cases for feedback, which may not always be available in real-world scenarios.
The Qwen3-8B model outperforms specialized models like Qwen2.5-Coder-7B, highlighting the importance of multilingual reasoning over code-specific training.
The primary metric for our evaluation is pass@1 on the HumanEval benchmark (Raihan et al., 2025a).

citacoes.trecho: Zero-Shot CoT elicits spontaneous reasoning by appending “Let’s think step by step” to problem descriptions, encouraging the model to produce reasoning chains before code without requiring exemplars.
Zero-Shot serves as the baseline, generating code directly from problem descriptions without intermediate reasoning steps.
Self-Planning uses GPT-5-Mini with 3-shot in-context learning to generate hierarchical reasoning.
Given exemplars demonstrating task decomposition, the model first breaks problems into subtasks, outlines their execution order, then generates code following the plan.
SCoT (Structured CoT) also employs GPT-5-Mini with 3-shot in-context learning, but constrains reasoning within predefined template slots (e.g., sequence/branch/loop structures).
Reasoning-CoT leverages DeepSeek-R1, an open-source reasoning-oriented model trained with reinforcement learning.
Without requiring exemplars, DeepSeek-R1 generates long-form reflective reasoning chains featuring explicit problem decomposition, multiple solution explorations, and self-correction mechanisms.

Using structured CoT as a controlled framework, we compare high-quality reasoning (SCoT generated by GPT-5-Mini via 3-shot ICL) against lightweight reasoning (MSCoT produced by a fine-tuned 7B model) as prompts for downstream code generation across six models and 12 languages.

Both MSCoT and SCoT follow identical template structures (problem analysis → algorithm design → edge case handling → implementation), differing only in generation quality and token length (MSCoT: 150 tokens average, SCoT: 380 tokens average).
Naive Zero-Shot CoT often degrades performance due to reasoning hallucinations.

This indicates that unguided self-generated reasoning often degrades performance, likely due to reasoning hallucinations where models produce logically coherent but functionally incorrect intermediate steps.

This indicates that low-quality structured reasoning can harm performance by introducing spurious constraints that mislead generation, validating our information-theoretic prediction that poorly-formed C may increase H(Y|X,C) rather than reduce it.
While Reasoning-CoT ranks first in 18/36 model-dataset combinations, its 10× higher token cost makes it impractical for deployment scenarios with budget constraints.
Reasoning-CoT consumes 2,000–7,000 tokens per problem, compared to 200–700 tokens for Self-Planning and SCoT.
Implementation issues (e.g., evaluation scripts, execution environment, decoding hyperparameters) and benchmark contamination could bias absolute Pass@1 scores.
We reuse or closely follow public evaluation pipelines where available, perform sanity checks on sampled tasks, and keep decoding settings consistent across paradigms within each model.
Since we do not control model pre-training corpora, we focus our conclusions on relative differences between CoT paradigms under the same model, which are less sensitive to potential data leakage.

These metrics do not capture aspects such as readability, security, or runtime performance, and our information-theoretic analysis (via I(Y;C|X)) is conceptual rather than based on exact mutual information estimation.
Manual inspection of all 174 asymmetric cases reveals three dominant error patterns (Table 8):

With 164 problems per language (1,968 total), it enables systematic evaluation of CoT effectiveness across statically typed languages (Java, C++, C#, TypeScript, Go, Rust, Swift, Kotlin) and dynamically typed languages (Python, JavaScript, Ruby, PHP).
BigCodeBench Zhuo et al (2024) comprises approximately 1,140 Python tasks with 33.5 lines of code and 5–6 test cases per problem on average.
Data available on request from the authors.

tecnicas.observacao: Prompt mínimo com o código quebrado (contexto), um objetivo de reparo e um menu de ferramentas (instrucao); a política 'if stuck, then retrieve' é codificada no prompt (instrucao). Ferramentas: GHDL Syntax Check, o mesmo compilador do fluxo de base, com iteração sobre os erros (feedback); RAG Retrieval condicional de exemplos VHDL sintaticamente corretos, top-3, truncados a 1200 tokens (contexto e exemplos); Code Rewrite, em que um planejador produz lista de instruções e um segundo agente com contexto limpo gera a nova unidade VHDL (decomposicao e multiagente). 'outro' = seleção e sequenciamento autônomos das ferramentas pelo agente e gestão agressiva de contexto (reinício a cada tentativa, com só um breve resumo da tentativa anterior). Mecanismos acrescentados em relação ao Expert-Designed Flow, que já tem instrucao, contexto (o candidato HDL) e feedback (GHDL): exemplos, decomposicao, multiagente e outro; o MCP também substitui o prompt longo do especialista por um prompt mínimo, o que muda a instrucao sem criar categoria nova. Contrafactual: MCP contra Non-MCP nos mesmos três modelos, nas mesmas 42 funções e nas mesmas métricas (Tabelas 1-3). O 'sim' vale para o pacote inteiro (tamanho do prompt, ferramentas, política condicional, separação planejamento/geração e reinício de contexto mudam juntos) e não autoriza atribuir o ganho à recuperação condicional ou a outro ingrediente; os próprios autores dizem não ter testado diretamente o mecanismo. O protocolo MCP e o servidor de ferramentas são infraestrutura (ver componentes_fora_escopo); os orçamentos de tokens das duas condições não foram igualados.

O texto do prompt não é apresentado. Linha de base executada pelos autores.

tecnicas.localizador: Seção 3.4, p. 4; Seção 4.3, p. 5; Tabelas 1-3, p. 5-6; Seção 5.1, p. 7 ('negative control experiment')
tecnicas.observacao: Fluxo de base do especialista com os top-3 exemplos VHDL recuperados anexados incondicionalmente a todo prompt de reparo (contexto e exemplos; contexto já está presente na base, por isso só exemplos é acrescentado). O estudo o apresenta como variante para isolar a política de uso de ferramentas e como controle negativo. Contrafactual de ingrediente: Non-MCP+RAG contra Non-MCP, que diferem só nos exemplos anexados (Seção 3.4), nos três modelos (Tabelas 1-3). Isso isola a anexação incondicional de exemplos no fluxo do especialista, não a política condicional dentro do MCP: o contraste MCP contra Non-MCP+RAG difere em vários ingredientes.

riscos.descricao: Correções automáticas ingênuas no estágio de reparo de sintaxe podem alterar silenciosamente a semântica do código e levar a falhas de verificação; um gargalo semântico permanece depois do reparo (sucesso final de 16.9% a 58.1% nas Tabelas 1-3).
riscos.localizador: Seção 1, p. 1; Seção 5.5, p. 8; Tabelas 1-3, p. 5-6

riscos.descricao: Recuperação incondicional pode injetar código pouco relacionado que amplia o espaço de busca ou distrai o modelo; modos de falha identificados: poluição do contexto por exemplos grandes, incompatibilidades arquiteturais no código recuperado e truncamento de erros precisos do compilador.
Reparos plausíveis mas errados podem introduzir defeitos latentes.
Reparos plausíveis mas errados podem introduzir vulnerabilidades de segurança; sistemas agênticos ampliam a superfície de ataque (injeção no prompt ou na recuperação). Risco declarado, não medido.
Dependência excessiva de sistemas não determinísticos em contextos críticos; a vantagem de 2.3 p.p. do RAG ingênuo sobre o MCP em 235B pode estar dentro da variância entre execuções.

Aumento do uso de energia por modelos grandes; o benefício do MCP em 235B é descrito como pequeno em relação ao seu 'overhead'. Custo das condições não quantificado (o Apêndice A.1 informa horas de GPU por modelo, não por fluxo).
riscos.localizador: Seção 5.2, p. 7; Broader Impacts, p. 9; Apêndice A.1, p. 10

riscos.descricao: Propagação, via recuperação, de trechos com licença incompatível ou proprietários; amplificação de vieses presentes nos corpora de código.
Validade externa: 42 funções de um único domínio (processamento de sinais); resultados podem diferir com outros perfis de erro.

mitigacoes.descricao: Política de recuperação condicional ('if stuck, then retrieve') no MCP em vez de anexação incondicional; o contraste MCP contra Non-MCP+RAG muda vários ingredientes ao mesmo tempo, por isso o efeito da política não é medido isoladamente.
mitigacoes.localizador: Seção 3.4, p. 4; Seção 5.1, p. 6-7; Tabelas 1-3, p. 5-6

mitigacoes.descricao: Reinício do contexto a cada tentativa, com breve resumo, e gerador de contexto limpo no Code Rewrite para evitar 'context contamination' por tentativas falhas; motivado por experimentos preliminares sem valores relatados.
Remoção da ferramenta de consulta ao manual, que reduzia o desempenho quando invocada (ablação sem valores relatados).
Doze execuções independentes por função, com médias macro; procedimento de controle sem intervalos de confiança.

Recomendações não avaliadas: portões de verificação (compilação, testes unitários e diferenciais, fuzzing, verificações formais leves), recuperação no próprio ambiente com proveniência e varredura de licenças, invocação condicional e prompts curtos, registro de chamadas de ferramentas e diffs, restrição de ferramentas com efeitos colaterais e aprovação humana para ações de alto impacto, documentação da estocasticidade.

Proposta futura: ablações com orçamento de tokens igualado, ruído na recuperação, reranqueamento por similaridade de erro, desativação dos reinícios e intervalos de confiança; e pareamento do reparo agêntico com salvaguardas semânticas.

citacoes.trecho: We compare two LLM-driven methods for syntax repair in a MATLAB-to-HDL pipeline: a structured, expert-designed flow that follows a fixed sequence of operations, and a more autonomous agentic approach that uses the Model Context Protocol (MCP) [1] to dynamically select its own tools.
We study 42 MATLAB signal-processing functions and isolate the syntax-repair stage.
Naive, automated fixes at this step can silently alter the code’s semantics, ultimately leading to verification failures.

Finally, we isolate and demonstrate a key retrieval strategy, showing that on-demand tool use helps at small to mid scale, but naive inclusion of the same tools is actively detrimental to performance.
An LLM uses this version to generate multiple candidate HDL translations (in our case, 3).
After repair, syntactically correct code proceeds to a synthesis stage and is finally validated against the original testbench.
For each HDL candidate, the LLM is provided with a large, expert-written prompt containing detailed guidance and advice for repairing HDL syntax.
It uses the GHDL compiler to identify errors and iterates on the code in a fixed loop until syntax passes or a limit is reached.
The agent receives a minimal prompt containing only the broken code, a repair goal, and a menu of available tools.
RAG Retrieval: A tool to retrieve syntactically correct VHDL code examples from a vector database to provide relevant context.

citacoes.trecho: Therefore, the context was reset after each attempt, with only a brief summary of the previous attempt carried over.
In the naive Non MCP with RAG variant, the top 3 examples were appended unconditionally to every repair prompt.
In the MCP variant, retrieval was conditional on lack of progress or on compiler errors that indicated missing idioms, and the agent could choose to skip retrieval.
Variability across twelve independent runs was small (σ ≈ 2-3 pp on intermediate metrics in pilot logging).
To isolate the impact of tool-use policy, we tested a variant that naively appended RAG outputs to every repair prompt.
While we did not directly test this mechanism, the scale pattern in Tables 1-3 is consistent with this interpretation.
This gain is directly attributable to a conditional tool-use policy.
This policy was encoded in a prompt that created a simple "if stuck, then retrieve" loop, instructing the agent to first attempt a local fix and only invoke RAG when it failed to make progress.
We identified three failure modes for this approach: context clutter from large examples, architectural mismatches in retrieved code, and the truncation of precise compiler errors.
The observed advantage is small at 2.3 percentage points, so it may fall within run to run variance.
A second generator, with a clean context, produced a complete new VHDL unit from those instructions.
This separation increased candidate level syntax pass and function level reach across scales.
The manual lookup tool reduced performance whenever it was invoked, so we removed it.
Equalize token budgets when comparing policies to separate policy effects from length effects.
Our dataset consists of 42 functions from a single domain (signal processing), so these results may differ with other error profiles.
The dataset used in this study is currently internal to our company.

Risks include plausible-but-wrong repairs that can introduce latent defects or security vulnerabilities; propagation of license-incompatible or proprietary snippets via retrieval; over-reliance on non-deterministic systems in safety- or mission-critical settings; and increased energy use from large models.
Agentic systems can also widen the attack surface (e.g., prompt or retrieval injection) and may amplify biases present in code corpora.
Decoding: temperature=0.6, top-p=1.0, top-k unset, max-new-tokens backend default (unset), no stop tokens.
Trials: R=12 independent runs per function; K=3 candidates per run.

tecnicas.observacao: Pacote: um LLM classificador (Qwen3-8B), instruído por um prompt de classificação, atribui a cada problema o rótulo Simple ou Complex e gera uma justificativa textual (instrucao, raciocinio); problemas Simple recebem few-shot com três exemplos pergunta-código (instrucao, exemplos); problemas Complex recebem ICoT em dois estágios (exemplos, raciocinio, decomposicao, restricoes). 'outro' = roteamento por dificuldade, isto é, seleção da estratégia de prompting conforme o rótulo previsto por um LLM. Base identificável: zero-shot (as variações relativas da Tabela 1 são sobre zero-shot). Contrafactual de pacote: RoutingGen contra zero-shot, few-shot, ICoT estático e demais linhas de base na Tabela 1, mesmos modelos e benchmarks. O 'sim' vale para o pacote; o ganho não se atribui a um ingrediente isolado. A escolha do modelo classificador (Qwen3-8B, GPT-4o ou o próprio gerador) é seleção de modelo, fora do escopo. O prompt de classificação T_cls não é apresentado no artigo.

tecnicas.observacao: Estágio 1: o modelo recebe o problema e três exemplos resolvidos e é instruído a produzir um 'structured solving process' no formato '1: Specification' (entrada e saída) e '2: Idea' (lógica central e complexidade de tempo); são amostradas 20 cadeias (5 no DeepSeek-V3). Estágio 2: o código é gerado por decodificação gulosa condicionado ao problema e a cada ICoT, também com três exemplos. Mecanismos: instrucao (pedido de análise, instrução de conferir o processo de solução), exemplos (três exemplos nos dois estágios), raciocinio (Idea com lógica e complexidade), decomposicao (dois estágios encadeados: intenção e depois código), restricoes (formato estruturado imposto e especificação de entrada e saída). As 20 cadeias não são seguidas de seleção (Pass@1 é estimado sobre os candidatos), por isso não há amostragem. Contrafactual de pacote: ICoT estático ('without dynamic routing') contra zero-shot e demais linhas de base na Tabela 1, e contra a variante 'w/o Intermediate Reasoning' na Figura 4 (DeepSeek-V3, valores não impressos).

Ablação 'w/o Specification' contra ICoT completo com DeepSeek-V3-671B nos seis benchmarks (Figura 4, sem rótulos numéricos); valores impressos só na prosa para HumanEval (92,07% para 88,17%). Como o prompt da variante ablada foi ajustado (por exemplo, nos exemplos) não é informado.

riscos.descricao: LLMs tendem a produzir programas sintaticamente corretos que não se alinham à intenção da tarefa, resultando em saídas funcionalmente incorretas (falta de abstração de intenção).
