citacoes.trecho: Finally, the architectural intent and code constraints are assembled to prompt the LLM to generate compliant HashiCorp Configuration Language (HCL) code.
To evaluate the practical applicability of the proposed system, comprehensive ablation studies and cross-model experiments were conducted on the IaC-Eval dataset.

1) Scenario Recall and Decomposition: The system first inputs the ambiguous instruction into the “Intent Orchestration Graph” for semantic matching, retrieves similar architectural cases, and guides the LLM to decompose high-level requirements into specific resource configuration subtasks.
The system aggregates the high-level architectural blueprint and the low-level parameter constraints, assembling them into a context-rich system prompt.
This prompt directs the LLM to generate an architecturally sound Terraform configuration file that strictly adheres to HCL syntax.
Leveraging an LLM prompted as a cloud architect, the system integrates the initial intent with this subgraph context to reason and output a structured Terraform resource execution plan.
Furthermore, only the examples with the highest semantic similarity to each sub_task description are incorporated.
To prevent LLM context overflow from redundant inputs, a filtering mechanism is applied to retain only mandatory parameters and essential configuration items.
These elements are assembled into a final, tailored system prompt that directs the LLM to generate the declarative Terraform code.
Baseline (Naive RAG): This system performs static text chunking on official Markdown documentation and retrieves relevant segments based on the cosine similarity of feature embeddings.
These fragments are then supplied as contextual input to the LLM during generation.
V1 (Resource Graph RAG, RG RAG): In this configuration, unstructured text retrieval is replaced by a retrieval mechanism over an underlying resource graph.
This variant primarily examines the impact of fine-grained, structured knowledge constraints on syntactic correctness.
V2 (Dual-layer Graph RAG, DG RAG): The complete dual-layer graph architecture further introduces a first-stage intent orchestration graph comprising Scenario and Task nodes.

Consequently, LLMs trained solely on general open-source corpora frequently generate configuration code with non-compliant syntax, missing dependencies, or execution failures when applied to IaC scenarios characterized by domain constraints and rigid logic.
Consequently, when processing abstract natural language instructions, flat vector retrieval may yield mismatched results laden with irrelevant low-level parameter noise, which can misguide the LLM.
This premature generation can introduce hallucinations and undermine the semantic abstraction of the intent nodes.

For smaller-scale models, introducing detailed graph-based context may overwhelm their information processing capacity, leading to attention drift and degraded reasoning coherence in long-context scenarios.
Furthermore, when applied to real-world knowledge graphs of substantial size, the volume of retrieved nodes may increase significantly, leading to information redundancy.

Additionally, because the extensive, uncompressed structured context of Terraform projects can easily exceed model context limits and degrade token efficiency, future research will explore extracting highly abstract semantic representations—akin to domain ontologies [6]—from high-quality orchestration cases.
Specifically, the temperature was set to 0.0 to minimize hallucination and top-p was fixed at 0.9.
To prevent structural truncation during JSON generation, the maximum output token limit was unconstrained.
For instance, with Qwen3-14B, parameter coverage decreases from 43.9% under the baseline configuration to 30.2% after incorporating the proposed architecture.
Among the successfully executed cases, resource coverage rises from 23.2% to 76.7%, while required parameter coverage improves from 50.9% to 89.3%.

Experimental results demonstrate that, compared to conventional baseline systems, the proposed method improves the execution success rate by 62% in complex architectural scenarios, while resource coverage and required parameter coverage increase by 53.5% and 38.%, respectively.
Additionally, a single-hop retrieval strategy was applied for all entity association queries throughout the experiments.
The current evaluation relies primarily on open-source benchmarks and lacks validation against large-scale industrial datasets.

tecnicas.observacao: Fluxo proposto pelo estudo: o LLM recebe o prompt de geração HLS (Fig. 3: objetivo e otimização equilibrada para latência e ADP → instrucao; protótipos exatos, precisão máxima, compatibilidade com Vitis e distribuição dos 88 bits aleatórios → restricoes; SamplerZ.c, imagens dos algoritmos divididos em etapas e arquivo de cabeçalhos → contexto) e o projeto é refinado em laço quando os KATs falham na C-simulation ou quando a implementação não atinge as metas de tempo e utilização (feedback). As imagens do pseudocódigo dividido em etapas são insumo fornecido, não decomposição feita pelo LLM, por isso foram classificadas como contexto. O laço é mediado por humanos: o estudo diz que os autores refinam o projeto, o código HLS ou as diretivas, e não publica os prompts de refinamento. Pacote híbrido: inclui ferramentas de síntese (Vitis, Vivado), diretivas de síntese e P&R e intervenções manuais (ver componentes_fora_escopo). Não há condição do mesmo modelo sem o fluxo ou com outro prompt; as únicas linhas de base da Tabela I são projetos RTL escritos à mão de outros trabalhos ([16], [22]), que não isolam o fluxo nem qualquer mecanismo. Sem prompt base identificável, mecanismos_acrescentados vazio.

citacoes.trecho: We propose a design flow that iteratively leverages LLMs to generate, refine, and evaluate synthesizable C code using HLS tools.
We develop a prompt-guided, feedback-driven flow that leverages synthesis results to iteratively refine LLM-generated outputs and adapt the software-oriented code for hardware synthesis.
In this paper, we conduct a case study comparing human and LLM-assisted hardware design for SamplerZ and its supporting subroutines.

Using this, we prompt LLMs to generate synthesizable, HLS-compatible C code, emphasizing algorithm structure, control flow, and hardware synthesis features (pipelining, loop unrolling, fixed/double precision).
Goal: Generate HLS-compatible C code for four functions ApproxExp, BerExp, BaseSampler, SamplerZ optimized equally for latency and area-delay product.
I will attach the following files for Context SamplerZ.c (source code) and images of all of the algorithms broken into steps for easier optimization of each step.
If tests fail, we refine the design by looping back to prompt/code generation until all KATs pass.
If implementation fails to meet targets (timing, utilization), we refine the HLS code or directives and re-run Vitis from C Simulation to FPGA Implementation.
Feedback after simulation and PR guides refinements, ensuring a correct and optimized FPGA design.
We use a hand-coded C testbench with KATs vectors to check the generated HLS code’s functional correctness in AMD Vitis 2023.2 [33] (C-simulation), comparing outputs to expected KAT results.
This process uses the same synthesis directives for optimizations across all implementations we tested.

ChatGPT-o4-mini achieves execution time within 4% and Area Cost around 30% of Ouyang et al.’s work [16], and attains 60% higher clock frequency while requiring only five design iterations (20 hours) to produce functionally correct, synthesizable RTL code.
Second, LLMs can generate code closely matching expert-designed RTL; for example, our design achieves execution time within 5% and area around 30% of the state-of-the-art FALCON implementation [16].
Despite being prompted to balance execution time and area–delay product, the LLMs prioritized execution time (Fig. 1).

Consequently, unlike the area-optimized design by Yu et al. [22], which consolidates operations onto a single shared floating-point unit (FPU) to minimize area, the LLM-assisted implementations did not employ FPU sharing, resulting in higher DSP utilization and increased area cost.
The utilization of the ChaCha20 PRNG block from [16] has been subtracted to enable a direct comparison.

citacoes.trecho: In this study, we conduct the first large empirical study to investigate the zero-shot learning ability of ChatGPT for solving competition programming problems.

To make ChatGPT understand the given questions better and generate code solutions in batches, we optimize the prompt design and invoke ChatGPT’s API to automatically generate code solutions by asking it with an additional sentence at the front of each question: “Please generate the Python solution code for the following question.”

tecnicas.observacao: Prompts de sistema e de usuário estruturados que enunciam a tarefa (problemas do MBPP ou kernels próprios) e enfatizam o paralelismo (instrucao), com três restrições explícitas: uso de NumPy para vetorização, paralelismo via multiprocessing ou concurrent.futures e assinatura de função exata (restricoes). O estudo só executa a condição com essas restrições; não há prompt sem as restrições nem outra técnica de prompting, por isso não há base identificável (mecanismos_acrescentados vazio) nem contrafactual. A comparação de tempo de execução é com implementações de referência escritas por humanos, não com outra condição de prompting. A Fig. 1 parece rotular um «Self-repair loop (k)» e «Code gen + Guards» (texto pequeno na imagem), mas o texto não descreve laço de autocorreção e a seção Future Work o apresenta como extensão futura; por isso feedback não foi atribuído.

citacoes.trecho: This paper introduces a framework for parallel-aware code generation and evaluation, built on local large language models (LLMs) orchestrated with open-source infrastructure.

Experiments on 20 workloads—10 kernel benchmarks (e.g., GEMM, FFT, Conv2D, BFS) and 10 MBPP tasks—demonstrate that correctness is preserved while measurable speedups are achieved, particularly for computationally intensive workloads.
By embedding constraints for NumPy-based vectorization and multiprocessing-based CPU parallelism into prompts, the system enforces an emphasis on both correctness and performance.

Finally, through empirical studies, the paper provides experimental results demonstrating measurable runtime improvements across a diverse set of algorithmic kernels, thereby establishing the effectiveness of parallel-aware prompting in real-world computational scenarios.
Following this, the Code Generation stage leverages Ollama with the Qwen2.5-Coder (2B) model, guided by carefully engineered system prompts that explicitly emphasize parallelism.
Prompts are designed to enforce specific constraints on the generated code.
First, all implementations must rely on NumPy for vectorized operations, ensuring efficient mathematical computation.
Second, parallelism should be achieved using Python’s multiprocessing or concurrent.futures libraries, which provide robust ways to distribute work across multiple cores.
Finally, the generated code must follow the exact function signature provided, without deviation, to ensure compatibility with validation scripts.
Within the code generation pipeline, the system employs structured system and user prompts that are passed to the local LLM instance through controlled subprocess calls.
The raw output is then post-processed to ensure usability: markdown formatting is stripped, code fragments are extracted, and only executable Python snippets are isolated for further validation.
This ensured that the comparisons were not biased by artificially weak baselines.
Any workload that failed even a single correctness test was disqualified from subsequent benchmarking.
Runtime was measured across repeated trials with an initial warmup iteration, and the median runtime was recorded to smooth variability.
From these measurements, the speedup ratio was calculated as the baseline runtime divided by the generated runtime.

This methodology ensured that any speedup observed was genuinely attributable to improvements in parallelization or task decomposition, rather than the artificial contrast of optimized versus naive code.
A total of 20 workloads were employed, divided evenly between 10 kernel benchmarks and 10 MBPP tasks.

However, these constraints also introduced challenges: limited memory capacity occasionally restricted the size of input datasets, and CPU contention meant that some experiments suffered variability in timing.
Complementing the kernel workloads, ten problems were sampled from the MBPP benchmark suite.
The kernel benchmarks demonstrated decent correctness rates once the prompt constraints enforced explicit use of NumPy and multiprocessing.
The MBPP tasks, on the other hand, exhibited better correctness.
The corresponding correctness plot seen in Figure 2 illustrates these trends, highlighting the robustness of kernel tasks and the moderate variability of MBPP problems.

citacoes.trecho: The results show clear runtime improvements for most workloads, with gemm and reduce_sum achieving the highest speedups (1.84× and 1.77×), followed by conv2d (1.68×) and fft1d_batch (1.43×).
On the other hand, lightweight MBPP tasks often yielded negligible or no speedup, and in some cases incurred slight slowdowns due to the overhead of multiprocessing.
This outcome is expected, as the cost of parallel orchestration can outweigh the benefits for small-scale problems.

Nevertheless, across the workload set, the median speedup exceeded unity, demonstrating that parallel-aware prompting consistently produced implementations that were at least competitive and often superior to optimized human baselines.
Across a diverse set of 20 workloads, the system consistently produced implementations that matched the functional correctness of reference solutions and, in many cases, outperformed them in runtime.

riscos.descricao: As abordagens agênticas (MapCoder, LLMDebugger) têm sobrecarga computacional, alto uso de tokens e mais chamadas à API, que podem elevar custos operacionais e causar problemas de escala; tokens e chamadas são medidos (Tabela III), mas o custo monetário não é quantificado. O estudo também cita a cobrança por token de modelos em nuvem como motivação, sem quantificar.

riscos.descricao: Métodos de passo único (Zero-shot, Test-driven, CoT) frequentemente têm desempenho inferior, e métodos iniciais teriam dificuldade com tarefas algorítmicas complexas; pass@1 varia de 16.46% a 88.02% entre modelos e técnicas (Fig. 2).

tecnicas.observacao: Condição 3-shot comparada com a condição zero-shot para os mesmos modelos (GPT-4o, Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct, CodeLlama-7B-Instruct). O prompt inclui três exemplos de CSP#-PAT-84 selecionados por correspondência de categorias e tags (exemplos de código como demonstração -> exemplos e contexto) e regras de gramática derivadas do manual do PAT (documentação -> contexto). O estudo não informa se as regras de gramática G também estão no prompt zero-shot; por isso o contraste é tratado como pacote (exemplos, possivelmente com gramática) e o efeito não pode ser atribuído só aos exemplos. O texto dos prompts de avaliação não é apresentado; instrucao é atribuída pela condição zero-shot herdada. O estudo apresenta o few-shot também como linha de base (baselines) do benchmark, mas a conclusão destaca 'few-shot learning and grammar prompting' como achado.

tecnicas.observacao: Pacote híbrido: síntese de dados por LLMs (Gemini-2.0-Flash-Exp e GPT-4o-mini), filtro gramatical com ANTLR4 e pré-treinamento continuado do Qwen2.5-Coder-3B-Instruct (fora do escopo), seguido de inferência em 3-shot com regras de gramática. O contrafactual da Fig. 4 compara NL2CSP com o modelo base Qwen2.5-Coder-3B-Instruct no mesmo ajuste 3-shot; o prompting é mantido nas duas condições, de modo que a diferença corresponde aos componentes que não são prompting (dados sintéticos e pré-treinamento continuado). Nas Tabelas II e III, NL2CSP é comparado com modelos de outros backbones (7B e GPT-4o), condições não comparáveis para isolar a técnica. O efeito do pacote não é efeito isolado de prompting; mecanismos_acrescentados vazio porque, em relação ao comparador da Fig. 4, não há ingrediente de prompting acrescentado.

citacoes.trecho: For both process generation and model generation tasks, the LLMs are evaluated in zero-shot and 3-shot settings.
To fully utilize the in-context learning capabilities of LLMs, grammar rules G derived from the PAT manual and few-shot examples are also included in the prompt.
Examples are selected from CSP#-PAT-84, prioritizing those with matching categories and tags.
Moreover, we introduce NL2CSP, a multi-stage approach designed to improve the performance of LLMs in generating codes in CSP#.
NL2CSP leverages a combination of data augmentation, grammar-guided code synthesis, and in-context learning to improve the quality of the generated code.
We synthesize 5 million tokens of CSP code snippets and conduct continual pre-training on Qwen2.5-Coder-3B-Instruct to enhance its domain-specific knowledge of CSP code.
We compare the performance of NL2CSP with the base model, Qwen2.5-Coder-3B-Instruct, using a 3-shot setting.
This improvement can be attributed to the use of only syntactically correct training data for continual pre-training.

The experiment results demonstrated that, through few-shot learning and grammar prompting, GPT-4o and Qwen2.5-Coder could effectively extract key information from requirements and transform it into CSP code.
Similar to the process generation task, few-shot prompting consistently improves the results for all models except Code Llama.

While the 3-shot version generally performs better than the zero-shot version, manual inspection reveals that the Code Llama in the 3-shot setting tends to copy the provided examples into its generated output.
This behavior leads to improved Pass@3 in some cases but does not guarantee improvements in semantics or syntactic similarity.
This indicates that although it can generate syntactically correct code, it may occasionally overlook key information in the requirements.
The low absolute scores across most metrics also indicate that generating complete and semantically correct CSP# models remains a challenge.
While AST-based automated metrics are useful for evaluating structural similarity, they are approximations of semantic correctness.
However, the synthesized codes have limited complexity.
The performance improvements observed with NL2CSP may not generalize well to more challenging tasks, such as the model generation task.
To mitigate this limitation, we conduct a human review and investigate the correlation between automated metrics and human review metrics.
Online discussions among the reviewers are organized to reach a consensus on the evaluation criteria, ensuring the reliability and consistency of the human review.
Only syntactically correct codes are retained for further training.
citacoes.localizador: Seção V, item 3, p. 5 do PDF

citacoes.trecho: For each process and model, the experimental results are averaged across three runs with different random seeds.
In addition to automated metrics, we perform a human review of a randomly selected 20% of the generated codes.
GPT-4o significantly outperforms the others, achieving a pass rate of 0.6009, 3.5926 on Sufficiency, and 3.0535 on Semantic Correctness.
GPT-4o outperforms other LLMs in both zero-shot and 3-shot settings, exhibiting its capability to generate processes in CSP#.
In addition, none of these models shows the ability to generate complete syntactically correct processes.
Specifically, NL2CSP achieves a Pass@3 rate of 0.4889, significantly higher than GPT-4o (0.1556) and Qwen2.5-Coder (0.0222) in the 3-shot setting.
In particular, the Pass@3 metric doubles in the process generation task and increases nearly tenfold in the model generation task.
Tree Similarity (TRS) also provides the metrics to measure the similarity between two ASTs using tree edit distance.
It computes the percentage of subtrees in the candidate AST that are also present in the reference AST.

To investigate the correlations between automated and human review metrics proposed in Section VI-B, we calculate the Pearson Correlation Coefficient [46] for the results of GPT-4o, as shown in Fig. 3.
We evaluate the baseline models and our approach on the CSP#-Handwrite-45 dataset.

citacoes.trecho: Using prompts from HumanEval dataset, each model’s generated code snippets are assessed for validity by compilation and for correctness through unit tests to compare their performance.
It evaluates how both model types perform under challenging conditions, specifically when prompts lack essential information like docstrings or function names.

To investigate the impact of prompt variations on code quality, the prompts from the HumanEval dataset are modified for each problem in the following ways: (1) full, (2) signature only, and (3) dummy name.
To create the second group, the docstrings are removed from the original prompt; to create the third group, function names are replaced by a generic placeholder (i.e., ”foo”).

Each problem within this dataset is defined by several components: (1) task ID, (2) prompt with function signature and doc string, (3) canonical solution provided by human programmers, and (4) a collection of unit tests.

The units of analysis include the standard DeepSeek-chat versus the reasoning-focused DeepSeek-reasoner [2]; the standard ChatGPT 4o versus the reasoning o4-mini [16]; and the standard version of Claude 2.5 Sonnet and its reasoning variant Claude 3.7 Sonnet [18].

However, the standard approach of translating a prompt directly into code carries an inherent risk of producing suboptimal or erroneous output, particularly when prompts are ambiguous or describe complex logic.
This process is hypothesized to yield higher-quality code, but it introduces a critical computational trade-off.
Code that is syntactically valid but functionally incorrect fails to meet user requirements and introduces critical defects into the system.
To ensure that our observed outcomes are due to the model type and that our results are reproducible, we mitigated this threat by setting the API temperature parameter to 0 where available.
Correctness, however, was generally impaired across all models, confirming the importance of docstrings.
Here, reasoning models showed a notable advantage in the OpenAI and DeepSeek families.
The reasoning model o4-mini showed substantially higher validity than its standard counterpart GPT-4o, and DeepSeek-reasoner slightly outperformed DeepSeek-chat.
For code validity, there were significant differences among the groups (Q(29) = 369.15, p < .001).
Similarly, for code correctness, an overall test confirmed significant differences among all groups (H(26) = 969.65, p < .001).
Post-hoc analysis between the standard and reasoning versions of the LLMs are conducted to find results relevant to the stated research questions.
Finally, we calculated an average correctness score for each model by averaging these individual scores across all problems.

citacoes.trecho: This paper presents a security governance framework that combines pre-generation rule embedding, ESLint-based static analysis, structured feedback, and LLM-based repair.
However, LLM-generated front-end code may reproduce insecure patterns, including unsafe innerHTML use, unchecked media URLs, weak input handling, and incomplete upload validation.
A common output protocol asks the model to return one concise, self-contained HTML document using vanilla HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.
It excludes explanations, Markdown fences, external frameworks, and placeholder code.
This protocol is identical across all groups.
For groups with prompt embedding, a second block lists client-side rules.
It discourages unsafe HTML sinks, string-based code execution, unchecked dynamic URLs, weak upload pre-validation, and plaintext handling of sensitive information.
The output is normalized into a structured report containing rule identifiers, locations, and short explanations.
Repair groups receive the original requirement and generated document.
The Full Framework and the variant without prompt embedding additionally receive the structured static report.
The repair prompt asks the LLM to remove reported issues while keeping the requested layout and interaction logic.
The variant without static feedback receives only a general instruction to check and improve security.
This contrast separates specific machine-readable feedback from a vague self-review request.
A malformed or incomplete output is retried at most twice with the same frozen prompt.
Such failures remain in the denominator of the valid output rate and are never counted as zero-finding secure outputs.
The equivalence rules were checked with fixed regression examples before the formal run, including positive cases and deliberately incomplete counterexamples.
Vanilla provides the functional requirement only.
Prompt Only adds security rules but skips repair.
The two “w/o” variants remove one component from the full pipeline.
The experiment uses the logged model identifier deepseek-chat.
Generation uses temperature 0.3 and at most 8,000 output tokens; repair uses temperature 0.2 and at most 10,000 tokens.
Each of the 10 requirements is evaluated under five groups and three independent repeats, producing 150 requested outputs.
Results from earlier debugging runs are kept separate and are not included in the statistics.
To avoid bias caused by different numbers of valid outputs, the metrics are computed on matched valid requirements.
SSVOR is not a dynamic functional-success metric.
Because the sample is small and generation failures create missing pairs, these tests are exploratory.
A total of 132 outputs were valid and 18 were recorded as generation failures.
Prompt Only reduces average initial findings per valid output from 3.30 in Vanilla to 1.11.
The Full Framework starts from 1.52 initial findings per valid output.
Across three repeats, the no-prompt repair group achieves an RR of 88.14%, compared with 90.48% for the Full Framework.
The comparison with the variant without prompt embedding is not supported after correction (p = 0.159724).
Paired sample sizes range from 25 to 27 because generation failures remove incomplete pairs.
Sixteen failures are caused by missing required video behavior and two by missing audio behavior.
It also shows a boundary of the method: security prompts and repair feedback cannot compensate for a model that does not implement a core requested media function.
The overall VOR is 88.0%.
Reported issues are static candidate findings that may include false positives or miss runtime-specific flows, and SSVOR does not verify full browser behavior.

The endpoint exposes no deterministic random seed, and the framework covers only client-side patterns, which must be complemented by server-side validation, authorization, output encoding, and deployment testing.
The scanner and validator were developed for this experiment, so rule selection may favor syntactically observable patterns.
Because the hosted endpoint may change over time, saved prompts and metadata improve reproducibility but cannot guarantee identical reruns.
Repair-enabled configurations increased the average runtime from approximately 51 s to 79 s.

tecnicas.observacao: Prompt base do estudo: as perguntas 'Is there a bug in this program? If there exist a bug, how can we fix it?' (instrucao), uma linha em branco e o código com defeito do QuixBugs sem docstrings e comentários (código fornecido como insumo → contexto). É a condição principal avaliada pelo estudo (avaliação do ChatGPT), mas o objeto declarado é o modelo, não o prompt; na Tabela I ela é comparada com Codex [1] e Standard APR [3], resultados de outros artigos e de outros sistemas, o que não constitui contraste de prompting. Funciona como linha de base de prompting da condição com dica (seção IV.C). As quatro requisições independentes por problema, com critério 'pelo menos uma correta', foram tratadas como parâmetro da métrica de avaliação, não como mecanismo de amostragem da técnica, porque o estudo as apresenta como forma de avaliar a capacidade do modelo.

tecnicas.observacao: A requisição com dica acrescenta descrições específicas e detalhadas do defeito e mantém a docstring do programa (ambos insumos informativos → contexto). Foi aplicada somente aos problemas não resolvidos na rodada base (15 linhas na Tabela II), depois da rodada base; o total 30/40 é cumulativo (25 da rodada base + 5 resolvidos com a dica), sem condição com a dica sobre os 40 problemas. Além disso, a condição difere do prompt base em mais de um ingrediente (docstring mantida, descrição do defeito e, possivelmente, contexto da conversa anterior, pois o texto fala em 'follow-up request' e em 'conversations', mas também em informação dada 'at the time of request'). O texto do prompt com dica não é mostrado; não se afirma que as perguntas do prompt base foram mantidas, embora seja provável pela descrição. A dica não deriva de execução, testes ou compilador, por isso não foi classificada como feedback.

citacoes.trecho: This paper evaluates the effectiveness of GPT-3.5 in automatically fixing bugs in Python code using QuixBugs.
Through testing with 40 different Python bugs, We discovered that GPT-3.5 was able to accurately fix 30 out of 40 bugs cases from QuixBugs benchmark.

This benchmark contains docstring and comments of the representative of the algorithm, but all of the docstring and comments will be removed first before ask to ChatGPT and evaluate the quality of the patches generated by the ChatGPT with the correct versions provided by QuixBug.
ChatGPT is asked to debug Python code that has no docstrings or comments.
This is done for each problem in the benchmark, and ChatGPT's answers are manually verified for accuracy.
The same format is followed for every query: the questions are written first, followed by a blank line, and then the code with errors.
Four independent requests were made to ChatGPT for each programming problem with errors or bugs to assess its ability to solve them.
These methods have been tested on QuixBugs and the results published in [2].
The results of the large-scale language model Codex were taken from a recent paper [1],[2].
The experiment was conducted on ChatGPT versions from May 15, 2023, to June 10, 2023.
In the research, ChatGPT's parameters were set to the default values from the ChatGPT API [31].

For the results that were obtained through experimenting with ChatGPT, we mark a (V) indicating that at least one of the four runs was correct and we mark an (X) indicating that no answer was given in any of the runs.
Overall, in this experiment ChatGPT managed to find and fix bugs for 25 benchmark problems, 21 by Codex and only 7 by Standard APR.
Only for the BUCKETSORT and SHORTHEST-PATH and IS-VALID-PARENTHESIZATION problems did ChatGPT need 4 runs to find a bug fix.
Therefore, it appears that ChatGPT has a relatively high variance in terms of problem fixes.
Only patches that identified and corrected the bug introduced by QuixBugs were considered correct.
ChatGPT is likely just repeating what it has already learned.
Additionally, a bug was not considered fixed if additional changes made in response to ChatGPT's suggestions resulted in brand-new errors that hindered the program's functionality.
In this evaluation, only a single request was sent to ChatGPT, which means that the full potential of the dialogue system was not used.

For example, in Figure 5 where the input is a question about the longest common subsequence problem, ChatGPT generates an answer that contradicts the facts or has nothing to do with the question, in this response it cannot detect the bug or acknowledge that there is no bug in the program.
By providing specific and detailed bug descriptions as hints, the effectiveness of ChatGPT in automated program repair is significantly enhanced.
ChatGPT's successfully resolves 5 out of 15 problems that can't be solved before without the hint makes it able to fix 30/40 bugs.
Table 2 shows the results obtained from conversations with ChatGPT by providing additional information (without deleting the docstring) about unsolved benchmark problems.
ChatGPT managed to solve 5 out of 10 problems that were previously unsolvable by providing additional information about bugs at the time of request.

One of the key concerns is that ChatGPT may produce plausible-sounding but incorrect or nonsensical answers, leading to True, True-False or False in bug fixing, and even introducing new bugs or vulnerabilities in the code.

Additionally, the model's sensitivity to variations in input phrasing or repeated prompts may impact the consistency and reproducibility of bug fixing results, potentially causing unexpected behaviors in the code.
Moreover, ChatGPT's tendency to be excessively verbose and overuse certain phrases might reduce code readability and maintainability, potentially introducing unnecessary complexity and redundancy.
Furthermore, the scope of QuixBugs, focusing solely on one-line defects in classic algorithms, may not adequately reflect the diversity and complexity found in real-world Python programs.

riscos.descricao: LLMs produzem código que parece correto mas falha na execução ou trata mal casos de borda; é o problema que o estudo pretende mitigar.

Suítes de testes incompletas permitem que soluções incorretas passem na verificação; cobertura escassa de casos de borda pode gerar veredito falso-negativo e levar o Refiner a corrigir em excesso uma solução correta.

Abordagem algorítmica fundamentalmente errada do Creator se propaga pelo pipeline; tarefas com raciocínio complexo ou algoritmo novo podem derrotar Creator e Refiner; enunciados ambíguos causam interpretações inconsistentes entre agentes e saídas incorretas.

Quatro chamadas sequenciais de agentes acarretam latência de cerca de 3-4× a do passo único (tempo de execução); o artigo não descreve como essa razão foi medida. RQ3 menciona «moderate multi-agent overhead».

Verificação fundamentada em execução em sandbox (Verifier) para reduzir falsa confiança em código plausível mas incorreto; não há condição sem o Verifier.

citacoes.trecho: This paper presents COM (Cost-efficient Open-source Multi-agent), a framework that mitigates hallucinations and enhances reasoning reliability in zero-shot code generation, and GenEval, an industry-oriented DSA benchmark curated from competitive programming platforms and real-world practitioner problems, publicly released on HuggingFace.

COM decomposes code generation into four specialized agents—Creator, Critic, Verifier, and Refiner—coordinated through an execution-grounded critique–verification–refinement cycle to approximate self-corrective behavior absent in single-pass systems.

The Creator Agent receives the zero-shot problem and generates an initial Python function based on semantic comprehension, constraint adherence, and algorithmic reasoning—without access to test cases or execution feedback, reflecting the limitations of single-pass generation.
Output is produced in structured JSON format, enabling precise inter-agent communication and reducing prompt-induced bias in subsequent stages.
By grounding validation in real execution traces, the Verifier reduces false confidence in syntactically plausible but functionally incorrect code.

The Refiner synthesizes the Creator's output, Critic's structured feedback, and Verifier's execution diagnostics to generate a freshly reconstructed Python function—not a minor patch—explicitly addressing detected reasoning flaws and execution failures.
We compare COM against four prompting and refinement strategies on HumanEval using Pass@1 and hallucination rate.
Single-Pass Generation produces code directly from the task description without feedback.
Chain-of-Thought Prompting (CoT) incorporates step-by-step reasoning for improved logical coherence.
Structured Pre-Planning requires an explicit algorithmic plan prior to code synthesis.
Execution-Feedback Debugging (+Trace) feeds runtime traces back to the model for iterative self-correction.

citacoes.trecho: Despite this, LLMs frequently hallucinate—producing code that appears logically correct yet fails during execution or mishandles critical edge cases.
First, incomplete test suites can allow incorrect solutions to pass verification, as the Verifier is inherently dependent on test case quality.
Third, ambiguous problem statements cause inconsistent inter-agent interpretations, yielding incorrect outputs.
The Verifier's verdict is bounded by test suite completeness—sparse edge-case coverage can produce false-negative verdicts, causing the Refiner to over-correct a functionally sound solution.

A fundamentally flawed algorithmic approach from the Creator propagates through the pipeline, as structured feedback cannot recover from reasoning failures that exceed the LLM's intrinsic capability ceiling.
Finally, four sequential agent calls incur ≈3–4× single-pass wall-clock latency, and evaluation remains restricted to Python-based DSA problems.

citacoes.trecho: Translating Oracle PL/SQL into BigQuery SQL (BQ-SQL) is a persistent obstacle in data-platform migration.

Evaluation on quarterly batches (N=100) with execution-free metrics shows consistent gains across three refinement loops (t = 0…3); most units satisfy a practical stop rule (no High discrepancies; DSB ≥ 0.70, MCov ≥ 0.75, EDA ≤ 0.12, CQI-3 ≥ 0.80).

The main contributions of this paper are: (i) a novel, sequential DAG-based architecture that formalizes the end-to-end code conversion process; (ii) a structured feedback loop for automated discrepancy detection and iterative refinement that demonstrably improves conversion accuracy; and (iii) an empirical comparison across few-shot and SFT configurations of five Gemini family models, showing the practical benefits of a fine-tuned emitter for deterministic SQL.
The LLM, prompted as a senior DB architect, summarizes purpose, I/O, data flow, dependencies, and assumptions.
The content of the source file is embedded in a detailed prompt.
Detect FUNCTION / PROCEDURE boundaries; segment the package; for each segment, generate a BigQuery-compatible CTE; aggregate CTEs ([3a])
Provide main script + CTEs + few-shot patterns (cursor-to-set rewrites, date/exception handling, window functions); enforce house style and mappings.
It performs a comparative analysis by prompting the LLM to act as a meticulous code reviewer.
The LLM is provided with a precise prompt that includes both the script to be corrected and the list of issues to fix.
Because LLMs are powerful yet imperfect on domain-specific code, the workflow is semi-automated by design: the model acts as an assistant whose output is always subject to expert review.
A data or QA engineer reviews and, if needed, edits the artifact before triggering the next DAG.
The refined output from DAG 5 (v2.0) can be programmatically fed back as input to DAG 4 for another round of gap detection.
This iterative process handles the inherent non-determinism of LLM outputs and helps the final code meet production quality standards.

We maintain a prompt pack (GCS) with 15–20 short examples that cover the migration patterns encountered most often: cursor-to-set rewrites, date truncation/rounding, analytic windows with QUALIFY, DECODE / NVL / NVL2 mappings, %TYPE/%ROWTYPE, sequence / identity handling, and typical exception branches.
Fine-tuning reduces variance and lowers edit effort across iterations.
Packages are split at the package level to avoid leakage.
Decoding for code emission: temperature 0.0–0.1; “SQL-only” contracts; stop tokens to block commentary.
Metrics are computed over iterations t = 0, 1, 2, 3, where t = 0 is the first draft from DAG 3, and t ≥ 1 are successive DAG 4 → DAG 5 refinement loops.
For completeness: baseline runs used Gemini 1.5 Pro (few-shot) for DAG-1 and DAG-4, and Gemini 1.0 Pro (SFT) for DAG-2/3/5; later experiments include Gemini 2.5 Pro (few-shot) for analysis stages.
The Fully Few-Shot configuration used a single few-shot model for all five DAGs to establish a baseline (results in Table I, Fig. 2).
The Hybrid SFT configuration combined few-shot model for analysis (DAGs 1, 4) with SFT model for code emission (DAGs 2, 3, 5) to measure fine-tuning impact (results in Table II, Fig. 3).
A principal limitation is the reliance on execution-free metrics; while valuable for tracking structural fidelity, they cannot guarantee functional correctness or performance post-deployment.
Due to corporate confidentiality, source code, prompts, production logs, and proprietary datasets cannot be released.

Filtragem de soluções do CodeNet que não compilam ou não executam.
Configurações de inferência padronizadas (temperatura fixa 0,7) para reduzir a variabilidade; não há comparação com outras configurações.
Templates padronizados e instanciação controlada, com só o código C variando, para mitigar a sensibilidade ao prompt.

Testes de Wilcoxon signed-rank entre estratégias de prompt e entre modelos, para verificar que as tendências não são artefato de variação estocástica; procedimento estatístico, não comparação com e sem mitigação.

citacoes.trecho: We evaluate open-source LLMs using three prompting strategies to understand the impact on translation performance.

To improve coverage, we augment the dataset with LLM-generated test cases and assess the impact of prompting strategies by comparing standard zero-shot (S-ZS), curated zero-shot (C-ZS), and Chain of Thought (CoT) approaches.
We assess the ability of seven open-source LLMs to translate C programs into Python, Java, and Rust.
1) Standard Zero-Shot (S-ZS): provides direct instructions without examples or additional reasoning.
Each prompt is built from a template and instantiated with the relevant source code and task details during execution (see PolyglotWeb.site for the prompt templates):
Starting from the minimal S-ZS baseline, we incrementally added elements to clarify the task, constrain output format, and emphasize functional equivalence.
3) Chain-of-Thought (CoT): encourages the model to explain its reasoning before generating the translated code, but still in a zero-shot manner regarding external examples.
Note that CoT in Polyglot is implemented in a zero-shot fashion: models are instructed to reason step by step before producing the final code, but without in-context demonstrations or examples.

The defined scope also sets specific evaluation conditions: Polyglot currently operates under zero-shot prompting without in-context examples, reflecting typical usage, and evaluates a single translation per program.
We also found that LLM-generated code frequently introduces syntactic errors and semantic bugs, impacting reliability and maintainability.
For instance, successful execution does not guarantee that code is maintainable, idiomatic for the target language, or performance-optimized.
Training data leakage remains a concern, as LLMs may memorize content seen during pretraining.
However, since translations of our dataset are not publicly available, this risk is limited.
While we use datasets with clear provenance, leakage cannot be fully ruled out.
Reproducibility is another limitation, as LLMs can produce different outputs across runs, even with identical inputs (a result of their inherent stochasticity).
LLM performance is also sensitive to prompt formulation, making it challenging to disentangle true model capability from the effectiveness of the prompt strategy.
To mitigate this, we use standardized templates and controlled instantiation, e.g., fixed prompt structures with only the C code varying, though some input sensitivity remains.
Selection bias may occur from filtering criteria (e.g., requiring multiple valid solutions), potentially reducing diversity.
Computational constraints also limit the scope of our evaluation.
Lastly, despite relying on objective metrics, human interpretation bias remains a risk.
While this introduces synthetic elements, all additions were validated to minimize bias.
We discarded invalid test cases and used three randomly selected C++ solutions to determine expected outputs (we used C++ to avoid data leakage with respect to our experimental evaluation).
We retained only test cases where all three solutions produced matching outputs.
To mitigate these issues, we filter out non-compiling or non-executing solutions from the CodeNet dataset.
We apply standardized inference settings to reduce variability stemming from the inherent stochasticity of LLM inference.
All models were evaluated under a fixed inference configuration (temperature = 0.7) with one decoding trial per model–prompt setup, reflecting standard zero-shot usage.

In our experiments, we tested 150 problems, and for each, we considered six solutions of varying complexity (Table I).

citacoes.trecho: This corresponds to more than 56700 translations (150 problems × 6 solutions × 3 languages × 7 LLMs × 3 prompts).
Overall: S-ZS and C-ZS outperform CoT across all metrics (compilation, runtime, and test success).
Rust is excluded due to consistently low pass rates, though similar prompt-related trends were observed.
While contextual metrics offer a complementary view, they are omitted due to space constraints.
A key finding is the effectiveness of structured prompting: S-ZS and C-ZS strategies outperform CoT in runtime reliability, reinforcing the benefit of concise, instruction-based guidance.

Não há base identificável: o estudo não executa prompt único, ReAct nem outra condição sem o pacote; só varia os modelos atribuídos às ferramentas. Pacote híbrido: inclui seleção de modelo por ferramenta, orçamento de tentativas, Guardrails e infraestrutura de observabilidade (ver componentes_fora_escopo). Os prompts das ferramentas não são reproduzidos no artigo.

citacoes.trecho: Through this methodology, we enhanced the architecture and structure of the evolving agentic framework for code generation, achieving a notable 98% accuracy in solving challenging coding tasks via specified workflows.
In our AI agent implementation, we crafted precise prompts tailored to each tool, ensuring the models perform as intended.
We implemented a structured iterative workflow agent (see Fig. 2), which provides process control and maintains shared state across tools throughout the entire generation flow.
A retry mechanism was also incorporated, allowing to configure code - generation attempts (a state parameter) to effectively manage unsuccessful outputs.
Analyzer: This tool verifies if a task is a coding - related one. If it is, it directs the task to the Developer; if not, it responds with a generic answer.
Developer: Responsible for designing and implementing Python code to solve the task. It also generates test cases and code to execute them. When all tests pass, the tool outputs “All tests passed.”
Evaluator: Acts as a code reviewer, validating the code, making necessary corrections, and adding comments for clarity.

Executor (Tester): Runs the code and checks for the presence of the phrase “All tests passed” in the output. If successful, it returns the result; otherwise, it sends the task back to the Developer with detected errors.
Using ensemble models with distinct roles - where the critic/validator is a separate model - proves to be an intuitive and effective approach for achieving optimal results.
This indicates that the validation model not only corrects the code but also enriches it with detailed comments, as specified in the prompt instructions.
Without proper control and reliability mechanisms, agents can exhibit unpredictable behavior, leading to high operational costs, potential security risks, and performance degradation.
Cost Control: Generative models are invoked by agents without transparency, making it difficult to track the number of calls per execution and manage associated costs.

Prompt Control: Many agent libraries conceal the actual prompts passed to LLMs, relying on complex, often opaque prompts (Fig. 1), and making decisions based on tool function comments and argument types in ReAct agents.
By design, they always generate a response, and, notably, an LLM can often produce different outputs for the same prompt due to inherent variability.
One challenge, however, is hallucination - when the model generates erroneous information that may not align with the prompt or its training data.
Testers may encounter a range of potential errors when running these scripts, and it’s essential for our agent to handle and log these issues effectively.
Our validation tool acts much like a code reviewer in a traditional SDLC, addressing a substantial portion of errors before execution.

It is beneficial if agents can work effectively for specific use cases; however, in our experience, such applications often make too many autonomous decisions, leading to frequent errors and incorrect outcomes.
React agents often suffer from inconsistent or missing state management, which can lead to unpredictable behavior and errors when state isn’t properly passed or updated across tools.
While the 4 - bit quantization of DeepSeek - Coder - V2 offers significant advantages in terms of reduced memory and power requirements, it also poses challenges in maintaining model accuracy.
This paper presents an analysis of the quantization’s impact on model fidelity and discusses potential mitigation strategies, including hybrid quantization techniques, to optimize performance.
Each LLM call is routed through AWS Bedrock Guardrails, which filters out inappropriate or offensive content.
To ensure robust monitoring and observability, we log every tool's state, utilizing AWS CloudWatch for real - time logs and alerts.
All models are from reliable and trustworthy vendors (Meta, Anthropic, AWS, Depseek - AI and Mistral), costing less than $1 per one million tokens, and MMLU benchmark over 70.

tecnicas.localizador: Seção III.A, PDF p. 3; seção IV.A, PDF p. 4; seção V, PDF p. 5 (sem página impressa visível)
tecnicas.observacao: Condição avaliada no experimento: módulo de reparo sintático seguido de módulo de reparo semântico (etapas encadeadas → decomposicao), com templates de dicas pré-desenhados (→ instrucao), cadeia de raciocínio (→ raciocinio), descrição do problema, código errado, bloco de erro, mensagens de erro, entradas/saídas de exemplo e informação de contexto (→ contexto) e código correto de colega mais semelhante como dica candidata (→ exemplos e contexto); o resultado de 62,7% inclui reamostragem de dicas com reteste local (→ amostragem). Comparada pelo estudo com 'the baseline version without a multi-source prompt strategy', também descrita como 'a baseline with simple prompts for proper output formatting'; a composição do baseline não é detalhada (não se informa se mantém a cadeia de raciocínio, o encadeamento em duas etapas ou a reamostragem), por isso os mecanismos acrescentados registram só o que a própria denominação do baseline indica faltar (informação multifonte e código de colega) e o contraste é tratado como pacote. Pacote híbrido: inclui análise estática por AST, compilador/parser, localização de bloco de erro e algoritmo de similaridade de código (fora do escopo); o modelo Xiaohang foi ajustado finamente (não se informa se o baseline usa o mesmo modelo). O ganho relatado é do pacote, não de um ingrediente.

tecnicas.nome_original: Chain-of-thought heuristic strategy / thought-chain guided hierarchical hint generation ("chain-of-thought prompting strategy")
tecnicas.localizador: Resumo, PDF p. 1; seções IV.A e IV.B, PDF p. 4; seção V, PDF p. 5
tecnicas.observacao: O resumo diz que o estudo 'pioneers a chain-of-thought heuristic strategy' (sequência de dicas 'error attribution, logic reconstruction, and optimization validation'); templates de dicas com contexto do bloco de erro e mensagens de erro são entregues ao modelo, que analisa as causas passo a passo. Não há condição com e sem a cadeia de raciocínio com resultado relatado; a comparação relatada é a do pacote contra o baseline sem estratégia multifonte.

tecnicas.nome_original: Peer-code selection / similar-code search (código correto mais próximo como dica candidata)
tecnicas.localizador: Seção III.B e Eq. (1), PDF p. 4; seção V, PDF p. 5
tecnicas.observacao: Seleção, entre todos os códigos corretos, do mais semelhante ao código errado por similaridade de fluxo de dados e AST (pesos a = b = 0,5), integrado à dica enviada ao modelo. O estudo declara ablação 'with and without peer-code selection', mas não relata nenhum valor dessa ablação (nem na Fig. 2, que mostra só o sistema, nem no texto); o isolamento existe no desenho declarado, sem resultado extraível.

tecnicas.localizador: Seção V e Fig. 3, PDF p. 5
tecnicas.observacao: Quando a primeira tentativa falha nos testes locais, o sistema regenera o reparo a partir de dicas reamostradas e retesta (várias tentativas com seleção pelo teste → amostragem). Não se descreve devolução da mensagem de erro dos testes ao modelo, por isso não se registra feedback. O estudo relata só a contribuição por rodada (32,6% na primeira tentativa; +30,1% após duas rodadas; total 62,7%), sem condição comparável sem a técnica.

citacoes.trecho: This paper aims to explore an automated method for detecting errors in program source code and offering heuristic correction guidance.

Pedagogically, it pioneers a chain-of-thought heuristic strategy that guides students through a progressive hint sequence of "error attribution, logic reconstruction, and optimization validation," fostering a complete cognitive process from "requirement analysis" to "algorithm design" and "code implementation."

This strategy combines task background information, sample inputs and outputs, and contextual analysis of the error type for comprehensive analysis, rather than being limited to simple error descriptions.
Next, the hint generation module will first employ a program code analysis algorithm to select a code from all correct codes that are "closest" to the erroneous code as a candidate hint.
a and b are weights, both set to 0.5 by default.
Initially, this module employs pre-designed hint templates.
Through a “chain of thought” mechanism, it gradually analyzes the causes of the error.
This study selected 10 representative C - language programming problems, covering basic and advanced topics like array processing, string manipulation, and recursion.
From an online judging platform, we collected 12,102 code submissions for these problems, of which 6,049 were erroneous (failed to pass all test cases) and 6,053 were correct.
To simplify the evaluation, for each problem, we randomly selected 25 erroneous and 10 correct code samples, forming a test set of 236 codes in total.
It is built on an open, private-domain large-model framework and has been fine-tuned and optimized for higher-education teaching and research scenarios.
During interface calls, the temperature was uniformly set to 0.2 to ensure stable and diverse outputs.

The experimental process consists of three steps: first, the original error - code and problem description are input into the "syntax repair module" of the Xiaohang AI Assistant, which automatically removes all compilation errors and outputs intermediate products that pass the syntax check.
Next, the intermediate product is fed into the "semantic repair module", where the model uses a chain-of-thought prompting strategy.
It combines similar-code search and multi-source prompt generation to produce the final repaired and complete code.
A repair is deemed successful if the repaired code passes all test points in one go without modifying the test cases or the coding environment.
These compare the model's performance with and without peer-code selection, and against a baseline with simple prompts for proper output formatting.
Nevertheless, the repair success rate for questions H, I, and J remained below 40%, with that of question G being less than 20%.
As shown in Figure 3, the system has a 32.6% first-time repair success rate.
In the second stage, it regenerates repair codes based on resampled hints and conducts local retests.
After two rounds of iterations, an additional 30.1% of samples were correctly repaired, bringing the total repair rate to 62.7%.

These results demonstrate that the Xiaohang AI Assistant has competent automatic repair capabilities at the compilation level and shows significant potential for improvement in handling complex business logic and boundary cases.
Compared to the baseline version without a multi-source prompt strategy, our research method achieves an average repair rate improvement of approximately 13.56 percentage points.
Additionally, beginners' over-reliance on generative large models can somewhat weaken their ability to think independently and solve problems [11].

Instead of directly supplying complete correction solutions, this method not only improves the accuracy of error detection but also stimulates students' abilities to think critically and solve problems.
Experimental validation demonstrates that the framework effectively promotes knowledge internalization and skill enhancement.

citacoes.trecho: Results demonstrate that incorporating explicit design constraints during prompting significantly boosts initial generation accuracy (measured via the pass@k metric), particularly in Python but also in C++.

Each LLM was evaluated under two experimental conditions: one using detailed design specifications including explicit preconditions and postconditions, and another condition using the same specifications but with preconditions and postconditions removed and replaced with extended natural language descriptions of each method’s behavior.
As shown in Fig. 7, each prompt includes a base template, the class name, file name, class description, instance variables (with names and types), and method signatures.
Method-level preconditions and postconditions were also provided for the design constraint specifications.
The prompt also specifies the collaborating classes and their specifications.
Second-order collaborations were also provided to the model, as the added understanding of types returned by method calls improved generation quality.
You are an expert software engineer implementing a system in C++.
Do not write anything except code.
Remember that anything in a precondition can be assumed to be true, and assertions should not be written for them and they should not be checked at runtime.
The designed system, Tic-Tac-Toe, consists of 15 interacting software classes.
To ensure validity, each set of preconditions and postconditions was carefully reviewed, iteratively refined, and verified against the intended behavior of the system.
Each testing suite comprises 73 distinct test cases specifically designed to provide thorough coverage of all functional requirements of each class and method.
This ensured that a class-level test failure was not caused by an incorrect implementation in another class.
For each model, each class was generated 20 times, and the generated code was evaluated using the appropriate testing suite (Python, Java, or C++).
T-statistics and p-values were calculated using the ttest_rel function within Python’s scipy.stats library.
Additionally, some established benchmarks face challenges regarding continued validity, particularly HumanEval, due to potential leaks into the training datasets of popular LLMs [25].
These unpredictable variations could result in varying output quality and correctness when using LLMs for automated code generation, as it does with human developers [1].

This suggests that structured constraints are especially effective at guiding the model toward a correct solution on the first attempt, which is critical in real-world settings where regeneration may be costly or impractical.
Python saw the most pronounced improvement (+39.85 percentage points), followed by C++ (+9.67) and Java (+8.10).
Interestingly, the improvement in C++ only reached statistical significance at pass@1, while not achieving significance at pass@10.

Java, while showing consistent improvements, did not reach statistical significance (p = 0.066), though the trend is notable and suggests the potential for significance with larger sample sizes or more complex systems.

However, Gemini Flash 2.0 and Llama 3.3 showed the largest relative improvements under the constraints condition, suggesting that more structured prompts may help bridge performance gaps in less powerful or smaller models.
In C++, structured prompts reduce compilation failures.
In Java, they mitigated runtime issues from unexpected boilerplate.

Additionally, investigations could be carried out to mitigate problems with correctly importing external libraries by prompting the LLM to write the imports at the bottom of the code file, so that it has the full context of the implementation with which to guide its selection of imports.

tecnicas.observacao: Pacote híbrido proposto pelo estudo. Mecanismos: papel de sistema ('You are a data analyst...') e regras em linguagem natural → instrucao; metadados estruturais e documentação Markdown de domínio inseridos no prompt → contexto; exigência de retornar só código Python executável, sem explicações → restricoes; encadeamento de etapas (extração de contexto, construção do prompt, geração e execução do código, síntese de insights por um segundo LLM a partir das saídas executadas) → decomposicao. Os dois LLMs atuam em sequência (o segundo consome as saídas do primeiro), sem interação descrita; por isso não se atribuiu multiagente. Inclui componentes fora do escopo (validação sintática/semântica/contextual e execução em ambiente controlado). Não há condição executada sem o framework nem com prompting alternativo (por exemplo, 'ad hoc prompting'); a comparação é com a análise de um especialista humano, que serve de referência de correção, não de condição de prompting. Sem base identificável, mecanismos_acrescentados fica vazio.

citacoes.trecho: Ad hoc prompt-based use of LLMs is brittle, difficult to reproduce, and prone to hallucination.
Game analytics depends on high-volume gameplay telemetry, but Large Language Models (LLMs) cannot directly operate on full logs due to token limits, schema variability, and compute cost.

In evaluation on induced-latency gameplay data, GameLogLLM reproduces expert quantitative analysis and produces domain-relevant narrative insights using locally hosted 7B–14B parameter LLMs, without external APIs, supporting reproducible and privacy-preserving analytics.
LLMs exhibit the “lost-in-the-middle” effect [5], and dense, domain-specific logs deviate from pretraining distributions, often leading to hallucination and poor comprehension.
This motivates a code-centric framework for game analytics, where LLMs generate validated Python scripts to operate on structured data.
Stage 2 transforms the metadata produced in Stage 1 into a structured prompt that defines both the LLM’s role and its operational boundaries.

Instead of generic instructions, the template explicitly incorporates three inputs: the dataset description ({structural_metadata}), the domain knowledge from the Markdown file ({markdown_documentation}), and the user’s question ({user_inquiry}).
5) Return only executable code, without explanations.
citacoes.localizador: Quadro 'Code Generation Prompt Template', item Constraints, PDF p. 2 (impressa 527)

citacoes.trecho: The output of Stage 2 is thus a fully context-aware, inquiry-constrained prompt.
The LLM (Qwen2.5-coder-7B) generates Python code which is then cleaned, validated, and executed in a controlled environment.
Syntactic validation: the generated code must import permitted libraries, compile, and run without errors.
A second LLM is therefore introduced, operating at a higher interpretive level.
Unlike ad hoc prompting or conventional tooling, the framework enforces controlled prompt construction, rule-guided code generation, and evidence-linked insight synthesis.
This reduces analyst effort and cost while preserving reproducibility.
Over 100 participants used 46 gaming workstations with automated latency manipulation across five conditions (0ms, 50ms, 100ms, 150ms, 200ms) using kernel-level traffic control.
One example of visual analytic outputs for total kill counts across latency conditions for all players are shown in Fig. 2.
The two plots exhibit identical trends and values: : across all latency buckets (0 – 200 ms), the absolute difference in reported kill counts is ≤2 kills per bucket (≤1.3% relative error).
We tested several 7B-14B LLMs and selected two models for detailed evaluation: LLaMA-3.1-8B and Qwen3-14B.
The results, summarized in Table I, show that both models produce interpretations that are consistent with the expert analysis.
Using the expert-verified tables as reference, both models exceed 90% factual alignment.
Finally, both stages run on locally hosted 8B–14B models served via Ollama, without external API calls.

By grounding the LLM in dataset metadata and domain knowledge, the framework reduces hallucination, supports reproducible analysis, and cleanly separates deterministic computation from interpretive reasoning.
Latency shows minimal influence on kill counts (r = 0.08), with a gradual decline as latency increases.

tecnicas.nome_original: MASDP (multi-agent system for code generation via dynamic precaution tuning)
tecnicas.localizador: Resumo e contribuições, PDF p. 1–2 (impressas 86–87); seção III.B e Algoritmo 1, PDF p. 3–4 (impressas 88–89); Tabela I, PDF p. 9 (impressa 94)
tecnicas.observacao: Pacote híbrido: quatro agentes (Reminder, Programmer, Executor, Tester) que interagem → multiagente; precauções em linguagem natural (diretrizes de prevenção de erros) geradas pelo Reminder antes do código → instrucao, em etapa encadeada (precaução → código → testes → execução) → decomposicao; atualização das precauções a partir de mensagens de erro normalizadas da execução, até 4 iterações → feedback; estratégia de duas soluções (com e sem precauções) com seleção por testes ou pelo usuário quando ambas passam → amostragem. Reminder, Executor e Tester são Llama3-8B ajustados por destilação (LoRA) a partir de instruções geradas pelo GPT-3.5 (fora do escopo, ajuste_fino); o Programmer é Magicoder-7B sem ajuste, zero-shot. Contrafactual de pacote: linha Magicoder (entrada direta do requisito) na Tabela I, mesmo modelo do Programmer. O ganho do pacote inclui o ajuste fino dos agentes (Tabela III mostra MASDPgen sem ajuste fino com valores menores) e não é efeito isolado de prompting nem de um único mecanismo. Duas condições de teste: MASDPgen (testes gerados pelo Tester, experimento principal) e MASDPprov (testes fornecidos pelo benchmark, sem Tester, cenário idealizado); tratadas como condições da mesma técnica. Mecanismos acrescentados em relação à entrada direta do requisito ao Magicoder (que já é instrucao); instrucao aparece também como acrescentado porque as precauções são um ingrediente novo de diretrizes.

tecnicas.localizador: Seção IV.A.3, PDF p. 7–8 (impressas 92–93); Tabela I (grupo 'LLM Enhancement Approaches (based on Magicoder-7B)'), PDF p. 9 (impressa 94); seção IV.F (RQ5) e Fig. 4, PDF p. 10–11 (impressas 95–96)
tecnicas.observacao: O LLM primeiro gera precauções a partir do requisito e depois as usa como prompt para gerar o código: precauções são diretrizes curtas (2–3 frases) de prevenção de erros → instrucao, produzidas em etapa anterior encadeada → decomposicao. Papel focal porque o estudo a apresenta como proposta própria ('the proposed precautions', RQ5; 'a novel type of error-avoidance prompt', RQ9) e a avalia como abordagem separada na Tabela I; é também componente do MASDP (Reminder). Contrafactual: linha Magicoder (entrada direta) na Tabela I, mesmo modelo, diferindo no ingrediente das precauções. O artigo não diz se, nessa linha, as precauções são geradas pelo próprio Magicoder-7B ou pelo Reminder ajustado; o cabeçalho do grupo indica 'based on Magicoder-7B'.

citacoes.trecho: To overcome these, we propose MASDP, a multi-agent system for code generation with dynamic precaution tuning, inspired by the whistleblowing mechanism.

MASDP introduces a fine-tuned Reminder agent that proactively anticipates potential errors, shifts the burden of code optimization from the Programmer to itself, and iteratively refines precautions based on execution feedback—thereby enhancing cooperation and reliability.

Extensive experiments show that MASDP, built entirely on small LLMs, outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, including GPT-4, while substantially reducing computational overhead and safeguarding data privacy.
It comprises four specialized agents: the Reminder, the Programmer, the Executor, and the Tester.
The requirement is provided to the Programmer in two forms: (1) augmented with the generated precautions, and (2) in its raw form without precautions.
If both versions pass, they are presented to the user as alternative solutions.
This process is repeated iteratively until a correct solution is found or a maximum number of iterations is reached.
These precautions serve as concise, targeted error-prevention prompts.
However, code relies on strict logic and contextual coherence, which CoT prompts for incremental reasoning can disrupt.
Errors in these prompts can critically impact the code.

To ensure fairness, we employ an unaltered base LLM without any modifications or enhancements (such as fine-tuning or prompt engineering) as the Programmer agent and execute zero-shot code generation.
This is because in some cases, the precautions may mislead LLMs to generate incorrect code.
In this scenario, concerning the code generated in the previous stage that did not pass the test cases, the Tester provides error feedback to the Reminder.
If an error message appears, the Tester determines the error type and outputs a standardized version.
This dataset consists of 164 programming tasks, each comprising a natural language description, a corresponding Python function signature (such as ‘def name():’), and associated test cases.
MBPP (sanitized version) [35] is introduced by Google Research, includes 427 Python programming problems, each accompanied by a natural language description, a code solution, and 3 test cases.
This paper employs the fixed version ‘gpt-3.5-turbo-0301’.
The final result is reported as the average of five independent experimental runs.
Specifically, for CoT (Chain of Thought), we follow the standard zero-shot CoT prompt [14], prepending the phrase “Let’s think step by step” to the input.
For Self-planning, we adopt the strategy in [29], which involves a planning phase where the model, given two reference examples, outlines a high-level solution strategy before generating code.
For Self-Edit, we leverage the PyCodeGPT-110M developed in [6] as the code editor to optimize the code based on the error results from executing the code generated by the LLM.
Regarding Precautions, the LLM first generates precautions according to requirements and then use these precautions to guide the LLM to generate code.
This standardization ensures that observed differences stem from agent-level design rather than disparities in underlying model capacity.
All fine-tuning is performed via the LoRA method [40] using consistent hyperparameters (rank: 8, alpha: 16, dropout: 0.05, batch size: 16).
According to the experimental results presented in Section IV-E, we limit the number of iterative precaution updates to 4.
For all LLMs, the maximum token limit is fixed at 1024, and the temperature parameter is set to 0 to ensure deterministic outputs.
The experimental results in Table I indicate that MASDP in both scenarios achieves state-of-the-art performance on four code generation datasets.

Shifting the focus to approaches for enhancing LLMs, it is intriguing to note that Zero-shot CoT negatively impacts performance on HumanEval and HumanEval-ET, performing worse than the base model, Magicoder.
Notably, even when using only Precautions as prompts, we achieved impressive performance, demonstrating the effectiveness of precautions.
Compared to GPT-3.5, MASDP achieves better performance on introductory and interview-level problems but shows no clear advantage on competition-level tasks.
This suggests that while precautions are effective at preventing local errors, solving highly complex problems still requires LLMs with stronger reasoning capabilities.

Notably, when removing the Reminder, to preserve the functionality of the Executor, we adopt a framework in which the Executor feeds back error messages to the Programmer for code revision–similar to the Self-collaboration setting.

First, the fine-tuned MASDP significantly outperforms the non-fine-tuned baseline (by approximately 10%), confirming the necessity of knowledge distillation for developing the specialized capabilities of small LLMs.
Third, the performance degradation after removing the dual-solution strategy confirms its effectiveness in mitigating prompt misguidance.
Moreover, since both the Executor and Tester share responsibility for precaution tuning in MASDP, removing either role effectively disables this process.
LLMs from the LLama family are fine-tuned in the same manner as this paper to assign specific roles to each function, whereas GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 perform role assignments solely through prompts.
Besides, online calls raise data-privacy concerns that limit adoption in finance, healthcare, and other sensitive arenas.
Specifically, during the training phase, MASDPgen and MASDPprov incur approximately $10.25 and $16.61 in costs, respectively—additional expenses that do not arise in the API call mode;
Under strict evaluation on the HumanEval and MBPP datasets, the test cases generated by the Tester achieved accuracy rates of 62.3 and 64.4, respectively.

For the multi-agent system, the overall error inheritance rate of MASDPgen is 56.0%, higher than the average single-agent rate of 52.8%, demonstrating an error amplification effect during collaboration.
Typical issues include overgeneralized warnings and logically inconsistent precautions.

In addition, the extended experiments in Appendix B show that using more advanced models (such as DeepSeek-V3 [16] and GPT-4o [45]) instead of GPT-3.5 as the teacher model can further improve the performance of MASDP, although it may be accompanied by an increase in cost.

tecnicas.observacao: Pacote completo na configuração few-shot: prompt de sistema com papel de 'reverse engineering expert' e instrução da tarefa (instrucao); exemplos (p, s̃) recuperados por similaridade semântica (Top-K) → exemplos e contexto; pseudocódigo-alvo fornecido como insumo → contexto; saída restrita a {Yes,No} sem explicação na identificação, exigência de preservar a semântica e 'No explanation' no refatoramento → restricoes; paradigma 'identify-then-refactor', que percorre os seis tipos de distorção e encadeia prompt de identificação e prompt de refatoramento → decomposicao. Sem prompt base identificável para o pacote: o contrafactual 'sem o pacote' é o pseudocódigo bruto do descompilador (linha 'Raw PseudoCode' da Tabela IV), e há comparação com DeGPT, SAILR e DREAM (Fig. 5). Pacote híbrido: inclui recuperador CodeBERT com ajuste fino e verificador Twin-Closure (fora do escopo); o ganho do pacote não é atribuível a um único mecanismo. O verificador classifica a equivalência semântica, mas o artigo não descreve reenvio ao LLM quando a verificação falha, por isso não se registra feedback.

Contrafactual: colunas/linhas 0-shot (sem exemplos) contra 1-, 5- e 10-shot no mesmo modelo e conjunto (Tabelas III, IV e V), mantidos os demais ingredientes. Parte do sistema proposto, por isso componente. O contexto já existe no 0-shot (pseudocódigo-alvo como insumo); a recuperação acrescenta novo ingrediente de contexto, por isso 'contexto' consta em mecanismos_acrescentados.
