citacoes.trecho: By dynamically injecting structured rules from a domain-specific knowledge graph into the prompts, the framework ensures that safety standards are inherently respected during code generation, rather than through post-hoc inspection.
The essence of this module is to embed the entire rule library, which consists of 225 validated (head, relation, tail) triples in JSON format, directly into the system prompt as a unified context.
Upon receiving a natural language requirement, the system performs no explicit rule matching or retrieval.
However, the initial experiments revealed that embedding all the extracted rules directly into the system prompt led to input truncation, increased response latency, and degraded code quality.
Before generation, the system selects the top-k most relevant rules (e.g., k = 40–60) based on keyword overlap and semantic similarity with the input.
Generated using a locally deployed Qwen3-30B model, with only natural language requirements provided and no additional rules or knowledge injected
citacoes.localizador: Tabela II, linha Group B, coluna GENERATION METHOD, PDF p. 5

citacoes.trecho: Generated using the proposed KNSE-Code framework, where relevant rules from the knowledge graph are dynamically injected into the prompt to guide code generation
citacoes.localizador: Tabela II, linha Group C, coluna GENERATION METHOD, PDF p. 5

citacoes.trecho: Input the three types of natural language requirements into each comparative method, record the generated code and compilation results, and collect statistics for each evaluation metric.
Group B omits one channel’s state validation and lacks explicit state checking, resulting in incomplete logic.
Group B’s function lacks array boundary checks, posing a potential out-of-bounds access risk.

Group C, while structurally sound, lacks input validation for critical signals such as airspeed and command values, including boundary checks and validity verification, which may result in erroneous state transitions under invalid input conditions.
Although the logic is correct, this may lead to maintenance errors and is classified as a low-severity issue, with no impact on functional correctness or safety.
Furthermore, the generation process lacks transparency, there is no clear trace from requirement to code.
After extraction, each rule is manually reviewed by domain experts for consistency with the original document, clarity, and executability.
In addition, the code generated by KNSE-Code includes comments for key logic sections, indicating the rule clauses they comply with, supporting manual auditing and tool-based tracing.
To ensure data security and full control, Qwen3-30B is deployed locally within a secure intranet environment, with no external communication.
The results show that KNSE-Code matches 100% functional complete, reduces safety violations by up to 85% compared to direct LLM generation, and completely avoids high-severity violations.
Although the evaluation is limited to three representative requirements, the framework was designed from the outset with the goal of cross-project and cross-model reusability.

citacoes.trecho: In this study, we present SelfCoder, a self-guided, single-agent framework for code generation utilising the OpenAI Assistant API built upon GPT-4.
By tapping into a comprehensive Python code knowledge base, SelfCoder creates an initial draft and refines it iteratively through a feedback loop using the Code Interpreter tool.
SelfCoder is defined as a code generation assistant with instructions specifying its input/output formats.
The initial generation phase includes creating test cases for the Code Interpreter to assess the quality of the output.
If errors are found, SelfCoder iteratively regenerates the code and reruns the tests until all cases pass.
The codebase includes 50 classic programming problems and optimal Python solutions sourced from Leetcode, addressing lists, strings, dictionaries, and list-nodes.
We require SelfCoder to identify similar problems, analyses similarities and differences with user requirements, and drafts initial code accordingly.

The ablation study results, shown in the last four rows of Table II, highlight the impact of different self-interactive tools.
Incorporating the Knowledge Retrieval and Code Interpreter tools separately enhances the base model’s performance, confirming the effectiveness of the self-interactive mechanism.
However, current LLMs face challenges like code hallucination due to ambiguous task instructions and limited testing mechanisms.
This self-interactive loop relies on internally stored information, reducing hallucinations and ensuring comprehensive access to relevant data.
However, its performance declines on the extended versions, indicating that SelfCoder may still struggle with robustness, especially for extreme and boundary value cases.
Stability is inconsistent due to an apparent fixed temperature setting, leading to unreliable output for identical inputs.
The combined use of Knowledge Retrieval and Code Interpreter tools raises operating costs up to 25 times compared to the base GPT-4 API.
Additionally, the 512MB token cap for knowledge base files in the Assistant API restricts specialised domain development and limits SelfCoder’s accessible information for code generation.
The extended versions, HumanEval-ET and MBPP-ET, add additional test cases to rigorously evaluate robustness.
The multi-agent framework, utilizing multiple GPT agents, outperformed completion models but lagged behind instruct models due to errors in formatting and incomplete code.

É a linha de base (G3P sem semente) e também a etapa de evolução do pacote proposto. citacoes.trecho: In this work, we proposed to combine GPT (in our case ChatGPT) with a G3P system, forcing any synthesised program to fit the BNF grammar–thus offering an opportunity to evolve/fix incorrect programs and reducing security threats.
For the first step of the research, we used ChatGPT to generate the code by providing the task textual descriptions.
However, using the original problem descriptions, verbatim, as prompts to ChatGPT will return code snippets (instead of functions) with console prints (instead of function returns).

To overcome this issue, we slightly modified the original textual description of the benchmark suite to explicitly request that ChatGPT generates a program formatted as a function and that the function returns the result instead of printing it on the console (as it is defined in the benchmark [28], [29]).
The mapped program from the previous section is seeded into G3P’s initial population to guide its evolution more effectively.

However, challenges such as ensuring correctness and safety still need to be addressed as some GPT-generated programs might not work while others might include security vulnerabilities or blacklisted library calls.

GPT techniques might output: (i) several incomplete snippets or not fully fit-for-purpose codes which often makes them impossible to exploit in their form, (ii) incorrect programs which need improvement, or (iii) programs that include security vulnerabilities or blacklisted library calls that posing a safety/security risk.

The goal of this research is double: (i) generate programs that correctly solve program synthesis problems (ii) while fitting a pre-defined grammar to reduce their security threat and ensure their safety.
However, in its default configuration, G3P is not successful in fixing some incorrect GPT-generated programs–even when they are close to a correct program.
Overall, ChatGPT has demonstrated remarkable power in generating code for benchmark problems, correctly suggesting 26 out of 28 considered problems.

For “Wallis Pi”, it generated a program that calculates the value of π instead of π/4, whereas for “Digits”, it successfully separated each digit into a list but was unable to handle the negative sign (i.e.,“-”).
A checkmark (✓) indicates that GPT-generated programs were correct or at least one correct solution has been found with 100 runs.
Overall, our proposed algorithm successfully mapped GPT-generated codes for 13 problems into programs that fit BNF grammar with no loss of information (i.e., Completely Mapped).

In this subsection, the GPT-generated codes and our grammar-mapped programs are reported for the four mostly mapped programs from table I (i.e., Replace Space with Newline, Even Squares, Last Index of Zero, and Digits).
Eleven poorly mapped problems are categorised and analysed in this subsection.

However, for the remaining two problems in the “Mostly Mapped” category (i.e., “Even Square” and “Digits”), G3P was unable to fix the incomplete/incorrect GPT-generated programs through evolution even though these GPT-generated programs were very close to the correct solution.

The general settings for the GP system are: 100 Runs; 300 Generations; Population size of 1000; Tournament selection with tournament size of 7 (we forced at least one of each pair of first 500 parents contain seeded code to guarantee the seeded program is fully utilised); 0.9 Crossover probability and 0.05 mutation probability; 3 variable for per data type; and 1 second max execution time.

tecnicas.observacao: Condição de prompting do framework GRACG: trechos do repositório recuperados pelo recuperador baseado em GNN são concatenados num prompt estruturado, antes da descrição da consulta, ordenados por relevância. Pacote híbrido: o conteúdo do contexto depende de um recuperador treinado (GraphSAGE heterogêneo e projeção MLP), registrado em componentes_fora_escopo. O contrafactual é a condição «w/o context» do bloco EvoCodeBenchPlus da Tabela III (só descrição da tarefa e assinatura da função). `instrucao` e `restricoes` vêm do prompt base (descrição da tarefa em linguagem natural e assinatura da função como especificação de interface); a presença desses elementos na condição GNN context é inferida da descrição do pipeline («concatenated into a structured prompt alongside the user query»), mas o template literal não é mostrado. O ganho, se houver, é do pacote, não de um mecanismo isolado. Não há condição fim a fim com contexto recuperado por KNN, nem condição «local context + GNN context»; qual configuração do GraphSAGE (3, 5 ou 7 camadas; fase de pré-treino ou de ajuste) foi usada na geração não é informado.

citacoes.trecho: To address this issue, we propose a graph-based Retrieval-Augmented Code Generation (GRACG) framework that leverages repository-level context.
Retrieved nodes are then used to construct prompts for LLMs to perform repository-aware function generation.
However, in terms of end-to-end code generation, we observe non-significant improvements in the metrics, even when oracle functions are used.

We address the task of repository-level code generation, where the goal is to synthesize a function or method implementation using information that may be distributed across multiple files of a repository.

tecnicas.observacao: Linha de base de prompting: um plano em linguagem natural, passo a passo, é inserido junto à descrição do problema antes da geração do código (decomposicao); herda do Vanilla a geração zero-shot a partir da descrição (instrucao). O contrafactual é o pacote SP contra Vanilla (geração direta zero-shot) na Tabela II, para quatro modelos e dois benchmarks; o estudo comenta o contraste só na narrativa (SP «minimal assistance» e deterioração no CodeContest). Segundo a p. 7, os planos seguidos foram «generated by state-of-the-art LLMs», sem nomear os modelos; não é informado se o plano foi gerado pelo próprio modelo avaliado, nem o texto do prompt, nem se houve exemplos few-shot nesta implementação. A seção de trabalhos relacionados (p. 2 do PDF) descreve o Self-Planning original com few-shot prompting, mas isso não é afirmado sobre a execução deste estudo; por isso `exemplos` não foi listado (nao_informado). citacoes.trecho: Specifically, we apply a lightweight fine-tuning process on code-oriented models to automatically learn algorithm embeddings.
The algorithmic embeddings are treated as learnable parameters in the LLM’s input layer, optimized through standard language modeling objective on a frozen LLM.

Self-planning (SP) [9]. A prompting method that leverages LLMs’ planning capabilities to decompose intents (problem descriptions in algorithmic programming tasks) into several easy-to-solve sub-problems, which takes the form of step-by-step plans, and solve them accordingly.
citacoes.localizador: p. 6 do PDF (p. 436 impressa), seção IV.B

citacoes.trecho: Self-Planning [9] divides the process of code generation into two phases, planning and implementation; the former step utilizes LLMs’ comprehension ability and few-shot prompting to decompose problems into a directive plan, then the plan is appended to the input, allowing models to follow during the implementation in the latter step.
citacoes.localizador: p. 2 do PDF (p. 432 impressa), seção II.B

We apply our approach to models of three different parameter sizes and evaluate them on three algorithmic programming benchmarks.
Additionally, our method outperforms traditional full fine-tuning approaches by a significant margin across all tested benchmarks.
In contrast, the large (15B) model showed a peak performance of 15.6 at the length of 416.

tecnicas.observacao: Pacote completo: prompt com instrução da tarefa (nome da função), contexto recuperado do repositório e requisito da tarefa (assinatura e docstring) -> instrucao e contexto; geração de um rascunho que serve de consulta para a segunda recuperação e geração final -> decomposicao (etapas encadeadas sem retorno de erros, portanto não feedback). Mecanismos acrescentados calculados em relação ao Direct Generation, tomado como prompt base (instrução e requisito sem contexto recuperado). O contrafactual é de pacote: CECoder contra Direct Generation com os mesmos modelos (Tabela I); contra Vanilla RAG e RepoCoder a diferença envolve vários ingredientes (consulta por blocos de invocação, fusão RRF, segunda geração). Não há ablação dos componentes; o ganho não pode ser atribuído à recuperação de granularidade fina isoladamente. A recuperação usa infraestrutura de busca (janela deslizante, Bag-of-Words, Jaccard, análise por AST, RRF) que seleciona o contexto do prompt; foi tratada como parte do mecanismo contexto. Os trechos recuperados são janelas de código do repositório; o artigo diz que eles demonstram usos de elementos de código, mas não são exemplos resolvidos da tarefa, por isso não se atribuiu exemplos (aplicado igualmente aos comparadores com recuperação).

citacoes.trecho: To this end, we propose CECoder, a novel framework that performs fine-grained and accurate retrieval of concrete code element usage, demonstrating how elements are invoked and composed.
All snippets are finally re-ranked and selectively integrated into a prompt template.
However, this often leads to irrelevant context and subsequent code element misuse, resulting in logic errors, type mismatch, and other errors.
The prompt consists of three essential components: task instruction, retrieved context, and task requirement.
citacoes.localizador: PDF p. 3 (impressa 91), Sec. III-A, Draft Code Generation

citacoes.trecho: Although the draft code incorporates a set of code elements, the semantic gap between natural language and code may still lead to irrelevant code snippet retrieval, causing LLMs to misuse code elements.
In addition, we include Direct Generation as a non-retrieval baseline, which inputs the task requirement into the LLM without any retrieved context.
RepoCoder iteratively retrieves code based on the code generated in the previous iteration.

In this paper, we select GPT-3.5-Turbo (gpt-3.5-turbo-1106) and Code Llama (7B) as base models for evaluation, due to their frequent use in code generation benchmarks and to address performance and data leakage.
citacoes.localizador: PDF p. 5 (impressa 93), Sec. IV, Implementation Details

citacoes.trecho: However, RepoCoder’s whole-function semantic retrieval may introduce irrelevant code snippets, particularly harming performance on smaller LLMs such as CodeLlama-7B, where it underperforms even single-round methods like Vanilla RAG.
The integration of both retrieval results via reciprocal rank fusion enhances generation accuracy and reduces misuse of code elements.

tecnicas.localizador: p. 5 do PDF (p. 648 impressa), seção III.C Prompting Methods; p. 3 do PDF (p. 646 impressa), Fig. 2; p. 6 do PDF (p. 649 impressa), seção IV.C e Tabela IV
tecnicas.observacao: Quatro etapas encadeadas: (1) gerar só o HTML a partir da captura de tela; (2) gerar o CSS a partir da captura e do HTML da etapa 1; (3) inferir informações de interação a partir da captura e do prompt; (4) gerar o JavaScript a partir da captura, do HTML e da interação inferida. Cada etapa recebe instrução em linguagem natural (instrucao) e as saídas intermediárias alimentam as etapas seguintes (decomposicao). O contrafactual é o pacote completo de quatro etapas contra o direct prompting (geração única de HTML, CSS e JavaScript), na Tabela IV, para três modelos; não há ablação das etapas, de modo que o ganho não pode ser atribuído a uma etapa específica (por exemplo, à etapa de inferência de interação). O pacote é só de prompting, mas o WebCoder-8B foi ajustado com amostras de instrução que reproduzem as quatro etapas (p. 3 do PDF), o que é componente fora do escopo e pode favorecer o formato multi-step nesse modelo. O texto não informa o conteúdo completo dos prompts; a Fig. 2 mostra só trechos truncados.

citacoes.trecho: In this paper, we introduce RetypeR, an integrated retrieval-based framework to repair Python type errors automatically.

To integrate the information retrieved from the aforementioned external and internal stages, RetypeR constructs context-aware repair prompts for LLMs to guide them in generating correct patches for type errors.
The context-aware repair prompts include five parts: the external information, the internal information, the buggy line, the context before and the context after the buggy line, as shown in Figure 3.
The placeholder token <INFILL> signals to the model the precise location where new code should be generated according to the applied template.
Each repair prompt includes only one donor code identifier.
To repair each bug, we sample the model 5,000 times and set a five-hour timeout limit following previous study [13].
Subsequently, it executes the test suites on each patch to identify the plausible patches that successfully pass all the test suites.
Following common APR practice, we conduct thorough manual evaluations of each plausible patch to determine its accuracy as a correct patch.
We use the OpenAI API of ChatGPT (gpt-3.5-turbo) and Codex (code-davinci-002) for evaluation, invoking these models using the same prompt from the prior work [12].
Specifically, we begin with a scenario where no retrieval stage is applied, meaning both the external and internal retrieval stages of RetypeR are ablated, and only the base LLM is used.
Moreover, when considering the entire project, some identifier tokens unrelated to the repair may achieve high rankings, introducing more noise [16].
Following prior work [16], and due to the high cost of APR, we focus on the pandas project within the TypeBugs benchmark which has the largest number of type errors.

Due to the limitation of computational resources, we only explored the case of directly fusing the retrieval ranking results of lexical-aware and semantic-aware retrieval modules employing the RRF strategy.
To mitigate this concern, we conduct experiments on two different benchmarks, TypeBugs and BugsInPy, and demonstrate that RetypeR achieves state-of-the-art results on both benchmarks.
TypeFix [12] is the state-of-the-art approach for fixing Python type errors, which mines fix templates by hierarchical clustering and applies these templates as domain knowledge for patch generation.

citacoes.trecho: Using these datasets, we evaluate two different techniques for generating code with LLMs:
Retrieval-augmented generation, which involves searching for and packing relevant language documentation in the query’s context to be used during inference time.

When presented with a textual query for generating code, a search is done for documentation about relevant APIs and the results are concatenated with the original textual query as context; this augmented query is presented to the GPT4 model for generating the final code.
We compare the effectiveness of the fine-tuning and RAG approaches for Ansible code generation, and we also include both the base models, StarCoder and GPT-4, as baselines.
We use GPT4 instead of StarCoder for the base model for RAG because GPT4 is a significantly more powerful general-purpose model that is better suited for text analysis and information retrieval.

While all four types of tasks are required for a complete code generation tool, we choose to focus on the simplest case of description → task, which occurs in practice when generating the first task of a role.
The latter can be implemented using prompt engineering, where a pre-existing model is instructed to treat the documentation as added context for the user’s prompt.
The chat assistant is constructed as a layer on top of the GPT-4 API, using a series of API calls to first search for relevant documents, and then incorporate found material into the final answer.
Course material is uploaded to a vector database, which is searched via semantic similarity check using a smaller model to provide citations that improve the accuracy of responses.
Playbook content is analyzed using PyYAML to normalize the syntax, and duplicate entries were removed.
Data is split into 90% training data and 10% test data.
In comparison, while the output of the RAG implementation appears correct, it misses key details including a conditional and looping over two services.
Omitting details from the prompt or ignoring relevant context can lead to code that work that looks good in the abstract but is non-functional in practice.
In our experiments with UIUC.chat, we found that it was often over-relying on the documentation and providing what amounted to templates, as opposed to actual working code.
A major limitation in our evaluation of the RAG approach is that we do not have sufficient data to rigorously compare it to fine-tuning.
The full inference process, including the model’s specs and the full data that it was trained on are not public knowledge, so reproducibility and data-leakage are a concern.
This may cause additional bias in our evaluation metrics and limit the potential utility of this tool outside of open-source projects.

In the process of training and running inference on these models, we used over 100 GPU credits on a super-computing cluster, which is a non-insignificant amount of resources, and potentially more than is available for DSLs with a smaller user base.
Another concern is whether existing evaluation methods, which can often be brittle and unreliable, can be used effectively in comparing code generation techniques across languages.

citacoes.trecho: Ansible Lightspeed is an LLM-based service designed explicitly to generate Ansible YAML, given natural language prompt.
The description becomes a prompt for the model to generate the code of the task, which usually consists of the module name followed by module keys and values.
The completion request consists of a prompt field and the value is the Ansible code before the cursor position where the inline suggestion is triggered in the code editor.
In the pre-processing stage the prompt is checked for valid YAML syntax and the indentations are adjusted based on the requirements of the inference request.
After that, it is passed through Ansible Anonymizer [7] to remove any personal, identifiable information.
The model is pre-trained with about 143 billion tokens and then fine-tuned with about 500k natural language to Ansible task samples.

After the inference response is received by the Ansible Lightspeed service the response is again passed through the Ansible Anonymizer to cleanup any personal identifiable information that might be present in the model output.
It also redacts any credentials and removes and/or replaces any deprecated Ansible syntax from the suggestions.
Currently, we use greedy decoding to generate one suggestion for every prompt.
Generated shell commands are also likely to be incorrect, which could inspire more user edits.
Such edits indicate that the generated suggestion is not necessarily incorrect, but is definitely incomplete and can be better organized.
The second largest source of complaints, accounting for 15.71%, is due to poor suggestions provided by the model.
The majority of the negative feedback, 66.49%, is coming from users that do not manage to get Ansible Lightspeed to work.
Our Telemetry data includes events from users who may not be Ansible programmers and simply want to try out the system with toy examples, which could add noise to our analysis.
To mitigate this issue, we created a cohort of returning users who used Ansible Lightspeed on two or more days.
We filter out duplicates and consider only unique requests for our analysis.

We compared our acceptance rate with the initial acceptance rates of Google Machine Learning enabled code completion system [24] (MLECC) which is an internal tool at Google, Github CoPilot [49] and CodeCompose [26], which is an internal tool at Meta.
As per this definition, the Strong Acceptance rate for Ansible Lightspeed comes out to 49.08%, compared to the initial acceptance rate of 65.92%.
The first observation was that there were 306 instances of minor edits, or 5.4% of all accepted suggestions, in which the module name was also edited.
There are a total of 1,710 initially accepted suggestions which were explicitly edited by the users at the module level.
Out of a total of about 10,696 unique users, 3,910 or 36.6% were returning users.
3,910 users out of total 10,696 users, or about 36.5%, are returning users.

tecnicas.localizador: p. 1 do PDF (resumo); p. 3 do PDF, seção III.A e Fig. 2; p. 4 do PDF, seções III.D–III.F e Algoritmo 1; p. 5 do PDF, seção IV.B e Tabela II (página impressa não exibida)
tecnicas.observacao: Pacote que recupera documentação por busca densa (FAISS) e esparsa (BM25), combina os escores (Hybrid Confidence Scoring, Gear 1) e, se o índice PSI do modelo for maior que 1,0, reordena os documentos em forma de U no contexto do prompt (Gear 2). Mecanismos: `contexto` (documentação recuperada fornecida ao gerador); `outro` (posicionamento dos documentos no prompt segundo a confiança, colocando os de maior escore nas extremidades; não cabe nas demais categorias); `otimizacao_prompt` (o PSI, calculado com Exact Match em consultas de calibração, decide automaticamente se o prompt é reordenado). Acrescentados em relação ao Base RAG: `outro` e `otimizacao_prompt`; a recuperação híbrida altera o `contexto`, categoria já presente no Base RAG. O contraste com Base RAG compara o pacote inteiro; o ganho não pode ser atribuído a um único ingrediente. O modelo de prompt (instruções, formato) não é descrito.

tecnicas.localizador: p. 3 do PDF, seções III.A e III.C, Eq. (2); p. 5 do PDF, seção IV.C e Tabela III
tecnicas.observacao: Fusão normalizada (Min–Max) dos escores FAISS e BM25 (α = 0,3; β = 0,7). Modifica a seleção e o ranqueamento da documentação recuperada (`contexto`, já presente no comparador), por isso a lista de acrescentados fica vazia. A passagem de Static U-RAG para CAUS-RAG muda ao mesmo tempo o HCS e o uso do PSI, de modo que não há condição que difira apenas no HCS. A Tabela III varia os pesos α/β dentro do CAUS-RAG (0,9/0,1; 0,5/0,5; 0,3/0,7), mas não traz condição sem o componente (nem só densa nem só BM25); é variação de parâmetro, não contrafactual com e sem.

tecnicas.observacao: Reordenação em U dos documentos recuperados (maior confiança nas extremidades, menor no meio). O estudo define a condição Static U-RAG «without hybrid scoring or PSI» para estudar a contribuição de cada componente; Static U-RAG e Base RAG diferem apenas na reordenação, ambos com ranking semântico FAISS (Tabela II). A profundidade k usada nas condições Base RAG e Static U-RAG não é informada (só a do CAUS-RAG, k = 10).

tecnicas.localizador: p. 3 do PDF, seção III.A; p. 4 do PDF, seção III.D, Eq. (3) e Algoritmo 1 (linhas 13 e 25–26)
tecnicas.observacao: Índice calculado uma vez por arquitetura com médias de Exact Match quando o documento correto está no início, no meio e no fim do contexto; Ψ > 1,0 ativa a reordenação, caso contrário mantém a ordem do ranking. Classificado como `otimizacao_prompt` por selecionar automaticamente a disposição do prompt com base em desempenho medido. Os valores de PSI obtidos para Phi-3.5, Mistral e Qwen não são relatados, de modo que não se sabe se a reordenação foi efetivamente aplicada em cada modelo. Não há condição com e sem PSI mantendo os demais componentes.

citacoes.trecho: CAUS-RAG boosts the Exact Match accuracy of Qwen-2.5 from 17.3% to 86.5% and Phi-3.5 from 11.5% to 71.2%.
In the first step, a hybrid confidence score, based on semantic and syntactic match, is assigned to each retrieved document.
In the second stage, it ranks these documents into a U-shaped prompt structure, placing the chunks with the highest scores in areas where the model pays the most attention.
This reranking is performed only if the PSI probing step detects a U-shaped positional bias in the target model architecture.
The PSI is calculated once per architecture and treated as a model-level constant.
Otherwise, if ΨLLM ≤ 1.0, the documents are simply used in their ranked order without any reordering.
The final sequence X is the reordered context passed to the generator LLM.
The experiments were conducted on a PyTorch API benchmark comprising 52 queries, each requiring exact matches for method names, signatures, and arguments.
To study the contribution of each component individually, three different architectural methods are defined:
Static U-RAG: U-shape context rearrangement applied directly to the semantically ranked retrieved documents, without hybrid scoring or PSI.
citacoes.localizador: p. 5 do PDF, seção IV.B, item 2

citacoes.trecho: The second type is confabulation errors, where the model relies on its internal parametric knowledge instead of using the retrieved context, leading to outdated or incorrect API calls.
These contribute to 60% of the remaining EM failures and explain why the gap between KW and EM does not completely vanish.
CAUS-RAG successfully mitigates confabulation errors in 78% of cases compared to Base RAG.
For deployment, the interceptor can be precomputed and cached for frequently occurring queries, reducing overhead to sub-5 milliseconds.
If an exact match is not present in the top-k results, reranking is meaningless.
The approach also assumes a consistent U-shaped attention pattern, which may not be true for newer architectures.
Further, the current evaluation is limited to code generation tasks.

This, in turn, causes the 69.2% improvement in models like Qwen (p < 0.01), indicating that the improvement is not caused by variations in the dataset but rather due to the combined effect of correct retrieval based on hybrid scoring and their correct placement.

O ganho é do pacote e não se atribui a um mecanismo isolado. Os exemplos de entrada e saída do problema são usados como restrições e testes de verificação, não como exemplos resolvidos; por isso não se registrou 'exemplos'. citacoes.trecho: On HumanEval, our framework improves Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct’s Pass@1 from 40.2% to 80.3%.
It first extracts structured constraints from problem examples, converting open-domain generation into controlled structured search.
Then, code is generated under these constraints, and an external verification mechanism (AST+example execution) creates a model-independent feedback loop to suppress hallucinations.

We explicitly decompose the process into: (1) Structured Constraint Generation (SCG) for extracting high-certainty information, and (2) Constrained Code Generation (CCG) for low-certainty implementation under explicit constraints.
Verification and feedback rely entirely on external executable rules, not model self-evaluation, avoiding hallucination accumulation.
Constraints are uniformly represented using a predefined JSON Schema, compressing open-domain information into a closed, verifiable space.

Considering that lightweight models may still have issues like bracket mismatch or missing fields in complex format generation, we introduce a rule-based legality check and lightweight post-processing module after the SCG stage to automatically correct format errors.
Experimental statistics show that about 64.6% of generated constraints are directly usable; remaining cases involve hallucinations (26.2%), incomplete parsing (6.1%), or content errors.
The prompt consists of the original problem, structured constraints, and generation instructions.
If generated code fails external verification, we trigger iterative optimization with maximum iterations N=5.

In even-numbered rounds, conditional Chain-of-Thought reasoning is introduced to guide the model in analyzing failure reasons; in odd-numbered rounds, standard re-sampling is performed to introduce new candidate solutions.
Input: Problem description P; Original test examples Sorig; Max iteration N = 6
All experiments use a uniform prompt template to ensure comparability, avoiding task-specific prompt engineering that could interfere with results.
Static constraint methods (Expert Prompt) actually reduce Pass@1 to 30.5%, indicating that weak natural language constraints alone are insufficient and may even interfere with generation.

Methods relying on model self-evaluation like CoT and Self-Refine show substantial improvement (up to 78%) but are prone to accumulating hallucination errors over multiple iterations, as the model cannot reliably judge its own output correctness.
ReAct+AST introduces external syntax checking but only verifies syntax, missing logical errors.
Notably, performance only drops by 3.2% without human assistance, demonstrating strong automation potential.

First, the method relies on example information available for verification in the problem description; when examples are scarce or coverage is insufficient, the filtering capability of dynamic verification is limited.
Third, external verification and multiple iterations inevitably increase inference latency.
Only code passing both verifications is considered valid.

tecnicas.observacao: Processo conduzido por humanos com ChatGPT 3.5: parte do prompt ingênuo (1), acrescenta requisitos de forma cada vez mais detalhada (grade 5x5, tamanho e orientação dos navios, dois jogadores, GetX) → restricoes; avança uma funcionalidade por vez (tabuleiro do Jogador 1, dois jogadores, navegação com GetX, controlador GetX) → decomposicao; os autores testam o código e enviam correções a partir dos erros observados (prompts 9, 10 e instruções de correção não transcritas) → feedback; a partir do prompt 8 o código gerado anteriormente é devolvido ao modelo → contexto. Base identificável para mecanismos_acrescentados: o prompt ingênuo (1), só com instrucao. Houve também regeneração de respostas (seis reformulações do prompt 7, cada uma regenerada três vezes), mas o estudo não relata seleção entre respostas; por isso amostragem não foi atribuída. Não há condição executada sem o processo: só a aplicação final recebe notas, e o processo inclui correções manuais de código (ver componentes_fora_escopo).

tecnicas.nome_original: providing ChatGPT with the previously generated code (code that was previously generated will be passed to ChatGPT)
tecnicas.localizador: p. 2 do PDF (seção III, Methodology); p. 4 do PDF (seção IV.B.3, prompt 8)
tecnicas.observacao: Parte do processo iterativo descrita na metodologia e adotada após o insucesso das reformulações do prompt 7. O prompt 8 implementou os dois jogadores sem erros de sintaxe, ao passo que as reformulações do prompt 7 mantinham erros; porém os prompts 7 e 8 diferem em mais de um ingrediente (texto, requisitos explicitados e presença do código), e a comparação é qualitativa e não controlada. Não há contrafactual que isole o fornecimento do código.

tecnicas.localizador: p. 2 do PDF (seção IV.B.1, prompt 1); p. 3 do PDF (Fig. 1 e texto seguinte)

citacoes.trecho: Results show that, up to a certain level of complexity and by using an interactive process of increasingly detailed prompts, the AI tool is capable of generating functional code, that can be the base for the inclusion of a more complex logic or structure.
For this work, ChatGPT 3.5 was used to generate a mobile application from scratch using the Flutter framework, while the complete process was evaluated at each step.
The initial proposed methodology of the activity included an iterative process of creating prompts.

citacoes.trecho: The process starts with providing simple instructions to ChatGPT to create the application from scratch, and then, with each iteration, the prompts become more technical and detailed than the previous one.

tecnicas.observacao: Agente ReAct em duas fases: na fase de raciocínio, chama ferramentas de análise estática (Joern/CPG, Tabela 1) para recuperar ingredientes internos (código doador) e analisar a causa-raiz; na fase de solução, recupera de um banco vetorial um par bug-correção com causa-raiz semelhante (top n = 1, Figura 5) e gera sugestões de reparo e vários patches, validados pelos testes (só o top-1 plausível é mantido). Pacote híbrido: inclui ferramentas de análise estática, modelo de embeddings, banco vetorial, orçamento de patches e temperatura, que não são prompting. O contrafactual é ReinFix_NN (dois componentes de busca removidos) contra ReinFix_DP (completo), ambos com GPT-4o no Defects4J V1.2 (Tabela 5, p. 9); o ganho é do pacote e não se atribui a um único mecanismo. Os mecanismos acrescentados são em relação a ReinFix_NN. A composição exata de ReinFix_NN (se mantém raciocínio sobre causa-raiz, decomposição e amostragem) não é detalhada. Não se marcou feedback: o estudo não informa se o resultado da validação de uma tentativa (até 3 por bug) é devolvido ao modelo; as observações das ferramentas são recuperação de contexto, não crítica do código gerado.

Ablação ❷ ReinFix_DN contra ❶ ReinFix_NN (GPT-4o, Defects4J V1.2). Também há o contraste ❻ ReinFix_DP contra ❸ ReinFix_NP, analisado pelo estudo no item 3 da seção 5.3.1. A ferramenta de análise estática em si não é prompting; o mecanismo de prompting é o código recuperado inserido no contexto. O estudo não detalha se a variante mantém amostragem e decomposição do pacote completo.

O estudo não detalha se a variante mantém amostragem e decomposição do pacote completo.

citacoes.trecho: In this paper, we propose ReinFix, a novel framework that enables LLMs to autonomously search for repair ingredients throughout both the reasoning and solution phases of bug fixing.

In the reasoning phase, ReinFix integrates static analysis tools to retrieve internal ingredients, such as variable definitions, to assist the LLM in root cause analysis when it encounters difficulty understanding the context.

During the solution phase, when the LLM lacks experience in fixing specific bugs, ReinFix searches for external ingredients from historical bug fixes with similar bug patterns, leveraging both the buggy code and its root cause to guide the LLM in identifying appropriate repair actions, thereby increasing the likelihood of generating correct patches.

To coordinate these processes, we implement our approach on the basis of the Reasoning and Acting framework [52], empowering the LLM to autonomously plan, analyze, and invoke the appropriate repair ingredients search tools as needed.
For each root cause and suggested fix pair, we ask the model to generate multiple patches.
For validation, only the top-1 plausible patch that passes all test cases is retained.
Only the internal ingredient search component is used for contextual code search, assisting LLMs in better analyzing the root cause of the bugs.
Only the external ingredient search component is used for bug pattern retrieval, assisting LLMs in better identifying repair behaviors to generate patches.
We removed two key components from the original ReinFix implementation to establish a basic baseline that represents the fundamental repair capabilities of ChatGPT.
One notable example is ChatRepair [49], a ChatGPT-based APR approach that combines patch generation with instant feedback, enabling conversational-style repair interactions.
Similarly, ThinkRepair [54] uses Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting on ChatGPT to enhance bug reasoning during repair.

For example, RepairAgent [2] enables the LLM-based agent to perform repair by invoking external tools, and FixAgent [24] realizes unified debugging by constructing the multi-agent collaboration paradigm.
For example, AlphaRepair [48] and GAMMA [58] generate patches directly for fault locations by leveraging traditional template-based techniques to design specific repair template prompts.
The training data of LLMs may contain correct patches for buggy projects, potentially affecting the evaluation.

To mitigate this risk, we follow previous work [54] and evaluate on bug cases collected after the cutoff date for LLM training data to ensure that the LLMs have not encountered the bug cases in the testing benchmarks during training.
We use the exact match strategy to filter out overlapping samples with those in benchmarks to avoid data leakage.
Using LLMs may lead to higher repair costs.
In comparison, ChatRepair, using GPT-3.5 as the base model, has an average cost of $0.42 per bug fix.

Upon analysis, we found that repair ingredient retrieval methods that do not consider program dependencies often introduce irrelevant or incorrect donor code. This can mislead the model into inferring incorrect root causes and result in repair failures.
Finally, the plausible patches are manually reviewed to verify the semantic correctness.
The agent reads the bug information and follows the Algorithm 1's analysis process to address complex tasks while avoiding potential infinite loops during reasoning and action.

Following the common practice in the APR community [42, 46, 48, 49, 54, 58–60], we reuse the reported results from previous studies [14, 32, 42, 46, 48, 49, 54, 58, 60] instead of directly running the APR tools.

Moreover, our ablation experiments (Section 5.3) demonstrate that the design choices in ReinFix further enhance the repair capability of base models, ensuring that the observed gains are independent of data leakage.
Overall, ReinFix achieves a 10.34% improvement over ThinkRepair.

citacoes.trecho: We propose an attention-guided pruning strategy that selectively removes less informative code tokens, allowing more representative examples to be included in the prompt and thus providing richer semantic context for LLMs.

Experiments on the ClassEval dataset using GPT-3.5 demonstrate that our strategy significantly outperforms random pruning, achieving 4.2%, 10.2%, and 13% higher accuracy in class-level code generation.
Further analysis shows that pruning up to 40% of tokens while including four additional examples maximizes LLM performance, enabling more accurate and coherent class-level code generation.

citacoes.trecho: Certainly, these examples do not contain desired code snippet and are chosen randomly.
The second process is to request LLM with temperature of 0 for the stability of LLM's output, namely GPT-3.5-turbo, to generate the code solution snippet for each input processed prompt.
The time complexity of attention-guided pruning algorithm is O(N∗L_T), where L_T denotes the target numbers of tokens.
Additionally, the 0-1 backpack algorithm demands to handle two-dimensional array when programming dynamically, costing space in memory.
The first experiment we conduct, compared with the pruning strategy we propose, is few-shot learning of LLM without pruning.
Furthermore, the prompt includes only a single code generation example in its examples part.
The second baseline experiment is conducted for ablation study, named random pruning.
In our work, we take all 100 class-level code generation tasks in ClassEval into experiments.
In addition, the desired code snippet does not emerge in those examples, chosen stochastically, in the prompt.

With several tries of pruning tokens from prompt, we find that pruning over 40% tokens can destroy both semantics and structure of prompt and the prompt just contains some meaningless and unrelated tokens.
Therefore the the pruning strategy is tested with the set of prune percentages: 10%, 20%, 30%, and 40% which averagely supply 4 code generation examples to the prompt.
For each method we test, we adopt greedy sampling to generate 2 code samples and evaluate the performance of each method by Pass@k with k = {1, 3, 5}.
For the attention-based pruning strategy, we used the CodeBERT model with default parameters to generate specific attention values and set the window length to 500 tokens.
To save on training time and costs, each code generation task requested the GPT model twice.
However, the LLM performs inferior when the pruning percentage of input prompt augments to 40% with the only Pass@k of Class-level and Method-level, 3.4% and 10.4% respectively.

Taking advantage of the context and focusing on the fine-grained token-level adjustment demonstrates that attention-guided pruning is significantly better than random pruning for both class-level and well-studied method-level code.

Os demais mecanismos são herdados do prompt selecionado e variam por configuração.

Seleção da melhor tentativa entre traduções iniciais e iterações de reparo (Best) para evitar a perda causada pelo reparo.

citacoes.trecho: Hence, we conduct an in-depth analysis of code smells and code correctness obtained by LLM-based code translations to fill this gap.
We consider numerous LLMs, datasets, PLs, and prompts, and we reveal that the prompt selection may have a statistically significant impact on an LLM’s performance.

Since prompts are considered to impact a model’s performance substantially and disparately (i.e., each LLM may react differently to the same prompt), we propose a dedicated prompt selection procedure.
The concrete templates and sources are given in Appendix A in Table A1.
Manually crafted by applying principle 2 from [5] in addition to the previous prompt.
citacoes.localizador: Tabela A1, 4ª linha, coluna Source, p. 39

citacoes.trecho: Additionally, although prompts p4 and p6 differ only in the fact that p4 starts with a whitespace, LLMs reacted to a certain extent differently to both prompts.
Since we propose to consistently leverage the non-determinism with k = 3, a mixture of top-p [27] and top-k [17] sampling is used.
This procedure leverages feedback loops and an LLM’s self-repair ability.
Fix the mentioned issue.
Nonetheless, the iterative repair procedure decreases the pass rate for all considered LLMs (Table 8).

In our experiments, the iterative APR technique decreased the pass rate, since we consider two performance dimensions; LLMs appear to alter the functionality and, thus, introduce bugs, when trying to improve the code quality on a previously functionally correct code sample.
We propose a backtranslation, i.e., a cyclic translation (Figure 5) to gain further insights into the evolution of code smells during LLM-based translations.

Surprisingly, we find that a backtranslation approach poses a viable way for mitigating code quality issues in the source, and that LLMs appear to reproduce code smells which were learned during the training process.
We observed, for instance, a variable renaming and the removal of an unused import statement.
Thus, this so-called collaboration setting performs at least as well as the best individual LLM with k translation attempts.
Leveraging the non-determinism of LLMs by sampling multiple times incurs additional computational costs.
Our analysis revealed that all 10 translations failed the provided test suit; furthermore, in all instances, multiple manual alterations were necessary to be able to compile and run the test suit.
Thus, we argue that LLMs resemble those code smells which were learned during training for each specific PL.
Additionally, EvoEval [78] is integrated to account for potential data leakage issues.
Apart from that, potential data leakage may be a source of varying translation effectiveness across datasets.
However, the non-determinism may lead to decreased reproducibility of our work.

The generation of multiple samples (as a means of exploiting the non-determinism) turns out to be an effective measure to improve code quality and code correctness; for selecting the best translation, however, a suitable oracle (e.g., testcases or human judgement) would be necessary.
Thus, the pass rate can be improved by around 10 percent points for many LLMs.

tecnicas.observacao: Pacote completo: fase de avaliação inicial (prompt de geração de código com persona e restrições), geração de testes por LLM (prompt com papel, raciocínio passo a passo, exemplo resolvido e formato $$$$), construção da população inicial por LLM (reescrita com tipos de entrada/saída, elaboração, três casos de teste adicionais e limite de 500 palavras), avaliação por aptidão (taxa de testes gerados aprovados), seleção aleatória ponderada com elitismo e mutação (por sinônimos via embeddings ou por LLM). instrucao: persona e diretrizes; restricoes: limites de palavras, formato e estrutura da função; exemplos: casos de teste acrescentados à descrição e exemplo do prompt de testes; raciocinio: raciocínio passo a passo no prompt de testes; feedback: resultado da execução dos testes guia a seleção dos prompts; amostragem: vários prompts/códigos candidatos com seleção do melhor; otimizacao_prompt: busca evolutiva sobre o próprio prompt. O contrafactual é o pacote contra «Zero-shot» com o mesmo LLM (Tabela 2; também Tabela 4), o que não autoriza atribuir o ganho a um único mecanismo. Pacote híbrido: inclui parâmetros de decodificação (temperatura 0,6 na construção da população e 0,0 na geração), validação sintática de testes por AST e critério de parada, que não são prompting (ver componentes_fora_escopo). Os mecanismos acrescentados são relativos ao Zero-shot, cujo prompt o estudo não descreve (nao_informado); se for o prompt de geração de código da Seção 3.1, restricoes já estaria na base. A assinatura e a docstring da função (enunciado do benchmark) estão em todas as condições e não foram contadas como contexto.

Prompt de reescrita da descrição da função (acrescentar tipos de entrada e saída, elaborar a descrição, manter os testes originais e acrescentar três casos de teste, manter a estrutura da função, no máximo 500 palavras), executado em temperatura 0,6 para gerar vários prompts candidatos. Não há condição de EPiC sem esse componente; a Seção 6 sugere que selecionar o melhor prompt da população inicial pode bastar, mas isso não é avaliado. Os parâmetros (três testes, 500 palavras) foram fixados em experimentos preliminares não relatados numericamente.

citacoes.trecho: To address this issue, we propose an alternative approach named Evolutionary Prompt Engineering for Code (EPiC), which leverages a lightweight evolutionary algorithm to refine the original prompts into improved versions that generate high-quality code, with minimal interactions with the LLM.
Candidate prompts are selected from the population using a weighted random selection approach and then mutated to form the next generation of prompts.

The mutation is carried out using two approaches: one utilizes an LLM guided by a prompt that specifies how to perform the mutation, and the other employs vector embeddings of words to find and replace similar words.
We define a fitness function based on the ratio of test cases passed.
Use step-by-step reasoning to validate each test case separately to ensure that all of them have the correct expected output.
citacoes.localizador: p. 8, Seção 3.1, Test Case Generation Prompt

citacoes.trecho: You are a Python developer who implements the correct code based on the function description provided.
We utilize the LLM to augment multiple prompts based on the initial given prompt.
3- Keep the original test cases and add three test cases to the description to cover the edge cases.
We employ a high-temperature setting (0.6) for the LLM to stimulate creativity in prompt generation.
For the baseline, we use a zero-shot prompting approach.
Unlike EPiC and other baselines, which generate tests for internal evaluation and feedback, LDB relies on ground-truth tests rather than generating new ones.
To mitigate the variability from the LLM’s non-deterministic outputs and to conduct a more rigorous evaluation, every experiment was repeated three times.
While EA is effective in navigating complex search spaces, it also has drawbacks, such as potential inefficiency when fitness evaluations are expensive and the risk of premature convergence.
While effective, these methods can be costly due to numerous interactions with LLMs, which result in extensive token usage, making them less attractive in practical settings.
The results highlight a clear trade-off: EPiC achieves higher functional correctness at the cost of increased token usage.

One construct threat we face is that our evaluation metrics rely on LLM-generated test cases for intermediate evaluations which could lead to misleading results if these test cases are not representative of the intended tasks.

One external limitation of this research is that the datasets used (HumanEval+, MBPP+, and BigCodeBench) may not fully represent the diversity of real-world coding tasks, which may limit the generalizability of our findings.
However, we chose LLMs from three different vendors to mitigate this threat.
We executed the generated tests against the ground truth implementations in the dataset to verify their correctness.
Our results demonstrate that sim_words_as_mutator consistently outperforms LLM_as_mutator in terms of cost-effectiveness across all evaluated configurations.

While individual synonym-based mutations may introduce noise, the fitness function (Section 4.4) evaluates each mutated prompt by executing generated code against test cases, which ensures that only mutations maintaining or improving the passing rate are selected for subsequent generations.
On BigCodeBenchHard, EPiC attains the lowest ACSP (0.53), while baselines range from 0.88–3.64 (Reflexion/LDB/LATS) with Self-Consistency at 1.54.

Our evaluation against state-of-the-art (SOTA) LLM-based code generation agents shows that EPiC not only achieves up to 5% improvement in pass@k but is also 1.2–10 times more cost-effective than the baselines.
After the initial evaluation, AgentCoder [17] and MPSC were excluded from further analysis as we found that they are much more expensive than the next most expensive alternative.

citacoes.trecho: To fill this gap, we conducted an empirical study to evaluate the performance of eight LLMs under four prompting methods.
To systematically evaluate the LLMs’ capabilities under various levels of task guidance, we employed four widely used prompting methods as baselines, while keeping the other components consistent.
Zero-shot prompting [29] provides LLMs with only the task requirement, without any examples.
One-shot prompting [29] provides a single example in the form of <example task, example code> pair.

One-shot Chain-of-Thought prompting (abbreviated as oneshot-cot prompting) [83] extends one-shot prompting by incorporating a Chain-of-Thought [83] (CoT) explanation, forming an <example task, CoT, example code> triple.
Few-shot prompting [23] provides multiple examples in the form of <example task, example code> pairs.
As a developer specializing in deep learning, you are expected to complete the code using Functional APIs of Keras, ensuring it meets the requirement of a task.
Please import Keras and all necessary packages, then complete python code in the dl_model() function and return the constructed model.
Notably, the prompt contains no example-related instruction when using zero-shot prompting.
To examine the practical utility of the taxonomy, we conducted a follow-up repair experiment on Tensor Shape Mismatch errors.
We compared a taxonomy-guided prompt with a compile-log-based baseline prompt, while keeping the components identical.
Beyond the buggy code and compilation log, the taxonomy-guided prompt incorporates a repair strategy derived from the recurring failure patterns captured by our taxonomy.
This strategy maps tensor-shape-mismatch errors to a constrained set of corrective actions, guiding the model to localize the root cause and apply specific parameter adjustments.
Second, we adopted nucleus sampling [42] to decode outputs from the LLMs, setting the temperature to 0.8 and the top-p to 0.95 to maintain controlled randomness across all LLMs.
To minimize the effects of LLM non-determinism and ensure result reliability, each task in DeepEval is performed three times, and the average performance for each task is reported.
Meanwhile, to mitigate the risk of data leakage from existing data sources, our benchmark is constructed entirely from scratch.
First, to prevent data leakage, all task descriptions in DeepEval were created from scratch, avoiding widely known terms (e.g., residual connection) that could trigger memorization in the LLMs.
LLMs face challenges in managing import statements and variables due to their limited awareness of global context and a tendency to hallucinate DL API elements.

O novo prompt traz papel e instrução (instrucao), o código gerado com a função vulnerável substituída pelo token <mask> (contexto: código fornecido como insumo), passos para eliminar a vulnerabilidade, como o padrão checks-effects-interactions (restricoes de segurança e diretrizes), e é reaplicado com base no relatório do Slither até não haver vulnerabilidade (feedback). citacoes.trecho: In consideration of these two viewpoints, this paper examines the utilization of large language models (LLMs) for the automatic generation of Solidity smart contracts based on specified criteria, while simultaneously ensuring the elimination of vulnerabilities through a novel masking strategy.
To achieve this, we propose SolGen, a framework for generating secure Solidity smart contract code using LLMs.
SolGen uses closed-source LLMs (e.g. ChatGPT and Meta AI) and static analysis to generate secure Solidity smart contracts through multi-round and masked prompting.
RQ2: How multi-round prompting technique effectively resolve the compilation issues of Solidity smart contracts generated by closed-source LLMs (such as Meta AI and ChatGPT)?
RQ4: How masked prompting technique assists in addressing vulnerabilities within Solidity smart contracts code generated by closed-source LLMs (such as Meta AI and ChatGPT)?

This work includes the use of instruction-tuning [30], iterative prompt refinement through feedback [18], and masked prompting [29] techniques for the generation of secure Solidity smart contract code with the absence of vulnerabilities.
Role: You are an excellent Solidity smart contract developer.

This iterative process continues until the LLM under consideration generates a new version of the code snippet when compared to the previous round and all errors in the generated smart contract code are resolved and fixed.
A new prompt is constructed by masking the identified vulnerable functions or methods in the smart contract.
This new prompt includes the vulnerable source code snippet that was generated by the LLM, which is masked with a special token called <mask>.
Additionally, it includes the steps and useful information that are necessary to eliminate the identified vulnerability.
The ‘-’ and ‘*’ symbol in Tables 2 through 8 indicates that the LLM failed to generate valid Solidity code and produced either gibberish or irrelevant output.
However, it is observed that LLMs do not consistently generate compilable code on the first attempt.
Thus, to avoid information loss due to generated large smart contract code in combination with error details during re-prompting is very crucial.
Thus, our methodology takes utmost care that there is no information loss during complete cycle of generating compilable, non-vulnerable and secure Solidity smart contract code.
Our analysis reveals that all compilable code generated from both Meta AI and ChatGPT exhibits vulnerabilities.
However, we focus on significant vulnerabilities, such as reentrancy, and disregard those with very low severity.
Table 4 shows that 10 out of 17 compilable Solidity codes have reentrancy vulnerabilities, generated by Meta AI.
Similarly, Table 5 shows that 9 out of 19 compilable codes generated by ChatGPT contain the same vulnerability.
In total, 83 vulnerable functions are identified in Meta AI’s generated code, compared to 54 vulnerable functions in the code generated by ChatGPT.
This approach involves iteratively masking a vulnerable function in the code until a new and unique version of code is generated when compared to the previous iteration.
As shown in Table 4, the Meta AI model does not perform well with the masking technique.
In most cases, ChatGPT is able to resolve reentrancy vulnerabilities after no more than four iterations.
The only exception is compilable code C5, which fails to produce a secure, compilable code even after multiple rounds of masked re-prompting.
At a temperature of 0.1, there are 12 vulnerable functions, which increases to 25 at 0.7, and then decreases to 16 at 1.2.

Along with this, our findings reveals the importance of adjusting temperature for improving security of generated contracts and thus contributing to the best practices for Ethereum smart contract development.
Therefore, for generating secure smart contract code the human intervention is necessary and important.

Moreover, the datasets used for training these LLMs are not disclosed publicly which makes it difficult to determine the fact that whether the problems we tested were part of the training data used in the model.

As a result, in this work the responses generated by LLMs are indicative of the models’ performance (i.e., GPT-4o for ChatGPT and Llama 3.1 for Meta AI) during specific time when our experiments were conducted, and hence it may not accurately represent their future behavior or capabilities.

citacoes.trecho: Finally planning-oriented prompting, code verification and retrieval augmented editing are used to promote the actual performance of the LLM generated code.
The evaluation results confirm that a rough speedup of 6.06X and 5.13X are achieved using Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-Coder-14B-Instruct LLM models.
Positive improvement is confirmed in our experiment with three LLM models (GPT-4o-mini, Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-Coder-14B-Instruct).
Planning is pivotal to the prompting workflow, including both single-stage prompts for direct parallelization and decomposed workflows for multi-stage code transformation.
The four prompt types represent different planning granularities:
serial: Do not explicitly specify a parallelization method; instead, instruct the model to rewrite and optimize the serial source code.
any: Suggest OpenMP parallel optimization as an available option, requiring the model to rewrite the serial source code into faster code without restrictions on serial or parallel execution.
multi-stage: Decompose the optimization process into two stages: first, perform serial optimization, and then apply parallel to convert the code optimized in the first stage into parallel code.
For LLMs with larger parameter sizes or broader context windows, the error information is explicitly fed back to the model, prompting it to regenerate the code.

As the code generated by LLMs may potentially yield incorrect results, we implement a self-correction mechanism that enables the LLM to predict, verify, and rectify the functionality of the generated code.
Based on this analysis, the LLM then regenerates the code to ensure functional correctness and the correctness rate is further improved with this technique.

To address potential inconsistencies in function interfaces that may arise from large language models (LLMs), we employ the nm tool to analyze the abstract syntax tree (AST) of the compiled object files.

Initially, We discovered some outliers in the speedup records of the synthesized data and identified two reasons for this: (1) erroneous code that occasionally passed all the program-generated test cases; (2) the speedup of some code is highly dependent on the test data.
If all tests pass, we calculate the average speedup after removing extremums to mitigate noisy speedup signals.
All long entries with token counts exceeding 1,000 will be eliminated, and finally 5,841 of these long entries were removed from the PIE dataset.
We perform multiple inferences on 60 questions from the ParEval dataset [17], collecting 500 effective samples for each question, and in total 30,000 distinct target code examples are gathered.

When a new program is received for optimization, the system retrieves the L most similar programs from this knowledge base based on their embeddings, and for practical cases, L can be set to be 1,2,3.
With the introduction of retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), the prompt includes the two most similar {source code: target code} pairs to guide the model.
The default version of RAG can retrieve two samples with identical source code, which, as observed from the experimental results, can negatively impact the quality of the generated code.
Therefore, we incorporated self-match verification to ensure that the two retrieved samples have different source codes, significantly enhancing the code quality.

riscos.descricao: Patches que passam na suíte de testes podem ser sobreajustados e incorretos (plausível não é correto).

Few-shot pode gerar mais patches não compiláveis do que zero-shot (Finding 3) e, por efeito de ancoragem, restringir o espaço de busca e desorientar o modelo quando o exemplo não corresponde ao padrão de reparo do bug.
riscos.localizador: PDF p. 13 e 27 (impressas 13 e 27), Finding 3 e seção 5

riscos.descricao: Os LLMs poderiam reconhecer e manipular os testes disparadores para passar nos testes, produzindo patches aparentemente plausíveis.
Possível vazamento de dados se os patches dos desenvolvedores estiverem nos dados de treino; para o StarCoder2, 122 dos 522 bugs foram identificados nos dados de treino.
A qualidade dos relatos de defeito pode variar em cenários reais, com conteúdo inválido, irreproduzível, incompleto ou enganoso; 38 relatos do Defects4J contêm instruções explícitas de correção.
Nem todos os tipos de informação específica do projeto estão garantidos para todo bug em cenários reais (validade externa).
Subjetividade da validação manual que distingue patches plausíveis de corretos (validade interna).
Disparidade de backbones e de seleção dos sistemas comparados ameaça a justiça da comparação (validade interna).
Os conjuntos de avaliação podem não generalizar os resultados (validade externa).

Usar GPT-4 nas duas etapas do SRepair consome em média 4,3× o custo de API da configuração padrão ($0.4128 vs. $0.0966 por bug); replicar o ChatRepair com GPT-4 foi estimado em mais de $6,000 pelo mecanismo de amostragem iterativa.

citacoes.trecho: In this paper, we conduct a comprehensive study of LLM-based function-level APR including investigating the effect of the few-shot learning mechanism and the auxiliary repair-relevant information.
Specifically, we begin with a description of the APR task as ‘Provide a fix for the buggy function’.
Notably, we employ the zero-shot learning approach as the default baseline in our study, i.e., adopting no auxiliary repair-relevant information or buggy-fixed code pair examples for prompting.
Table 2 presents our k-shot learning setups.
For evaluating the impact from the auxiliary repair-relevant information, we form seven different setups.

Specifically, for the project-specific information, we form four setups: PI(TT) with the trigger test only, PI(EM) with the error message only, PI(BC) with the buggy function comment only, and PI(ALL) with all such information.
In particular, SRepair first adopts a repair suggestion model which employs the Chain of Thought (CoT) technique [114] to generate natural-language repair suggestions.
SRepair then adopts a patch generation model to auto-generate a patched function with the assistance of the repair suggestions.
Your output format should be ”Root Cause: {content}” and ”Suggestion {id}: {title}\n{description}”

Table 12 shows that the CoT technique and the Dual-LLM framework lead to at least 7.9% (272 vs. 252) and 6.3% (252 vs. 237) gains in repair performance, respectively, with both p-values < 0.001 under McNemar’s test [84] on paired bug-level outcomes, indicating that the improvements are statistically significant.

Furthermore, to rigorously distinguish correct fixes from overfitting patches that merely pass the test suite [79, 93], we employ a manual validation process based on semantic equivalence to the developer’s ground truth, following prior works [53, 77, 79, 82, 85, 119, 120].
Finding 3: Applying the few-shot learning mechanism may generate more uncompilable patches than the zero-shot learning mechanism.

While this anchoring could be beneficial when the provided example closely aligns with the target bug’s repair pattern, it risks narrowing the search space and potentially misguiding the model when there is a mismatch.
Another threat is the risk of data leakage if the developer patches were included in the original training data.
An additional threat lies in the trigger tests adopted in SRepair where the LLMs might have recognized the trigger tests and manipulated them to pass all tests, creating seemingly plausible patches.

While the bug reports associated with dedicated projects like Defects4J are generally of high quality, as reflected by their effectiveness in our evaluation results, their quality may vary substantially in real-world settings [32, 66, 74], and they may contain invalid, irreproducible, incomplete, or even misleading contents.
An additional threat to external validity is that not all types of project-specific information are guaranteed to be available for every bug in real-world settings.
One potential threat arises from our manual validation process, which differentiates between plausible patches and those that are semantically correct.
Furthermore, the disparity in the backbone models used by different techniques poses a threat to the fairness of our comparison.
The main threat to external validity lies in our evaluation datasets used which may not well generalize our experimental results.

Moreover, while fully adopting GPT-4 as both the repair suggestion model and the patch generation model can produce 8% (294 vs. 272) more plausible fixes, it consumes an average of 4.3× ($0.4128 vs. $0.0966) API cost compared with the default SRepair setup.

Specifically, three authors independently cross-validate each plausible patch guided by a set of established equivalence rules (e.g., regarding control flow refactoring or variable aliasing) [128, 130], ensuring the patch truly resolves the bug.
Eventually, we rule out the 122 bugs present in StarCoder2’s training dataset and form Defects4J-clean dataset with the rest 400 bugs, creating a clean, uncontaminated dataset.

We also perform an evaluation on the newly released dataset ConDefects, a collection of programming contest bugs obtained after the knowledge cut-off date of gpt-4-0613 [25] to alleviate the data leakage concern.

Our SRepair’s Dual-LLM mechanism effectively mitigates this threat, as the repair suggestion model only suggests bug fixes without trigger test information, keeping the patch generation model isolated from such data.
To mitigate this threat, we instead evaluated SRepair using the same GPT-3.5-Turbo model under a comparable sampling budget.
To mitigate this, we carefully selected four recent, well-designed LLM-based APR techniques with sample sizes equal to or larger than those used in our study settings.
This threat can be partially mitigated in bug-report-driven scenarios by reproducing trigger tests from bug reports and executing them to obtain the corresponding error messages.
Our default setting for patch generation uses the nucleus sampling with top p = 0.9, temperature = 0.8 and 200 samples per bug following prior works [38, 92, 119].
Following the recent SOTA APR technique D4C [125], which enables an efficient patch sampling process for practice, we set the number of patches sampled by SRepair per bug to 10.

riscos.descricao: Semgrep detecta potenciais problemas de segurança no código gerado (zero em GPT-Neo, 13 em GPT-3.5, quatro em GPT-4, nove em Qwen-2.5); a métrica é omitida por baixa variância. A introdução também cita relato de código vulnerável gerado pelo Copilot.

O estudo presume sobreajuste do GPT-Neo ao APPS e memorização de trechos de código de treino, e fala em reações dos LLMs que revelam sobreajuste aos dados de treino; não há controle nem verificação de contaminação.

Custo do uso de LLMs motiva a amostragem de 6K data points do APPS e a escolha do GPT-3.5 como reformulador; gerar código para avaliar a métrica objetivo é descrito como custoso e demorado. Não quantificado.

Generalização limitada: poucos LLMs (família GPT e Qwen), dois conjuntos (APPS, BigCodeBench) e número limitado de instruções de reformulação; a aplicação da Seção 8 é prova de conceito em cenário idealizado; ausência de grafo de referência limita a validação da descoberta causal.

citacoes.trecho: This paper focuses on one of the most popular programming languages, Python3.
We illustrate the insights that our framework can provide by studying over four popular LLMs with over 12 prompt adjustment strategies.
In this paper, we focus on the 12 rephrasing intentions listed in Fig. 4(b), considering both expert experience and computational cost.
All synthesized meta-prompts are refined and optimized using the state-of-the-art LLM, GPT-4o, to enhance the quality of the rephrased prompts, thereby improving the quality of the generated code.
Please rephrase the programming problem in XML tags while keeping its original meaning and structure, to help enhance the understanding of the problem's intent and facilitate better code generation.
You should keep all mathematical symbols in latex format.
Furthermore, pre-defined intentions from various categories can be combined to form a more complex rephrasing intention.
In this pilot study, we ask ChatGPT [5] to rephrase the given programming problem by following three simple instructions: make the prompt shorter, longer, or more formal.
As a baseline, we also set up a control group that receives no instructions.
We use a genetic algorithm to find the rephrasing instructions that can maximize a given objective metric.
In contrast, our causality analysis-based approach can estimate the expected value of the objective metric without involving the actual code generation and subsequent evaluation process.
A slightly ambiguous prompt in Fig. 1(a) misleads the LLM into generating a program that capitalizes the initial letter of each word.
Specifically, the generation for a given prompt is stochastic rather than deterministic.
To avoid the randomness of LLMs, for each data point, we collect three solutions from each model.
Specifically, zero security issues are detected for code generated by GPT-Neo, while 13 security issues are detected on GPT-3.5, four on GPT-4, and nine on Qwen-2.5.
We presume that GPT-Neo has been fine-tuned to the point of relative overfitting on APPS, a clean dataset, resulting in no detected security flaws.
To learn causal graphs, we use all data from BigCodeBench and sample 6K data points from APPS considering the high cost of using LLMs.
The reason is that the objective metric requires instructing the LLM to generate code, which is costly and time-consuming.
First, our study primarily focuses limited LLMs (GPT-family and Qwen) and datasets (APPS, BigCodeBench).
We use the aggregated results to mitigate the impact of these factors.
We clarify, however, that the application is a proof-of-concept study in an idealized setting.

tecnicas.nome_original: ChatDBG (configuração +Dialog, com todos os recursos habilitados)
tecnicas.observacao: Pacote completo comparado com a configuração Default Stack, que o estudo usa como linha de base (p. 15-16). É pacote híbrido: além do prompt (instruções com papel de assistente de depuração, explicação até a causa-raiz, seção final «Recommendation», restrição de não alterar a asserção, rastreamento de pilha enriquecido, entradas, histórico, pergunta direcionada e pergunta de continuação), inclui a execução de comandos do depurador por function calling, o sanitizador de comandos, o fatiamento com ipyflow (notebooks) e o servidor clangd (código nativo), listados em componentes_fora_escopo. O ganho do pacote não se atribui a um mecanismo isolado. Mecanismos: instrucao (papel, objetivos e diretrizes, Fig. 5), raciocinio («Explain why each variable ... Continue with your explanations until you reach the root cause», Fig. 5), restricoes (formato «Recommendation»; lista de comandos permitidos ao depurador; asserção que não deve ser alterada; especificação do comportamento esperado na pergunta direcionada), contexto (rastreamento de pilha, erro, entradas, histórico; recuperação de estado e código por info/slice), exemplos (exemplos ilustrativos do formato das referências aceitas por info: «n, e.n ... t.n»), outro (segunda pergunta fixa de continuação sem feedback sobre a primeira resposta). A presença das instruções gerais da Fig. 5 também na Default Stack é inferida da Tabela 4 e da descrição da ablação como habilitação progressiva de recursos; o artigo não reproduz o prompt da Default Stack.

tecnicas.observacao: Linha de base: rastreamento de pilha padrão (ipdb) com 5 linhas de código por quadro e pergunta inicial «why?», sem take the wheel. O estudo a descreve como aproximadamente equivalente a copiar o rastreamento e a informação de erro numa janela de chat e pedir uma correção. As instruções gerais da Fig. 5 (sem os parágrafos 2-4 de take the wheel) são atribuídas por inferência da Tabela 4, que só varia as colunas listadas; o prompt desta configuração não é reproduzido.
